summary: Phase 1 of rebuild playbook: reverse-engineer SwartzNet behavior into SPEC.md source material
logs: Critic found 4 gaps; spawning gap readers

readers.purpose: cmd/swartznet is the single CLI binary that both runs the SwartzNet node (the `add` subcommand IS the daemon: engine + indexer + companion pub/sub + HTTP API via daemon.New) and provides thin client subcommands that drive a running daemon over its localhost HTTP API or operate offline on local files (search, trust, aggregate, create). cmd/dht-smoke is a standalone, network-touching ops probe that validates the BEP-44 put/get publisher path against the real mainline DHT, deliberately excluded from `go test`.

capabilities.behavior: Top-level dispatch: `swartznet <cmd>` with commands add, search, status, flag, confirm, create, index, files, trust, aggregate, crawl-probe, version (-v/--version), help (-h/--help); unknown command prints usage to stderr and exits 2; zero args prints usage to stderr and exits 2
Documented exit-code contract for shell scripts: 0 OK, 2 usage error, 1 runtime error, 130 interrupt (SIGINT/SIGTERM clean shutdown maps context.Canceled to 130)

`add <magnet-uri|path.torrent>` starts the full daemon (companion publisher/subscriber, HTTP API on localhost:7654 by default), adds the torrent (magnet: prefix -> AddMagnet, anything else treated as .torrent path), waits up to 5 min for metadata, prints name/hash/size/pieces/first-20 files, calls DownloadAll, then loops printing a one-line progress status every 3s plus a line per completed file, until Ctrl-C (exit 130)

`add` flags: --data-dir, --index-dir, --port (-1 sentinel = keep config default 42069; 0 = OS-assigned), --api-addr (default localhost:7654, empty disables API), --no-dht, --no-dht-publish (privacy: stay on DHT but publish no BEP-44 items), --leech-only, --no-index, --dht-bootstrap (repeatable host:port), --regtest, --dht-insecure
`add` refuses --regtest and --dht-insecure unless env SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1, exiting 2 with an explanatory message, so copy-pasted testbed commands cannot weaken a mainnet node

`search <query...>` (words joined with spaces) in local mode opens the Bleve index in-process (no daemon needed) and prints text or --json results; distinguishes [content] hits (path, mime, extractor, parent infohash) from [torrent] hits (name, infohash, file count, size, first tracker + count)

`search --swarm` / `--dht` / `--signed-by <64-hex-pubkey>` switches to POST /search on the running daemon, combining local + sn_search peer fan-out + BEP-44 DHT lookup in one call; text output renders separate LOCAL / SWARM / DHT sections with per-layer ask/respond/reject/hit counts and per-layer error strings; flags --limit (20), --swarm-timeout-ms (2000), --dht-timeout-ms (5000), --api-addr

`status` GETs /status from the daemon and prints Layer L doc count, Layer S known/capable peers, DHT routing-table nodes (block omitted when daemon runs with DHT disabled), and Layer D publisher pubkey + per-keyword hits/publish-count/last-published/error state; also best-effort GETs /aggregate and appends an Aggregate (PPMI/B-tree/RIBLT) block; --json merges both into one document {status, aggregate}

`flag <infohash>` POSTs /flag to demote reputation of indexers attributed to that infohash; `confirm <infohash>` POSTs /confirm to add it to the known-good Bloom filter (manual counterpart to the engine's auto-confirm-on-completion); both lowercase/trim and validate 40-hex infohash locally, print past tense 'flagged:'/'confirmed:' on success

`create <root> -o out.torrent` hashes a file/directory in-process (spins a minimal engine, deliberately not daemon.New), writes the .torrent, prints the infohash; flags --name, --piece-kib (0=auto), --tracker/--webseed (repeatable), --comment, --private (BEP-27), --sign, --identity, --seed, --data-dir; CreatedBy is embedded as 'swartznet <Version>'

`create --sign` signs the .torrent with the ed25519 identity (prints 'Signing with identity <pubkey>'); default identity path auto-creates via LoadOrCreate, but an explicit --identity path is load-only and errors if missing; --identity without --sign is a usage error (fail closed)

`create --seed` then seeds the just-created content in place from <root> (path-aware AddTorrentMetaInfoSeedFrom keyed on root's real basename), blocking until Ctrl-C (exit 130); seed-start failure prints a warning and exits 1 even though the .torrent was already written
`index <infohash> on|off` (also accepts true/1/yes and false/0/no) POSTs /torrents/{ih}/indexing to flip per-torrent indexing on a running daemon

`files <infohash>` GETs /torrents/{ih}/files and prints an IDX/PRIORITY/SIZE/PROG%/PATH table (or --json); `files <infohash> <idx> <priority>` POSTs /torrents/{ih}/files/{idx}/priority with priority restricted to none|normal|high and idx validated + canonicalized as a non-negative integer before URL interpolation

`trust list|ls / add <pubkey> [label...] / remove|rm <pubkey>` manages a local offline JSON trust list (default ~/.local/share/swartznet/trust.json, --file to override, --json for list); works with no daemon running; add lowercases/trims the pubkey and joins remaining args into the label

`aggregate build --out FILE [--in JSONL|-] [--key path] [--seq N] [--piece-size N] [--pow-bits N]` reads JSONL {kw,ih,t} records, signs each with the publisher ed25519 key, optionally mines hashcash PoW per record, packs them into a signed B-tree index file (mode 0644) and prints records/pages/bytes/fingerprint; fully offline, never touches DHT or daemon

`aggregate inspect <index-file> [--piece-size]` opens the B-tree (fails on bad magic/version/trailer signature) and prints trailer metadata: pages, records, publisher pubkey, seq, created timestamp, min PoW bits, tree fingerprint

`aggregate find <index-file> <prefix> [--piece-size] [--verify]` runs a keyword prefix query and prints matching (infohash, keyword, timestamp) records; --verify additionally runs VerifyFingerprint scanning every leaf

`crawl-probe --addr host:port [--target 40hex] [--timeout-ms 5000] [--json]` issues a single BEP-51 sample_infohashes query from a throwaway loopback DHT server (NoSecurity, Passive) and prints interval, num-tracked, sampled infohashes, and closest nodes; target defaults to a fresh random 20-byte ID per run
Logging level of the daemon-ish commands is controlled by env SWARTZNET_LOG (debug|info|warn|error, default info); structured slog text output goes to stderr

dht-smoke (`go run ./cmd/dht-smoke`): bootstraps a real mainline DHT server (waits up to 30s for >=8 good nodes, fails if <1), generates an ephemeral ed25519 key, Puts a synthetic KeywordValue under a timestamped salt, Gets it back and verifies hits==1 and name=='smoke test'; prints PASS/exit 0 or FAIL/exit 1

dht-smoke -stress N [-stress-timeout 60s] [-stress-concurrent 8] runs N concurrent BEP-44 puts after the smoke, reporting success rate, min/p50/p95/max latency, error buckets, post-load routing stats, and one sample get-back round trip (addresses v1.0.0 open question #2 on concurrent publish limits)

inputs_outputs: In: argv subcommand + flags; magnet URIs or .torrent file paths (add); local files/directories to hash (create); JSONL records on stdin or file (aggregate build); Aggregate B-tree index files (aggregate inspect/find); 40-hex infohashes and 64-hex pubkeys as positional args
In: env vars SWARTZNET_LOG (log level), SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 (unlock --regtest/--dht-insecure); signals SIGINT/SIGTERM (cancel context, exit 130)

In/Out: localhost HTTP JSON to the running daemon at --api-addr (default localhost:7654): POST /search, GET /status, GET /aggregate, POST /flag, POST /confirm, POST /torrents/{ih}/indexing, GET /torrents/{ih}/files, POST /torrents/{ih}/files/{idx}/priority; every unreachable-daemon error prints the hint 'start it with: swartznet add <magnet>'

In/Out: BitTorrent + DHT traffic via the embedded engine (add, create --seed); one-shot BEP-51 UDP query from an ephemeral loopback socket (crawl-probe); live mainline BEP-44 put/get traffic (dht-smoke)

Out: .torrent files (create), signed Aggregate B-tree payload files mode 0644 (aggregate build), trust.json mutations (trust add/remove), auto-created identity.key at the default XDG path (create --sign / aggregate build without explicit key)
Out: human text on stdout / errors on stderr; --json variants on search, status, files, trust list, crawl-probe; process exit codes 0/1/2/130
data_models: JSONL record for `aggregate build`: {"kw": string non-empty, "ih": 40-char hex SHA-1, "t": int64 optional (default 0)} — cmd/swartznet/cmd_aggregate_build.go:22-27; validation: length-40 check at read time (line 180-185), hex-decode to 20 bytes at sign time (lines 199-207)

Aggregate B-tree index file (single-file companion-torrent payload): paged structure read via companion.BytesPageSource{Data,PieceSize} + companion.OpenBTree; trailer carries NumPages, NumRecords, PubKey[32], Seq, CreatedTs (unix), MinPoWBits, TreeFingerprint[32]; per-record: Pk[32], Kw, Ih[20], T, Sig (ed25519 over companion.RecordSigMessage), optional hashcash PoW — consumed at cmd_aggregate.go:86-105, produced at cmd_aggregate_build.go:196-236; format itself defined in internal/companion (MinPieceSize=16384, internal/companion/build_btree.go:44)
trust.json: array of {PubKeyHex (64-hex, lowercased), Label} via trust.Store LoadOrCreate/Add/Remove/List, default path config.Default().TrustPath — cmd/swartznet/cmd_trust.go:84-88,149-157

identity.key: ed25519 keypair file, default config.Default().IdentityPath (~/.local/share/swartznet/identity.key); LoadOrCreate auto-generates only at the default path — cmd_aggregate_build.go:115-146, cmd_create.go:92-98

HTTP API JSON shapes the CLI depends on (defined in internal/httpapi, consumed here): SearchRequest{Q,Limit,Swarm,DHT,SwarmTimeoutMs,DHTTimeoutMs,SignedBy}; SearchResponse{Local{Total,Hits[LocalHit{DocType,Name,FilePath,InfoHash,SizeBytes,Score,Extractor}]}, Swarm{Asked,Responded,Rejected,Hits[SwarmHit{Name,InfoHash,Size,Seeders,Score,Sources}],Error}, DHT{IndexersAsked,IndexersResponded,Hits[DHTHit{Name,InfoHash,Size,Seeders,Files,Sources}],Error}}; StatusResponse{Local{Indexed,DocCount},Swarm{KnownPeers,CapablePeers},DHT*{GoodNodes,Nodes},Publisher{PubKey,TotalKeywords,TotalHits,Keywords[{Keyword,HitsCount,PublishCount,LastPublished,LastError}]}}; AggregateStatusResponse{PPMIEnabled,KnownIndexers,RecordSourceKind,RecordCacheSize/Max,ServicesAdvertised,Bootstrap{Anchors,Admitted,Pending}}; FlagRequest/FlagResponse{OK,InfoHash}; FilesListResponse{Files[{Index,Priority,Length,Progress,DisplayPath}]} — cmd_search.go:96-104,150-224; cmd_status.go:54-105; cmd_flag.go:55-91; cmd_files.go:74-97
dhtindex wire values used by dht-smoke: KeywordValue{Hits:[]KeywordHit{IH [20]byte, N string, S int}} published as a BEP-44 mutable item under SaltForKeyword(keyword) — cmd/dht-smoke/main.go:120-134
crawl-probe --json output: {addr, target(40hex), samples[]40hex, interval int64, num int64, nodes[]"<40hex-id>@<addr>"} — cmd/swartznet/cmd_crawl_probe.go:98-125
external_deps: github.com/anacrolix/dht/v2 (+krpc): crawl-probe's throwaway server and dht-smoke's live server; dht-smoke uses NewDefaultServerConfig with public bootstrap routers
github.com/anacrolix/torrent indirectly via internal/engine (add, create): BEP-3/5/9/10 mainline behavior

internal packages wired by the CLI: daemon (full node construction), engine (torrent ops, CreateTorrentFile, AddTorrentMetaInfoSeedFrom), indexer (direct Bleve open for local search), httpapi (request/response types + endpoints), companion (B-tree build/open, record signing/PoW), identity (ed25519 keys), trust (trust.json store), config (XDG defaults), dhtindex (BEP-44 putter/getter, SaltForKeyword, SampleInfohashes)

Protocols: BEP-3/5/9/10 (via engine), BEP-27 private flag (create --private), BEP-42 node-ID security (disabled by --dht-insecure), BEP-44 mutable items (search --dht, status publisher block, dht-smoke), BEP-46 companion pointers (daemon side of add), BEP-51 sample_infohashes (crawl-probe)
Bleve full-text index (opened in-process by local `search`)
ed25519 (crypto/ed25519) for torrent/record signing and the dht-smoke ephemeral identity

nonobvious_rules.rule: There is no `daemon`/`serve` subcommand: `swartznet add` IS the daemon. It starts the HTTP API, companion publisher/subscriber, and indexer, and every daemon-dependent command (search --swarm/--dht, status, flag, confirm, index, files) assumes an `add` process is alive at --api-addr
nonobvious_rules.evidence: cmd/swartznet/cmd_add.go:96-117; error hints at cmd_search.go:121, cmd_status.go:43, cmd_flag.go:69

nonobvious_rules.rule: Clean Ctrl-C shutdown of `add` and `create --seed` exits 130 (context.Canceled -> exitInterrupt), never 0 — scripts must treat 130 as the normal end of a foreground session
--regtest and --dht-insecure are hard-refused (exit 2) unless SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 is set in the environment; they are also omitted from the printed usage text

Identity fail-closed asymmetry: the DEFAULT identity path auto-creates a key (LoadOrCreate), but any EXPLICIT --identity/--key path is load-only and errors on a missing file — auto-minting there would silently orphan the signed torrent/records under an unknown pubkey and sever publisher reputation. Likewise --identity without --sign is a usage error rather than silently ignored

`create` deliberately bypasses daemon.New and spins a bare engine; engine config shape depends on --seed: without it DisableDHT=true/NoUpload=true (pure hashing run), with it DHT and upload stay ON (trackerless seeds must be DHT-discoverable); ListenPort is 0 (ephemeral) in BOTH modes because the DHT announce carries the actual bound port and this avoids clashing with a daemon on 42069
`add --port` uses -1 as the 'unset' sentinel so that --port 0 (OS-assigned) is distinguishable from 'keep config default 42069'; override only applies when port >= 0

`search` routes through the daemon API whenever ANY of --swarm, --dht, or --signed-by is set (signed-by alone forces the API path 'so the filter rides the same JSON shape'); in API mode --index-dir is silently ignored. The API request deadline is swarmTimeoutMs + dhtTimeoutMs + 2000 ms

`status` merges two endpoints: GET /status (fatal on failure) plus best-effort GET /aggregate where any error/404/decode failure silently omits the Aggregate block, keeping the command compatible with older daemons; the DHT routing-table block is omitted-when-nil meaning 'DHT disabled', distinct from zero nodes

Infohash arguments are lowercased+trimmed then validated locally as exactly 40 hex chars before any HTTP round trip, specifically to give a clearer error than the daemon's API-status message; the file index in `files` is Atoi-canonicalized ('+07' -> '7') and rejected if negative before being interpolated into the URL path
`flag`/`confirm` success output uses hand-built past tense: 'flag' -> 'flagged' (special case), otherwise name+'ed' ('confirmed'); a rewrite using '%sed' would print 'flaged'
`index` mode parsing accepts on/true/1/yes and off/false/0/no, not just the documented on|off

`aggregate build` refuses --pow-bits > 40 as cost-prohibitive (exit 2); default 0 = no mining; help text names 20 as 'production default'; default --seq is 1 and default --in is '-' (stdin); JSONL reader skips empty lines, errors carry 1-based line numbers, scanner buffer is raised to 1 MiB for long records
`aggregate inspect|find --piece-size` defaults to companion.MinPieceSize (16384) and MUST match the wrapping torrent's metainfo piece length or the B-tree paging is misread

crawl-probe's throwaway DHT server binds 127.0.0.1:0 with NoSecurity (arbitrary node ID allowed) and Passive (never answers incoming queries); the sample target is fresh random per invocation so repeated runs sample different slices of the keyspace

dht-smoke never touches the user's real publisher identity — it generates an ephemeral ed25519 key and a timestamped salt (swartznet_smoke_<unix>) so runs never collide with prior runs or real publishes; it is intentionally NOT part of `go test ./...` because it exposes the machine's IP to the public DHT

`add` progress loop keeps running (rather than exiting) when the file-events channel closes, so the UI only stops on ctx cancel; SubscribeFileEvents is an independent fan-out so the display loop cannot steal events from the indexer ingest pipeline

Version defaults to 'v0.8.0' and is overridden via -ldflags -X main.Version in release builds; it is surfaced in `version`, in daemon.Options, and baked into created torrents as CreatedBy='swartznet <Version>'
`create` prints '✓ Created ...' and the infohash BEFORE attempting to seed; a seed-start failure exits 1 but leaves the valid .torrent on disk

broken_or_unfinished.issue: dht-smoke code contradicts its own docs on stress-phase exit status: doc says 'does not fail the exit status unless ALL puts fail', but run() swallows runStress's all-failed error with log.Warn and returns nil, so the process prints PASS/exit 0 even when every stress put failed
broken_or_unfinished.evidence: cmd/dht-smoke/main.go:172-178 (error logged, nil returned) vs main.go:22-25 and runStress return at main.go:300-302

broken_or_unfinished.issue: Exported var ErrNoRecords is declared but never used anywhere in the repo (the empty-input path at cmd_aggregate_build.go:86-89 prints an inline message instead); dead code

Stale milestone-era package comment: main.go claims 'M1 only implements the engine smoke-test commands: version, add, and help' while the dispatcher has 13 command arms; similar stale M1/M2 comments in cmd_add ('M2 will add selective file downloading', 'for M1 we just drain it')

printUsage under-documents implemented flags: 'add' section omits --no-dht-publish, --dht-bootstrap, --dht-insecure, --regtest; 'search' section omits --signed-by; no usage section exists for create/files/trust/aggregate flags beyond one-line command summaries (flags are only discoverable via the flag package's -h per subcommand)

dht-smoke bootstrap wait loop degenerates to a busy-ish spin if bootstrapCtx expires before the deadline: the select's <-bootstrapCtx.Done() case returns immediately every iteration (both timers are 30s so the window is small, but the two timing mechanisms are redundant/uncoordinated)

open_questions: Is `add`-as-daemon the intended permanent design, or is a dedicated `daemon`/`serve` subcommand planned (the add command exits only via signal, so a completed download seeds forever and 'success' is exit 130)?
Are the testbed-only flags (--regtest, --dht-insecure, --dht-bootstrap, --no-dht-publish) omitted from printUsage deliberately to keep unsafe knobs undiscoverable, or is that doc drift to fix?

cmd_aggregate_build's comment says to 'pair it with a separate push-to-DHT step once the engine integration lands' — is a `aggregate publish`/push subcommand still planned CLI surface, or does the daemon's companion publisher now fully own that path?
For dht-smoke's stress phase, which is authoritative: the documented 'fail exit status if ALL puts fail' contract or the current always-PASS behavior?
Is `addTorrent`'s treat-anything-not-magnet-as-a-file-path dispatch (no infohash/URL forms accepted) intentional scope, or should `add <40-hex-infohash>` be supported eventually?

readers.purpose: Native desktop frontend for SwartzNet built on Fyne. cmd/swartznet-gui boots a full daemon (engine + indexer + companion pub/sub + optional HTTP API) exactly like the CLI, then internal/gui presents five tabs (Downloads, Search, Status, Companion, Settings) that call daemon subsystems directly in-process — no HTTP round-trip through httpapi. It is one of three coequal frontends; all subsystem lifecycle lives in internal/daemon, the GUI only polls and issues commands.

capabilities.behavior: Launcher flags: --data-dir, --index-dir, --port (-1 default = don't override; 0 = OS-assigned), --no-dht, --no-dht-publish, --api-addr (default localhost:7654, empty disables), --torrent (repeatable, auto-loads .torrent files at startup with per-file warnings on failure), --tab (open a named tab at startup). Exit code 2 on bad flag, 1 on daemon.New failure, 0 otherwise.
Config layering at startup: saved GUI Settings overrides (config.json data_dir/index_dir) are applied on top of config.Default(), then CLI flags win over the saved file.
Prints 'HTTP API listening on <addr>' to stdout when API enabled; SIGINT/SIGTERM cancel the daemon context; SWARTZNET_LOG env var sets slog level (debug|warn|error).

Main window: dark custom theme, restores previous window size from Fyne Preferences (default 900x600), title live-updates every 2s with aggregate down/up throughput ('SwartzNet vX — ↓ N/s ↑ N/s'), only calling SetTitle on change.

Window close is intercepted: persists window.width/height to preferences, then hides to system tray on desktop platforms (daemon keeps running) instead of quitting; real quit is via File>Quit / Ctrl+Q / tray Quit.
System tray (desktop only): Show SwartzNet, Add Magnet..., About items; tray icon and tray-linked window.

Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+N opens Add Magnet on Downloads tab, Ctrl+F switches to Search tab and focuses query entry, Ctrl+Q quits, bare Delete removes selected torrent(s) but only while Downloads tab is active. Main menu (File/Help) duplicates these with visible accelerator hints.

Desktop notification 'Download complete: <name>' fires when a torrent transitions to status 'seeding'; the first poll primes silently so torrents restored already-seeding from a previous session do not notify; map pruned to live torrents so a removed+re-added seeding torrent re-notifies.

About dialog: Version, Built date (falls back to '(dev build)' when BuildDate ldflag empty), full identity pubkey, BitTorrent port, HTTP API address — each with an inline Copy-to-clipboard button (suppressed for empty/'unknown'/'disabled'), plus a license line.

Downloads tab: 9-column table (Name, Status, Progress %, Size, Peers, ↓/↑ speed, Indexed yes/no, Signed) refreshed every 2s from Eng.TorrentSnapshots(); nameless torrents show infohash[:16]+'...'; Signed column shows '—' unsigned, '✓ '+pubkey[:8] signed, '★ '+pubkey[:8] trusted publisher; zero rates render '—'; empty-state overlay when no torrents.
Column-header click cycles sort per column: ascending → descending → cleared (engine insertion order); header shows ▲/▼ indicator; stable insertion sort.

Selection model: every row click toggles that torrent in a multi-select set keyed by infohash (no Ctrl/Shift needed since Fyne hides modifiers); selected names get a '✓ ' prefix; toolbar shows '(N selected)'; explicit Select All / Clear buttons; bulk actions hit the set, else fall back to the last-clicked row.
Toolbar actions: Add Magnet, Add .torrent (file picker filtered to .torrent), Create Torrent, Pause, Resume, Remove, Files..., Toggle Index, Select All, Clear.

Add Magnet dialog: URI entry + 'Index this torrent's files after download' checkbox (default on); client-side validation (magnet:? prefix, xt=urn:btih: present); on any error, an info dialog is shown and on dismiss the dialog REOPENS pre-filled with the bad URI and prior checkbox state so the user edits instead of re-pasting; engine errors rewritten to friendly text (zero infohash / parse magnet / engine closed).

Unchecking Index in Add Magnet flips SetTorrentIndexing(ih,false) immediately after AddMagnetURI so autoIndex doesn't index when metadata later arrives; Add .torrent always defaults indexing ON with no prompt.

Right-click context menu on the table (operates on selection): Files..., Pause/Resume (label reflects Paused state), Remove, Start/Stop indexing, queue Move to top/bottom (only shown when snapshot.Queued), Copy magnet link, Copy infohash; when the torrent is signed also Verify signature..., Trust this publisher / Revoke trust, Copy publisher pubkey. Action labels get ' (N selected)' suffix when 2+ selected.
Signature dialog shows torrent name, full infohash, full publisher pubkey, trust status ('✓ trusted' bold or 'untrusted'), and trust-store label.
Remove shows a confirm dialog explicitly stating on-disk files are kept (engine Drop() does not delete files or purge Bleve docs); on confirm removes each target and clears its selection entries.

Files dialog (per torrent): live 2s-polled list of files with name, size, progress bar, and per-file priority Select (none/normal/high); Select All = all normal, Deselect All = all none (failures aggregated into one error dialog); sort dropdown index/path/size/progress/priority; shows 'Waiting for metadata' info when file list is empty.

Create Torrent dialog: root file-or-folder (Choose File / Choose Folder browsers), editable torrent name auto-filled from root basename, piece-length presets (Auto/64KiB..16MiB), trackers (one per line, empty = DHT-only), webseed URLs (BEP-19), comment, Private checkbox (BEP-27), 'Sign with my ed25519 identity' checkbox default ON, output path auto-filled '<root>.torrent', 'Start seeding immediately' default ON. Hashing runs in background behind an indeterminate progress dialog; result dialog shows output path + infohash and seed status.
When seeding after create, the engine is told to seed from the user's original source path (AddTorrentMetaInfoSeedFrom(mi, opts.Root)) rather than DataDir, so the fresh torrent doesn't sit at 0%.

Search tab: query entry (Enter submits), layer checkboxes Local (default on) / Swarm / DHT (default off), Limit entry (strict positive-int parse, default 20), Search button, infinite progress bar, status line summarizing per-layer counts/errors ('Local: N hits | Swarm: N hits (asked=,responded=) | DHT: N hits (indexers=x/y)' or 'No search layers enabled'). Layers queried concurrently with a 10s overall context and 2s per-peer swarm timeout; a layer is skipped when its subsystem is nil.

Result cards per layer: local card shows [doctype] infohash[:16], score, file path for content docs, size, '✓ signed by <pk[:8]>'; swarm card shows score/seeders/sources/size; DHT card adds '(known-good)' when BloomHit. Every card has Confirm and Flag buttons plus a right-click menu: Add to downloads (via generated magnet), Copy magnet link, Copy infohash, Confirm (mark known-good), Flag as spam, Copy publisher pubkey (when signed).

Confirm adds the decoded 20-byte infohash to the known-good Bloom filter and records RecordConfirmed for every pubkey the SourceTracker attributes to that hit; Flag demotes only attributed indexer pubkeys (RecordFlagged) then Forget()s the attribution; with zero attribution it deliberately no-ops with an explanatory dialog.

Status tab (4s poll): cards for Torrents (counts by status downloading/seeding/queued/paused + aggregate rates), Local Index (docs/torrents/content docs/disk size), Swarm Peers (known / search-capable), DHT Routing (good/total nodes), Aggregate v0.5 (PPMI enabled, known indexers, record source kind cache/custom, cache size, bootstrap anchors/admitted/pending), DHT Publisher (keywords, total hits, pubkey truncated to 16 chars), Known-Good Filter (estimated items), and a Reputation list (pubkey[:16], score %.3f, hits 'returned/confirmed/flagged').

Companion tab (4s poll): Publisher card with full 64-char pubkey (monospace, selectable, wrap-break, Copy button), last refresh time (RFC3339), published count, last companion infohash, last error, and a 'Refresh Now' button calling CompPub.RefreshNow() asynchronously; Follow form (64-hex pubkey + label, validated); Followed Publishers list sorted by label then pubkey showing torrents/content imported, last sync time, last error, per-row Unfollow button, plus a right-click menu (Copy public key, Copy label, Unfollow) keyed by pubkey; empty-state hint when following nobody.

Settings tab: Sharing Capabilities card (radio L0 don't answer / L1 in-swarm only / L2 full local index, plus 'Share file paths' and 'Share content text snippets' checkboxes) mapped onto swarmsearch.Capabilities and applied live via SetCapabilities; Bandwidth Limits card in KiB/s (0 = unlimited, applied immediately via engine setters, value*1024 to bytes); Queue Management card for max active downloads (0 = unlimited); Storage Paths card with Browse dialogs, Save (persists to config.json, restart required — dialog says so; rejects empty paths) and Reset to defaults; read-only Runtime card (listen port, DHT enabled/disabled).
SelectTab(name) maps case-insensitive trimmed names downloads/search/status/companion/settings to tab indices 0-4, silently ignoring unknown names; backs the --tab flag.
Every tab's content is wrapped in a scroll container so the window minimum size stays small enough for 1366x768 laptops.

inputs_outputs: In: CLI flags (--data-dir, --index-dir, --port, --no-dht, --no-dht-publish, --api-addr, --torrent repeated, --tab); env SWARTZNET_LOG; SIGINT/SIGTERM; saved config.json overrides; Fyne Preferences (window.width/height floats under app ID net.swartznet.gui); .torrent files via file dialogs; user text (magnet URIs, queries, pubkeys, paths).

Out: stdout ('HTTP API listening on', 'Loaded <file>') and stderr warnings; process exit codes 0/1/2; OS desktop notifications on download completion; system clipboard writes (magnet links, infohashes, pubkeys, port, API addr); config.json written atomically (tmp+rename); .torrent files written via engine CreateTorrentFile; window title throughput updates.

nonobvious_rules.rule: Config precedence at GUI startup is Default() < saved config.json < CLI flags — operators can always force paths past a suspect persisted config.
--port default is -1 meaning 'don't touch cfg.ListenPort'; 0 is a meaningful value (OS-assigned), so the sentinel must stay negative.

All selection state (downloads rows, companion follow rows) is keyed by infohash/pubkey, never row index, because 2-4s poll loops re-sort lists underneath the user; a rewrite storing row indices would remove/unfollow the wrong item.
Every row click toggles multi-selection (no Ctrl/Shift) because Fyne's Table.OnSelected exposes no modifier state; paired with explicit Select All / Clear buttons as the deliberate compensation.

First notification poll 'primes' the lastNotified map silently so torrents restored already-seeding never fire a false 'Download complete'; pruning to currently-present torrents accepts re-notify on re-add as the lesser evil vs unbounded map growth.
Window title is only SetTitle'd when the computed string changes, because some window managers throttle apps that spam title updates (breaks interactive resize).

magnetLink URL-escapes the dn name: names come from remote peers/DHT and the generated magnet is fed straight back into AddMagnetURI, so an unescaped '&' would be magnet-parameter injection (e.g. bogus tracker), not mere cosmetics.

Flag-as-spam with no source attribution deliberately no-ops (dialog explains) instead of demoting all known indexers — a fallback demote-all would let an attacker weaponize unattributed spam to crater the whole reputation table.
Add-magnet with Index unchecked must call SetTorrentIndexing(ih,false) immediately after add, before metadata arrives, or engine autoIndex will index it when GotInfo fires (up to 5-min window).
Add-magnet errors reopen the dialog pre-filled with the bad URI + prior checkbox state (dialog → error → dialog loop) so users fix typos instead of re-pasting long URIs.

files_dialog.bindPrioSelect must detach OnChanged BEFORE SetSelected on the recycled Select widget: Fyne's SetSelected unconditionally fires OnChanged, and the still-attached handler is the previous row's closure — leaving it would write wrong-file priorities on every scroll/refresh. New handler also skips no-op writes.

Create Torrent Save As... browser closes and DELETES the empty file Fyne's writer created, because the real CreateTorrentFile path does its own atomic write; also seeds from opts.Root (not DataDir) after create so content isn't invisible at 0%.

Create dialog defensively autofills output path '<root>.torrent' at submit time if empty (OnChanged can be missed on paste/focus quirks on some platforms); trailing separator stripped so /a/b/ → /a/b.torrent.
Signing default is ON in Create Torrent because every running node has an identity and signing is infohash-preserving/free.
Search Limit is parsed strictly (whole field must be a positive integer, default 20) — Sscanf-style lax parsing previously let '5; rm' and negatives through to the search layers.
Header column sort is 3-state per column: asc → desc → cleared back to engine insertion order (add-time FIFO); sort uses stable insertion sort. Signed-column ascending puts signed torrents first.
Shortcuts use Control on ALL platforms including macOS (no Cmd mapping) — an explicit 'widely-compatible default' decision, deferred pending feedback.

Delete-key removal is registered via Canvas.SetOnTypedKey (fires regardless of focused widget) and gated only on 'Downloads tab is selected'; Remove always confirms via dialog specifically so a stray Delete can't silently vanish a row.
Remove keeps downloaded files on disk AND leaves Bleve content docs in the index — the dialog copy promises this; a rewrite that purges either changes user-visible contract.

Storage-path changes are persist-only (config.json) and require restart; live re-pointing is explicitly rejected as unsafe while torrents are active. Empty paths refused so next launch can't fail Validate on ''.

Companion publisher pubkey is shown FULL-length, monospace, selectable, with Copy button — truncation was reverted because the 'tell a friend my pubkey' flow needs a pasteable 64-char value; follow rows sort by label then pubkey to keep stable screen positions across 4s refreshes.
Per-row Unfollow buttons capture the full pubkey (not row index) at render time so a recycled list button firing after a re-sort still targets the right publisher.

Package-level test seams afterRemoveSelected/afterAddMagnet/afterRunSearch/afterCreateTorrent/afterSetAllPriorities/afterRefreshPublisher are nil in production and only exist so tests can join async UI goroutines; every user action that touches the engine runs in its own goroutine with errors marshalled back via fyne.Do.

Theme is a fixed dark palette intentionally mirroring the web UI's CSS variables (comments name each --var) so the two frontends look like one product; unknown names delegate to Fyne's default dark variant.
windowForObject resolves a widget's parent window by canvas identity, falling back to the driver's first window during early startup/tests — shared by all tabs for dialog parenting.

Version defaults to the latest release tag in source (v0.8.0) rather than a dev placeholder so go-run launches show something meaningful; BuildDate empty ⇒ About shows '(dev build)' as the tell for unofficial binaries.

broken_or_unfinished.issue: Status tab comment claims a disabled-DHT daemon renders '-' in the DHT Routing card, but refresh() always formats the (0,0) values with %d — after the first 4s tick the card shows '0'/'0', not '-'. Only the pre-first-refresh placeholder is '-'.

Search empty-state after zero-hit searches shows the original generic hint instead of a per-query 'no results for <q>' message; the code comment explicitly documents this as a punt ('we stuck with container.NewStack so we can't replace children').
About dialog license line says 'MPL 2.0 (engine) + MIT (SwartzNet code)' but the repository LICENSE is Apache 2.0 and CLAUDE.md states new files stay Apache 2.0 — user-visible misinformation.
FyneApp.toml Version is stale at 0.3.0 while main.go's default Version is v0.8.0; packaging metadata drifts from the ldflags version.
Local search-hit cards cannot show trusted-publisher status (only '✓ signed by'); comment defers it until indexer.SearchHit carries TrustedPublisher directly — acknowledged future iteration.

Search tab's constructor takes a context it ignores (newSearchTab(_ context.Context, ...)), unlike every other tab — leftover signature symmetry; per-search goroutines use their own 10s context instead, so an app-level cancel does not abort an in-flight search.

readers.purpose: internal/config defines the single runtime Config struct (every knob a node has), XDG-aware default paths for all persistent state, validation with fail-closed guards on production-dangerous flags, and a narrow GUI-persisted override file. internal/daemon is the wiring point: daemon.New(ctx, Options) constructs and starts every subsystem (engine, Bleve indexer, companion publisher/subscriber, Aggregate cold-start bootstrap, session restore, HTTP API) in a fixed order for all three frontends (CLI, GUI, web UI), and Daemon.Close tears them down in reverse. It also owns the daemon-side adapters that keep httpapi decoupled from engine/companion types, the on-disk companion follow-list format, and the v0.5 "Aggregate" cold-subscriber bootstrap (anchor PPMI fetch, endorsement/crawl admission policy, HTTPS anchor fallback).

capabilities.behavior: One-call node construction: daemon.New(ctx, Options) returns a fully wired node used identically by CLI `swartznet add`, the GUI, and (via embedded web UI) the HTTP API; frontends differ only in presentation. Startup order: engine -> indexer -> companion publisher -> companion subscriber -> aggregate bootstrap -> session restore -> HTTP API.

Graceful shutdown in exact reverse order: Close cancels the daemon-owned background context and joins bg goroutines FIRST (so no anchor fetch touches the engine mid-teardown), then stops HTTP API with a 3s timeout, companion subscriber, companion publisher, index, engine.

Options.NoIndex (CLI --no-index) skips opening Bleve entirely (Daemon.Index nil) AND mirrors into Cfg.NoIndex so the engine also suppresses the Layer-D BEP-44 keyword publisher — global opt-out semantics, verified by regression test.

Degraded startup instead of abort: only engine.New and indexer.Open failures make daemon.New return an error (indexer failure also closes the engine). Companion publisher/subscriber init, bootstrap init, and HTTP API Start failures print a 'warning:' line to Options.Stderr (io.Discard when nil) and the daemon runs without that subsystem.

Companion publisher starts only when ALL of: index open, engine PointerPutter (DHT put path), engine Identity, and Cfg.CompanionDir non-empty; writes artifacts into CompanionDir (never DataDir). Regtest flips it to accelerated RegtestPublisherOptions.

Companion subscriber starts when index + PointerGetter + CompanionDir present (no identity needed); on startup loads the follow list from Cfg.CompanionFollowFile — missing file = empty list, corrupt/oversized file = logged warn 'daemon.companion.load_follow_file_err' and empty list (fail-closed, follows still addable via API).

Follow/Unfollow via the HTTP API mutate the in-memory subscriber AND atomically rewrite companion-follows.json (tmp + rename, 0600) under a mutex so the list survives restart; persistence silently skipped when followPath is empty.

Aggregate cold-start bootstrap (P4.1) constructed only when eng.Lookup() != nil (DHT on): channel A fetches each anchor pubkey's PPMI in parallel and admits successes into the Lookup set + marks them reputation-seeded; a background anchor loop re-runs channel A whenever FallbackToHTTPS later adds anchors (initial run only if anchors already configured).

Channel C: swarmsearch peer_announce endorsement gossip routed into Bootstrap.IngestEndorsement via an EndorsementSink adapter; a candidate is admitted when already admitted, or when >= EndorsementThreshold (3) distinct endorsers each have tracker reputation >= 0.5, or when the bloom policy passes. Publisher pubkeys seen in sync records feed CandidateFromCrawl(sigValid=true) via a PublisherObserver adapter.

Admission bookkeeping surfaces to operators: IsAdmitted/IsPending/AdmittedCount/AnchorCount/PendingCount feed the httpapi /aggregate endpoint through the BootstrapProbe option; cap refusals are logged 'daemon.aggregate_bootstrap.admit_capped' so a starved node is distinguishable from a quiet network.

HTTPS last-ditch anchor fallback: FallbackToHTTPS GETs a JSON anchor list, enforces https:// scheme (loopback http allowed only via a test-only client flag, never on the public entry point), caps the body at 64 KiB, skips malformed hex entries silently, dedupes, appends new anchors, and wakes the anchor loop via a buffered coalescing channel.

HTTP API wiring: when Options.APIAddr non-empty, sets /healthz version from Options.Version and starts httpapi with adapters exposing: index search, swarm search, Layer-D publisher/lookup, bloom, reputation tracker, source tracker, torrent add, full torrent control (add-magnet, pause, resume, remove, per-torrent indexing toggle, file list, per-file priority, up/down rate limits, max active downloads, snapshots), companion status/refresh/follow, DHT routing-table stats, bootstrap probe.

Session restore: every torrent in the on-disk session manifest is re-added at startup so users see their previous list; per-entry failures are warn-logged inside the engine and the returned error is deliberately ignored so restore can never block startup.

Config.Default() supplies a fully usable out-of-the-box config: ListenPort 42069, Seed=true, all persistent-state paths rooted at the XDG share root (data/, index/, identity.key, publisher.json, reputation.json, seeds.json, known-good.bloom, companion/, companion-follows.json, trust.json), MinIndexerScore 0.

Config.Validate() (called by engine.New) rejects empty DataDir and out-of-range ports, creates DataDir (0755) and IndexDir's PARENT (Bleve creates the leaf), and fail-closed rejects Regtest/DHTInsecure unless running in a `go test` binary or SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 is set.

GUI settings persistence: SaveUserOverrides writes only {data_dir,index_dir} to shareRoot/config.json (pretty JSON, tmp+rename, 0644, empty fields omitted so defaults reapply); LoadUserOverrides treats missing file as no-op but errors on malformed JSON. GUI layers saved overrides on Default(), then CLI flags win over the saved file.

Sibling internal packages wired here: engine (anacrolix/torrent wrapper), indexer (Bleve v3), companion (BEP-46 pointer-pattern index torrents), httpapi, swarmsearch (sn_search BEP-10 LTEP extension), dhtindex (BEP-44 Lookup/PPMIGetter), reputation (Tracker, BloomFilter)

BEP references encoded in config semantics: BEP-44 mutable-item publishing (DisableDHTPublish), BEP-42 node-ID security (DHTInsecure maps to dht.ServerConfig.NoSecurity), BEP-46 companion pointers, BEP-51 sample_infohashes (planned bootstrap channel B), BEP-5 DHT bootstrap (DHTBootstrapAddrs overrides router.bittorrent.com defaults)
XDG Base Directory spec for default paths; ListenPort 42069 deliberately matches anacrolix/torrent's default

Design docs this area implements: SPEC.md sections 3/3.2/3.5 and PROPOSAL.md sections 2.2/3.5 (Aggregate bootstrap channels A/B/C, anchor trust seeds, HTTPS threat model), docs/08-operations.md (DisableDHTPublish privacy mode)

nonobvious_rules.rule: Startup/teardown order is load-bearing and fixed: engine, indexer, companion pub, companion sub, bootstrap, session restore, HTTP API — and Close must first cancel+join the daemon-owned background goroutines before any subsystem teardown, guaranteeing no anchor fetch touches the engine during Close even if the caller never cancels the parent ctx.

Options.NoIndex must be mirrored into Cfg.NoIndex before engine construction; skipping only Bleve while leaving Cfg.NoIndex false would keep the Layer-D keyword publisher announcing under the user's identity — an explicit documented privacy regression a rewrite must not reintroduce.

Empty string = feature off, consistently: IndexDir="" (valid, index validation skipped), CompanionDir="" (companion pub+sub disabled), CompanionFollowFile="" (in-memory follows only, no persistence), TrustPath="" (trust nobody automatically), APIAddr="" (no HTTP API), ListenPort=0 (OS-assigned). Frontends use port flag sentinel -1 for 'keep config default' so 0 stays meaningful.

TWO different env-var gates guard the same dangerous flags: the CLI refuses --regtest/--dht-insecure without SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1, and config.Validate independently rejects Regtest/DHTInsecure unless testing.Testing() is true OR SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1. A production binary needs BOTH set to run regtest. The value must be exactly "1" ("yes" is rejected).

Regtest accelerations are exact constants a rewrite must reproduce: dhtindex Publisher RefreshInterval 1h->5s, MinPutInterval 55m->100ms; companion Publisher Interval 1h->10s, MinInterval 1m->100ms; daemon.New selects companion.RegtestPublisherOptions when Cfg.Regtest; engine logs engine.regtest_mode_active at Warn.
Validate creates DataDir itself but only IndexDir's PARENT — Bleve must create the leaf directory (Bleve errors if the leaf pre-exists as an empty dir).

Anchor admissions are exempt from the MaxTrackedPublishers cap (cap check is len(admitted)-anchorsAdmitted >= cap); anchors also get reputation MarkSeeded while bep51/endorsement candidates start at the unknown score 0.5 and must earn reputation. Defaults: MaxTrackedPublishers=100, EndorsementThreshold=3 strong endorsers (tracker reputation >= 0.5 each; without a tracker ANY endorser counts).

bloomPolicy default-denies when no Bloom filter is attached (keeps channel B quiet on a cold cache) and otherwise admits only on tracker score >= 0.3 — the Bloom filter's contents are never actually consulted; presence alone gates. Crawl candidates that fail the gate are retained in the 'observed' set so IsPending is truthful and later endorsements can promote them.

runAnchorLoop skips the initial channel-A run when zero anchors are configured (the dev default) and instead waits on the anchorsAdded channel — a buffered size-1 coalescing signal fired by FallbackToHTTPS only when it added >0 new anchors. Without this loop a late HTTPS-supplied anchor list would never be fetched.

HTTPS fallback is https-scheme-only at the public entry point (loopback-http exemption exists solely for the test client), response body hard-capped at 64 KiB (read cap+1 to detect overflow), non-200 rejected, malformed hex anchors skipped silently, and the endpoint serves only pubkeys never records — compromise can delay bootstrap but cannot poison the index.

Follow file loading: >1 MiB fails closed wholesale (half-loading would silently drop a suffix of the user's follows), but individually malformed pubkey rows are skipped with a stderr warning and the rest load — partial loads deliberately permitted. Missing file is success (0, nil). Errors are BOTH written human-readably to stderr and returned for the structured logger (dual reporting is intentional back-compat).

GUI-persisted config is deliberately restricted to DataDir/IndexDir ('I keep my torrents on a separate disk' preference); port/DHT knobs are excluded on purpose to avoid support burden. Precedence: Default() < saved config.json < CLI flags. Empty fields are omitted from the JSON so next launch falls back to Default() rather than locking in blank strings.

ListenHost exists specifically so multi-node test harnesses can pin loopback: BEP-44 write tokens are keyed on the query's source IP, and OS source-IP flapping silently rejects puts. DisableIPv6 exists because dual-stack spawns two DHT servers but the Publisher drives only one, and v4-mapped-v6 addresses break put round-trips. Both default off.

RestoreSession's error is deliberately discarded ('_ =') — per-entry failures are warn-logged in the engine and must never block daemon startup; likewise httpapi Start failure leaves d.API nil rather than failing New.

The httpapi package must never import internal/engine or internal/companion; the daemon translates engine.TorrentSnapshot/TorrentFile and companion statuses field-by-field through adapters. A rewrite that shares types across that seam breaks the documented layering.

CandidateFromCrawl requires sigValid=true (SPEC 3.2: valid snet.sig before admission) — callers verify ed25519 upstream; the observer adapter hardcodes true because swarmsearch sync records were already per-record verified.

open_questions: Who/what is meant to invoke FallbackToHTTPS in production — an automatic daemon loop detecting 'channels A/B/C exhausted' (per bootstrap_https.go header), an operator action via the HTTP API, or release tooling? Nothing is wired today.

Are the two distinct env gates (SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 in the CLI, SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 in config.Validate) intentional defense-in-depth, or an accident that should be unified? A rewrite could easily collapse them and change operator-facing behavior.

What is the final intended bloomPolicy? The comment sketches 'at least 2 candidate hits in the known-good Bloom OR 1 overlap with an anchor's index', but hits are only available post-admission via the companion torrent — how is that chicken-and-egg meant to resolve?
Is Bootstrap admission state (admitted/observed/endorsements) meant to stay ephemeral across restarts, or should it eventually persist like reputation.json does?

Is the session-restore placement (after bootstrap construction, before HTTP API start) load-bearing beyond 'user sees their list when the UI opens', e.g. must restored torrents be visible to the first API request?
Should the GUI-persisted config.json ever grow beyond data_dir/index_dir (the comment says the narrowness is deliberate), and is 0644 vs the follow file's 0600 an intentional distinction?

readers.purpose: internal/engine is the single wrapper around anacrolix/torrent that all SwartzNet frontends (CLI, HTTP API, GUI, daemon) talk to. It owns the torrent.Client lifecycle and layers on top of it: session save/restore, a download-slot queue, pause/resume, per-file priorities, runtime rate limits, .torrent creation + ed25519 signing, and the extension hooks that feed the other three subsystems — piece/file-completion events into the Bleve indexer (Layer L), sn_search LTEP wiring (Layer S), and DHT keyword/pointer publishing (Layer D) — while keeping every wire behavior mainline-compatible.

capabilities.behavior: Add a torrent by magnet URI: URI is parsed locally first so invalid/zero-infohash magnets fail fast with an error instead of panicking the daemon; add is recorded in session.json; metadata fetch continues asynchronously. AddMagnetURI wraps this with recover() for the HTTP API so pathological input becomes a 400, never a crash.

Add a torrent by .torrent file: verifies an optional SwartzNet ed25519 signature (snet.pubkey/snet.sig) at add time; a verified pubkey becomes Handle.SignedBy (surfaced in snapshots/session), a bad signature is logged as rejected but the torrent still adds; the original raw bytes are copied to <DataDir>/torrents/<infohash>.torrent so restore works even if the user deletes the source file.

Add a torrent by raw 20-byte infohash (used by the companion subscriber for BEP-46 pointer targets): zero infohash rejected up front, client call wrapped in recover() because the infohash is attacker-controlled.

Add an in-memory metainfo and start seeding it (create-torrent and companion-publisher flows), optionally with per-torrent storage rooted at the content's real on-disk location (AddTorrentMetaInfoSeedFrom) so a torrent created outside DataDir seeds in place instead of showing 0%; kicks a background VerifyData rehash so the progress bar reflects on-disk state without waiting for peers; persists metainfo + DataPath/ContentName to the session.

Create a .torrent from a local file or directory: auto piece length via metainfo.ChoosePieceLength when unset, name override, tracker list (first URL = Announce, all as one AnnounceList tier), BEP-19 web seeds, BEP-27 private flag, comment, CreatedBy defaulting to "SwartzNet", and optional infohash-preserving ed25519 signing; CreateTorrentFile writes atomically (tmp+rename) and returns the hex infohash.

Session persistence and restore: every add/pause/resume/indexing-toggle/queue change updates <DataDir>/session.json (atomic write); RestoreSession (called by daemon.New at startup) re-adds every entry in queue order, preferring the on-disk .torrent copy, then magnet URI, then bare infohash, re-applying paused/indexing/queueOrder/signedBy and seed-from storage; per-entry failures are logged and skipped, never fatal; every restored torrent gets a background VerifyData so partial downloads resume at their real percentage.

Magnet-to-file session upgrade: once metadata arrives for a magnet/infohash-added torrent, the in-memory metainfo is serialized into torrents/ and the session entry gains a TorrentFile so future restarts skip the ut_metadata round trip; AddedVia stays "magnet"/"infohash" for posterity.

Auto-download on metadata arrival: flips every file to Normal priority (deliberately per-file, not DownloadAll) so both anacrolix priority surfaces update and the Files UI shows "normal"; respects paused state and the download-slot cap; gives up after 5 minutes if metadata never arrives.

Download queue: SetMaxActiveDownloads(n) caps concurrent downloads (0 = unlimited); over-cap torrents sit "queued" — metadata fetch and indexing still run, only the file-priority flip is deferred; promotion is FIFO by a monotonic per-handle queueOrder, re-evaluated on pause, remove, completion, or cap raise; QueueMoveToFront/Back reassign order to min-1/max+1; a promoteMu serializes count-then-activate so batch restores can't over-subscribe the cap.

Pause/resume per torrent (idempotent, persisted): pause is a soft stop — DisallowDataDownload+Upload, peer conns stay open for sn_search — and frees a download slot; resume re-runs queueOrActivate so a torrent paused before metadata still gets its priorities flipped later.

Per-file view and priority control: TorrentFiles returns index/path/length/completed/progress/priority per file (empty slice pre-metadata); SetFilePriority accepts none/normal/high, where "none" removes the file from the download set.
Runtime-mutable upload/download rate limits shared by all connections; 0 or negative = unlimited; getters return 0 for unlimited.

Per-torrent event streams: PieceEvents (raw piece state changes, buffer 64, drop-on-full with debug log) and file-completion events — exactly one FileCompleteEvent per file the first time all its pieces verify, fanned out to any number of subscribers with a replay buffer for files already complete at subscribe time.

Auto-indexing (Layer L): when an index is attached via SetIndex, each torrent's metadata-level doc (infohash, name, file paths, trackers, size, file count, signedBy) is written to Bleve on GotInfo, and each completed file is submitted to the content-extraction pipeline (100 MiB per-file extract cap) via a lazy NewReader; per-torrent opt-out via SetTorrentIndexing is prospective-only and persisted; SetIndex(nil) unwires both the pipeline and the sn_search LocalSearcher.

Layer-D publishing: on metadata arrival the torrent's keywords are submitted to the DHT BEP-44 publisher (unless NoIndex/DisableDHTPublish suppressed the worker), and MintAggregateRecords signs one LocalRecord per tokenized keyword of the name into the RecordCache (PoW=0 for the current migration window) for sync-session responders; RemoveTorrent retracts the infohash from the publisher manifest.

sn_search (Layer S) wiring: advertises the extension in every outbound LTEP handshake (PeerConnAdded), records remote capability from ReadExtendedHandshake, dispatches inbound frames asynchronously off anacrolix's read loop with a 256-slot admission semaphore (overflow frames dropped) and a separately gated reply writer (overflow replies fail with errReplyOverloaded); tracks addr→PeerConn for outbound query fan-out; runs the M16e feeler goroutine; peer state dropped on PeerConnClosed.

DHT wire-compat setup: installs an in-memory PeerStore so get_peers replies carry BEP-5 write tokens; honors caller-provided bootstrap node lists; optional BEP-42 NoSecurity opt-out (DHTInsecure) for private/docker DHTs; pins BEP-44 item expiry to 2h when upstream leaves it 0 (otherwise every stored mutable item is instantly expired).

Reputation/spam-resistance lifecycle: loads known-good Bloom filter, reputation tracker (+ curated seed list of ~20 maintainer pubkeys with decaying +0.45 bonus), trust store, and an always-present in-memory SourceTracker; wires them into the DHT lookup with optional MinIndexerScore; on download completion the infohash is auto-added to the Bloom filter; a torrent signed by a trusted publisher is Bloom-confirmed immediately at add time; bloom+reputation are saved on Close.

Publisher identity + gossip: loads/creates the persistent ed25519 identity, builds shared BEP-46 pointer putter/getter (putter exists even in leech-only mode for the user's own companion publications), adds self as a known indexer for --dht self-search, feeds gossip-discovered pubkeys into the lookup, and sets caps.Publisher=1 only when actively publishing so passive nodes don't gossip themselves as indexers.

Companion-index fetch (companion.CompanionFetcher): adds by infohash, waits for metadata, rejects multi-file torrents, rejects declared size > 32 MiB before requesting any piece, rejects unsafe names (path separators, dot entries, backslash), downloads fully (250 ms completion poll), returns DataDir/<name>; ctx cancel aborts the wait but leaves the torrent for retry reuse.

GUI/API snapshots: TorrentSnapshots returns per-torrent progress, peer counts, seeders, status string (metadata/downloading/seeding/paused/queued), per-second transfer rates sampled against the previous call (zeros on first call, cached result if <100 ms since last sample), indexing progress counters from the pipeline, SignedBy, and a TrustedPublisher badge; fully defensive pre-metadata to avoid anacrolix nil-Info panics.

Remove torrent: closes subscriptions and the removed channel (releasing per-handle goroutines), drops the anacrolix torrent, deletes the session entry and its .torrent copy, retracts DHT keywords, promotes the next queued torrent — but leaves downloaded data on disk and Bleve entries in the index.

Ordered idempotent shutdown: cancel background ctx → stop pipeline → stop DHT publisher → save bloom + reputation → close all piece/file subscriptions → close client; repeated Close returns the cached error.

Regtest mode: loud Warn log ("DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION"), accelerated feeler interval, record-cache prune every 200 ms with 500 ms max age, and accelerated publisher options — so scenario tests observe hourly/daily cycles in seconds.
Background record-cache hygiene: FIFO cap of 100,000 records and an hourly prune goroutine dropping records older than 30 days.

Test/ops accessors: LocalPort, DHTAddr, DHTRoutingTableSize (good/total nodes), HandleByInfoHash, and AddTrustedPeerEngine which cross-wires two in-process engines as peers for testlab clusters (explicitly not for production).

Files out: <DataDir>/session.json (atomic tmp+rename), <DataDir>/torrents/<infohash>.torrent copies, created .torrent files at caller-chosen outPath, downloaded content under DataDir (or under the original content root for seed-from torrents), bloom/reputation saves on Close

Network in/out: full BitTorrent peer wire via anacrolix (BEP-3/9/10 + trackers), sn_search LTEP frames in/out on existing peer connections, DHT KRPC including BEP-44 mutable puts/gets and BEP-46 pointer resolution, BEP-19 web seeds on created torrents

Events out (in-process): PieceEvents channel per torrent, FileCompleteEvent fan-out per torrent, TorrentSnapshot/FileSnapshot polling structs consumed by httpapi/GUI/CLI, structured slog records (engine.*, indexer.*, file.complete)

Signals: ctx passed to New governs feeler lifecycle; Engine.Close cancels bgCtx which unblocks all background waiters (autoDownload/autoIndex/verify/upgrade/autoConfirm); Handle.removed channel unblocks per-torrent waiters on RemoveTorrent

nonobvious_rules.rule: Rate limiters must have a positive burst even in unlimited mode (unlimitedBurst = math.MaxInt32): anacrolix's openNewConns refuses to dial when DownloadRateLimiter.Tokens() <= 0, so a zero burst silently blocks ALL outgoing connections.

The DHT server MUST get a PeerStore, or get_peers replies carry no write token and vanilla clients' announce_peer stalls (BEP-5 break); the same shared InMemory instance also backs the local per-infohash peer table.
BEP-44 expiry must be pinned to 2h when anacrolix leaves ServerConfig.Exp at 0 — otherwise every stored mutable item is treated as instantly expired and put-then-get returns 'value not found'.

Inbound sn_search frames MUST be handled asynchronously: anacrolix holds the client lock during PeerConnReadExtensionMessage, so a synchronous reply self-deadlocks and a synchronous Bleve search stalls every peer; the payload must be copied because the decoder buffer is reused. Admission is bounded by two 256-slot semaphores (handlers and reply writers) with drop-on-full, never queue.
Download activation sets priority per-file instead of Torrent.DownloadAll because anacrolix keeps two parallel priority surfaces; DownloadAll leaves File.Priority stuck at 'none' in the GUI snapshot.

upgradeMagnetSession must never run for file/metainfo-added entries: a re-marshalled metainfo can differ byte-wise from the original and metainfo.Load then rejects it with 'expected EOF' on restore; the guard checks both TorrentFile presence and AddedVia.

Seed-from storage is keyed on the real on-disk basename (ContentName), NOT info.Name, so a torrent created with a renamed display name still seeds in place; piece completion for such storage is kept in memory deliberately, to avoid dropping a completion DB into the user's source directory — VerifyData on create/restore repopulates it.

Every add path (create, restore, metainfo) kicks a background VerifyData rehash because anacrolix verifies lazily on peer request — without it a fresh seed or restored torrent shows 0% forever when no peer asks.

A torrent with indexing disabled still submits its keywords to the DHT publisher and still mints aggregate records — only the local Bleve write is skipped ('publish a torrent's existence without exposing its file list in local searches').

caps.Publisher is flipped to 1 only when the node actually publishes (neither DisableDHTPublish nor NoIndex): the gossip path gates on caps.Publisher>0 rather than pubkey presence, and passive nodes must not gossip themselves as indexers. Conversely the BEP-46 pointerPutter is built even in leech-only/NoIndex mode because companion pointers are a separate opt-in publication.

Queued torrents keep metadata fetch and indexing; only the file-priority flip is deferred. Metadata-only torrents count as active downloads; seeding (complete) torrents never occupy a slot; reducing the cap does NOT demote already-active torrents.

Paused state must be applied at registration time (registerLockedPaused) before any background goroutine spawns, so a restored-paused torrent can never race into Normal priority; activateDownload also refuses paused handles, and ResumeTorrent re-runs queueOrActivate to flip priorities that were never set.

The count-then-activate decision is serialized on a dedicated promoteMu (separate from e.mu) — without it N concurrent autoDownload goroutines from a batch restore each observe active<cap and over-subscribe.

Companion fetch fails closed before requesting any piece: declared length > 32 MiB rejected, multi-file torrents rejected, names with /, \, '', '.', '..' rejected (backslash included so a manifest written on another OS can't smuggle a separator past Windows); returned path is hand-built as DataDir/<info.Name>.
Restore rejects session TorrentFile values that aren't plain basenames, so a hand-edited/corrupted manifest cannot read outside the torrents dir.
persistAdd only overwrites MagnetURI/TorrentFile when non-empty, specifically so an upgradeMagnetSession that raced ahead doesn't get clobbered with empty strings.

fileTracker fans out to N subscribers with per-subscriber drop-on-full, and keeps a doneReplay buffer so late subscribers (the ingest pipeline goroutine racing the tracker on an already-complete seed) still receive events for files complete at startup; replay overflow beyond the 64-slot buffer is dropped with a warning. The earlier single-channel design silently split events between CLI and indexer.
Handle.FileEvents() creates a NEW subscription per call — evaluating it inside a for/select loop hangs forever; callers must bind once (SubscribeFileEvents is the explicit alias).
Rate sampling: first snapshotOf call returns 0 rates; calls <100 ms apart return the cached previous rate; designed for the GUI's 2-second poll.
snapshotOf must not touch Length/BytesMissing/Stats/Files before Info() is non-nil — anacrolix v1.61.0 nil-panics pre-metadata; only InfoHash/Name/IsPaused are safe.

Background waiter timeouts are load-bearing: autoDownload/autoIndex give up after 5 min without metadata, upgradeMagnetSession/verifyOnRestore after 10 min, autoConfirmOnComplete after 24 h; all also unblock on bgCtx cancel, and autoConfirm additionally on the per-handle removed channel.
Duplicate adds (same infohash) return the existing Handle rather than erroring — mirror of anacrolix's own dedupe.

Close order matters: cancel bgCtx, stop pipeline before storage shuts down, stop publisher before the DHT server dies, save bloom/reputation, close subscriptions, then client.Close; engine.New never fails over a corrupt session/bloom/reputation/trust/identity — all degrade to warnings.
Nonzero rate limits set burst to one second of tokens with a 16 KiB floor (the largest single anacrolix reservation is a 16 KiB chunk).
AddTorrentMetaInfo returns `any` instead of *Handle deliberately, so internal/companion can consume it without importing internal/engine.
SetIndex installs a 100 MiB global per-file extract cap (previously 0 = per-extractor defaults, which let pathological PDFs buffer unbounded).

broken_or_unfinished.issue: Queue promotion on download completion is silently skipped when no Bloom filter is configured: autoConfirmOnComplete returns early on `bf == nil` BEFORE reaching promoteQueuedLocked, so with BloomPath unset (or bloom load failure) a completed torrent never frees its slot until some other trigger (pause/remove/cap change) fires. Completion is the most common slot-freeing event, and the queue doc claims completed torrents release their slot.
broken_or_unfinished.evidence: internal/engine/engine.go:1969-1985 (`if closed || bf == nil { return }` at 1973, promoteQueuedLocked at 1985); contrast queue.go:29-31

broken_or_unfinished.issue: TorrentSnapshot.Status documents a "complete" value that is never produced — the code emits only metadata/paused/queued/seeding/downloading (missing==0 maps to "seeding").

Misleading '-Locked' naming: promoteQueuedLocked and queueOrActivate's doc header ('queueOrActivateLocked') / countActiveDownloads' doc header ('countActiveDownloadsLocked') all imply the caller holds a lock, but these functions acquire promoteMu/e.mu themselves and callers must NOT hold e.mu — a rewrite following the names would deadlock.
DHTRoutingTableSize is self-described as 'effectively dead code' in production, kept exported only for tests/hypothetical dashboards.

SetIndex doc contradicts itself: 'Safe to call at most once per Engine. Calling it twice replaces the attached index and pipeline' — the code does support replacement (stops the old pipeline first), so the 'at most once' sentence is stale.

queue.go's 'active' definition ('any non-None file priority AND not paused AND not fully complete') does not match countActiveDownloads, which never inspects file priorities — it uses the queued flag + paused + BytesMissing. A torrent whose files were all manually set to 'none' still counts as active.
MintAggregateRecords mints with PoW=0 as an acknowledged interim state: 'the dual-read migration window doesn't require miners yet; a future schema bump will set MinPoWBitsDefault here'.
QueueMoveToFront triggers a promotion pass but QueueMoveToBack does not — asymmetric; harmless (moving to back can't free a slot) but looks unfinished next to its 'mirror' claim.

open_questions: Is the early return in autoConfirmOnComplete when bloom is nil (which also skips queue promotion on completion) intentional coupling or an accidental bug? The promote call reads like it belongs before the bloom gate.

Is 'indexing disabled still publishes keywords to the DHT' the intended privacy posture long-term? The comment frames it as a feature (publish existence without local search exposure), but it means the per-torrent 'don't index' toggle never suppresses network-visible publication — only --no-index / DisableDHTPublish do.
Should reducing MaxActiveDownloads eventually demote already-active torrents, or is take-effect-on-new-adds-only the permanent contract?
Is TorrentSnapshot.Status 'complete' a planned state (e.g. complete-but-not-seeding when Seed=false) that was never implemented, or stale doc?

fileTracker replay silently drops events beyond the 64-slot subscriber buffer for torrents with >64 already-complete files — the comment says 'larger torrents would simply need a bigger fileTrackerSubBuf'; is a real fix planned or is 64 considered permanently sufficient?

AddTorrentFile accepts and seeds a torrent whose snet signature FAILED verification (logged as warn, signedBy left empty). Is add-anyway the intended trust model, or should bad signatures block the add?
The '-Locked' suffixes on queue functions that actually take their own locks: refactor leftover to be renamed, or a local convention meaning 'takes promoteMu'?

readers.purpose: internal/indexer is Layer L of SwartzNet's three-layer search: a Bleve full-text index over (a) torrent-level metadata docs and (b) content-level docs holding text extracted from completed torrent files. It also owns the ingestion pipeline (file-complete event -> extractor dispatch -> chunking -> index write) and the extractor registry under internal/indexer/extractors that parses ~20 file formats into searchable text. internal/index is an empty, git-untracked stray directory containing nothing.

capabilities.behavior: Local full-text search: user query (Bleve QueryString syntax: OR-by-default terms, +required, -excluded, "phrase", field:term, fuzzy~1, boost^2) returns interleaved torrent-level and content-level hits sorted by relevance score, each hit carrying infohash, name/size/trackers/signed_by (torrent) or file path/index/mime/extractor (content), optional <mark>-wrapped highlight fragments, total count, and query duration

Search-by-publisher facet: a request may filter to torrents signed by a specific 64-char hex ed25519 pubkey, combinable with a text query or standing alone (empty query + SignedBy is valid and returns all of that publisher's signed torrents)

Reached by three frontends: CLI `swartznet search` opens the Bleve dir directly (no daemon) or routes via POST /search when --swarm/--dht/--signed-by given; HTTP POST /search runs the same Search for the Local section of the combined response; GUI Search tab calls Daemon.Index.Search directly; Layer S (sn_search) peer queries are answered from this same index via an adapter

Automatic torrent-level indexing: when a torrent's metadata arrives (waits up to 5 minutes for GotInfo), a TorrentDoc (name, file paths, trackers, size, file count, signer pubkey) is written to the index — unless the per-torrent indexing toggle is off

Automatic content extraction: every file-complete event on an indexing-enabled torrent is submitted to a single-worker Pipeline that picks an extractor by MIME/extension, runs it under a panic-recovery net and a 60s hard watchdog, splits output into ~2 KiB chunks at paragraph boundaries, and writes one ContentDoc per chunk

Per-torrent indexing toggle exposed as CLI `swartznet index <infohash> on|off`, HTTP POST /torrents/{infohash}/indexing {"enabled":bool}, and GUI Downloads right-click 'Start/Stop indexing'; effect is prospective only (already-indexed chunks stay)

Index size/stats reporting: GET /index/stats and the GUI Status tab 'Local Index' card report on-disk bytes, total/torrent/content doc counts, summed corpus text bytes, and the DirBytes/CorpusTextBytes inflation ratio (the v1.0.0 'index bytes per TB of text' measurement)
Per-torrent extraction progress counters (processed/extracted/skipped/failed keyed by lowercase infohash) surfaced in engine TorrentSnapshots as IndexedFiles/IndexExtracted for progress display

Bulk export for companion-index publishing (M11): AllTorrentDocs() and ContentDocsForInfoHash() walk the whole index in 1000-doc pages so companion.BuildFromIndex can serialize a shareable digest of everything indexed

Bulk import from remote publishers: the companion subscriber writes remote torrents/chunks into the same local index via IndexTorrent/IndexContent, so followed publishers' content becomes locally searchable

Schema-version self-healing: opening an index dir created under a different SchemaVersion (sentinel missing/unparseable counts as v0) logs indexer.schema_rebuild, deletes the entire directory, and recreates it empty; docs are expected to repopulate from re-added torrents
Deletion API: DeleteTorrent(infohash) and DeleteContentForTorrent(infohash) (batched query-then-delete with a fail-closed progress bound) exist for forgetting a torrent's index footprint

Extractor coverage (each emits searchable text; Name() lands in the doc's extractor field): plaintext (text/* incl. source code, json, html-as-raw-text), subtitle (SRT/VTT/SSA dialog only, timestamps/tags stripped), pdf (embedded text layer, no OCR), epub (all XHTML chapters in lexical order), docx (word/document.xml <w:t> runs), odt+odp (content.xml text:p/text:h), pptx (ppt/slides/slideN.xml <a:t> in numeric slide order), rtf (control-word subset), fb2 (title + body paragraphs), mobi/azw/azw3 (EXTH metadata only: title/author/publisher/description/ISBN), archive zip/tar/tar.gz (member NAMES only, sorted, 4 MiB cap), exif (JPEG camera/GPS metadata), id3 (MP3 tags), flac+ogg/opus (Vorbis comments), mp4/m4a/m4b (iTunes ilst atoms), mkv/webm (EBML Title/Tracks/Chapters/Tags), zim (per-article HTML->text, zstd/uncompressed clusters, max 5000 articles / 32 MiB)

data_models: Bleve index schema v3 (schema.go): one index, two document types discriminated by field 'type' (TypeField, DefaultType 'torrent'). Torrent doc fields: infohash (keyword), name (standard analyzer), files (standard; multi-paths joined with '\n' into ONE string), trackers (keyword, stored as array), size_bytes (numeric), added_at (datetime, RFC3339), file_count (numeric), signed_by (keyword, lowercased hex, added in v3 2026-04-13). Content doc fields: infohash (keyword), file_index (numeric), file_path (keyword), file_size (numeric), mime (keyword), text (standard analyzer — the searchable body), extractor (keyword), indexed_at (datetime). Full-text fields have Store+Index+IncludeInAll+IncludeTermVectors.

Doc ID scheme: torrent = 't:' + lowercase(infohash); content = 'c:' + lowercase(infohash) + ':' + fileIndex + ':' + chunkIndex — re-index is put-or-replace, chunks independent (indexer.go:188-190, content.go:39-41)
Schema sentinel: Bleve SetInternal key '_swartznet_schema_version' holding ASCII integer; lives outside the document store (indexer.go:18-24, 134-154)

In-memory API types: TorrentDoc, ContentDoc (with ChunkIndex), SearchRequest{Query, Limit, Highlight, SignedBy}, SearchHit (union of torrent+content fields + Fragments map[string][]string), SearchResponse{Total, Hits, Took}, Stats{DirBytes, DocCount, TorrentCount, ContentCount, CorpusTextBytes, InflationRatio}, PipelineStats{Processed, Extracted, Skipped, Failed}, FileInput, extractors.Chunk{Text, Offset}, extractors.Candidate{Path, MIME, Size}
