nonobvious_rules.rule: Extractor dispatch is first-claim-wins in registration order, and registration order is Go init() order = alphabetical by filename within the package. plaintext.go therefore registers BEFORE subtitle.go and must explicitly DECLINE subtitle MIME types (application/x-subrip, text/vtt, text/x-ssa) so SubtitleExtractor can claim them. A rewrite that changes file/registration order silently changes which extractor handles a format.
nonobvious_rules.evidence: extractor.go:90-101 ('claims is called in registration order'); plaintext.go:114-143

nonobvious_rules.rule: Raw .html/.htm files are indexed by the PLAINTEXT extractor with tags left in (text/html is in plaintext's accept list); the tag-stripping HTML walker (extractHTMLText) is only used for XHTML inside EPUBs and ZIM articles — there is no standalone HTML extractor.
nonobvious_rules.evidence: plaintext.go:133 ('text/html'); htmltext.go:16-18 ('Used by both the EPUB extractor ... and any future plain-HTML backend')

nonobvious_rules.rule: Extract errors are counted as 'skipped', not 'failed': only OpenReader failure or all-chunks-write-failure increments failed. Extract error/timeout/panic logs at Debug as pipeline.extract_skip. Processed always equals Extracted+Skipped+Failed (deferred processed.Add(1)).
nonobvious_rules.evidence: pipeline.go:156-237 (handle: extract err -> skipped.Add at 188-197; failed only at 177-182 and 224-226)

nonobvious_rules.rule: The extract watchdog (60s, var not const so tests can shrink it) deliberately LEAKS the wedged extractor goroutine — Go can't kill goroutines — and the file reader is closed only inside the extracting goroutine after Extract returns, never by the caller, because anacrolix torrent.Reader Read/Close race is unsafe.
nonobvious_rules.evidence: pipeline.go:271-307 (extractWatchdog doc), 320-334 (Close in child goroutine defer, LIFO before recover)

nonobvious_rules.rule: A torrent with indexing disabled still gets published to the Layer-D DHT index and still mints aggregate records — the opt-out only skips the local Bleve write and content extraction ('publish a torrent's existence without exposing its file list in their own local searches').
nonobvious_rules.evidence: engine.go:2066-2095 (autoIndex: 'still go to the DHT publisher')

nonobvious_rules.rule: Schema mismatch (including missing/corrupt sentinel, which reads as version 0) triggers os.RemoveAll of the ENTIRE index directory and silent recreation — all locally extracted content docs are destroyed and only torrent docs regenerate (via autoIndex on restore); content docs only repopulate when file-complete events re-fire.

Torrent file paths are flattened into a single '\n'-joined string for the 'files' field and split back on '\n' when reconstructing TorrentDoc from stored fields — a path containing a newline would corrupt round-tripping.

Every extractor enforces layered caps a rewrite must keep: dispatch-time size ceilings (subtitle 16 MiB, rtf/fb2 50 MiB, mobi 64 MiB, plaintext/exif 100 MiB, id3/archive 500 MiB, flac/ogg 1 GiB, mkv/mp4 64 GiB), input read caps via io.LimitReader (pdf/docx/odt/odp/pptx/epub 256 MiB), per-zip-entry DECOMPRESSED stream caps of maxDocTextBytes=64 MiB (deflate amplifies ~1032:1; without it one text node OOMs inside Token()/Next() where recover() cannot catch), and OUTPUT accumulation caps that gracefully truncate (index partial text) rather than error. Engine sets the pipeline per-file cap to 100 MiB.
nonobvious_rules.evidence: extractor.go:42-52; docx.go:78-82; epub.go:91-99; chunker.go:19-28; archive.go:46-51; engine.go:323

nonobvious_rules.rule: Chunker split preference order is paragraph (blank line, tolerating \r\n) -> line -> hard split at targetBytes; a paragraph up to 1.5x target (3 KiB) stays whole; text <= 1.25x target returns as a single chunk with Offset 0; flushed chunks carry byte offsets into the source text for a future jump-to-match UI.

MaxSearchLimit=10000 is a defence-in-depth cap inside Index.Search itself, above the httpapi 500 and sn_search 100 caps; Limit<=0 defaults to 20; empty Query AND empty SignedBy is the only rejected request shape.

SignedBy filtering and content-for-infohash selection use exact-match TermQuery (never QueryString) so a hostile infohash/pubkey cannot inject Bleve query grammar; both values are lowercased before matching.

All paginated index walks (Stats text scan, AllTorrentDocs, ContentDocsForInfoHash) run 1000-doc pages under the single global mutex with a defensive ceiling of (count/batch)+2 pages, logging a *_truncated warning if hit; deleteByQueryLocked instead FAILS CLOSED with an error after (initialTotal/batch)*2+4 iterations if deletes are ineffective.

EPUB chapter reading order is deliberately wrong-for-humans: the OPF spine is ignored and .xhtml/.html/.htm entries are concatenated in lexical filename order, because order is irrelevant to a keyword index and it avoids an OPF parser.

Archive extractor indexes member NAMES only (never contents), sorted, capped at 4 MiB of concatenated names, with tar.gz decompression walk bounded at 1 GiB; format detected by magic bytes (PK\x03\x04 / gzip 1f8b / tar-by-trial) not extension.

Plaintext extractor rejects files with a NUL byte in the first 4 KiB, strips a UTF-8 BOM, and returns invalid-UTF-8 files anyway with bad bytes replaced by U+FFFD rather than failing ('searching the readable parts beats failing').

MIME resolution consults SwartzNet's extTypes override map BEFORE stdlib mime.TypeByExtension (so .txt indexes identically on Alpine/scratch images with no /etc/mime.types, and .ts means TypeScript not MPEG-TS); stdlib results have any ';charset=' suffix stripped.

ZIM cluster decompression uses a true-LRU 32-entry cache (container/list + map) specifically because the URL pointer list is only roughly cluster-sorted and random eviction thrashes; XZ-compressed (type 4) clusters are skipped by design so pre-2021 ZIMs index zero articles.
IndexContent rejects empty Text (error) while extractors signal 'no text' with a nil chunk slice + nil error; the pipeline drops zero-chunk results as 'skipped' before any index write.

Local and remote (companion-subscribed) documents share one index and one doc-ID namespace — a remote publisher's record for infohash X occupies the same 't:x'/'c:x:i:c' IDs as a local add, so whichever writes last wins; remote torrent docs carry no Trackers/SignedBy.
Fragments maps are deep-copied from Bleve and only populated when Highlight was requested; highlighting is scoped to fields name/files/text only, using Bleve's HTML style (<mark>).

readers.purpose: Layer S of SwartzNet's three-layer search: a BEP-10 (LTEP) user extension named "sn_search" that lets two BitTorrent peers on an ordinary piece-transfer connection exchange full-text search queries/results, announce capability bits and publisher pubkeys, and run RIBLT set-reconciliation ("Aggregate sync", msg_types 4-8) of signed keyword→infohash records. It is deliberately invisible to vanilla clients (unknown name in the LTEP `m` dict) and layers Bitcoin-Core-inspired defenses (AddrMan tried/new peer book, misbehavior scores + local bans, per-peer token buckets, feeler probes) on top of the wire protocol.

capabilities.behavior: Advertises "sn_search" in every outbound LTEP handshake (registered per-connection from the engine's PeerConnAdded callback) and records each remote peer's support + chosen extension id from their handshake `m` dict; unsupported peers are tracked but never sent sn_search frames

On seeing a capable peer, fire-and-forget sends one peer_announce (msg_type 3) carrying protocol version 1, a 64-bit services bitfield, and (when the node is an active Layer-D publisher) its 32-byte ed25519 pubkey; sends are queued to a single bounded worker (depth 64, overflow drops)

Answers inbound queries (msg_type 0) by running the query against the local Bleve index via a LocalSearcher adapter and replying with a Result (msg_type 1) that groups content hits into per-torrent Hit rows with FileMatch entries, or a Reject (msg_type 2) with codes 0-4

Inbound queries are rejected with reject code 0 when a per-peer token bucket (default 5 queries/s, burst 10, runtime-configurable via SetRateLimit) is exhausted; code 4 when no searcher / ShareLocal 0 or 1; code 2 when scope asks for f/c hits the node's capabilities lack; code 3 when the trimmed query is under 2 characters; per-peer limit clamped to 1..100, default 50

Outbound Query() fans a bencoded query out to all "tried" peers plus up to 2 untried "feeler" peers (all supported peers when the tried table is empty), waits until every asked peer answered or the timeout (default 3 s) expires, then returns merged hits deduplicated by infohash with summed rank (capped 1000), max seeders, first non-empty name/size, union of file matches, and per-hit source-peer attribution, sorted score desc then seeders desc

Maintains an AddrMan-style two-table PeerBook (tried max 256 / new max 1024): peers enter "new" on capable handshake, are promoted to "tried" only after responding correctly to a real query, get Failures recorded on timeout/reject, and are removed on disconnect; eviction is oldest-seen from new, least-recently-queried from tried

A background feeler goroutine (started once per engine, 30 s interval in prod / 2 s in regtest, CAS-guarded against duplicates) fires a throwaway query "__sn_feeler__" whenever untried peers exist, giving them a promotion chance through the normal query path

Tracks per-peer misbehavior points (bad bencode 20, bad record sig 20, stale txid 10, unexpected/unknown message 10, malformed result 10, rate-limited 5, too-broad query 5); crossing 100 points bans the peer locally for 24 h — banned peers are rejected at handshake and every inbound frame from them is dropped; bans are in-memory only, survive peer disconnect, and are never gossiped

Anti-spoofing on responses: a Result/Reject is only accepted if its txid matches a live pending query AND the sender is in that query's fan-out set; stale txids, unasked peers, and semantically-malformed results are charged misbehavior and dropped (malformed results are charged before the txid lookup)
Populates a 4096-entry LRU HitCache with merged hits after every fan-out (BIP-152-inspired; intended as state store for a future v1.1 compact short-ID wire encoding)

Responder side of Aggregate sync: on sync_begin (msg_type 4) snapshots matching records from the attached RecordSource, streams one batch of up to 100 RIBLT symbols (or immediately sync_end "converged" for a zero-record set), serves sync_need (6) lookups with sync_records (7), and tears down on sync_end (8); all sync frames are gated on the remote having announced BitSetReconciliation (bit 9), else reject code 2 + misbehavior charge

Responder sync sessions are bounded: max 4 concurrent per peer (re-begin on the same txid replaces, does not count), and any session older than 2 minutes is lazily reaped on the next inbound sync frame from that peer, emitting sync_end "aborted" so the initiator sees a terminal state; protocol violations mid-session (phase errors, symbol-index desync, budget overruns) produce sync_end "aborted"/"limit_exceeded" plus a misbehavior charge

Initiator side of Aggregate sync exposed as StartSync/SendSyncNeed/CloseSync/WaitSyncConverged: capability-gated, registers the session before sending sync_begin so fast replies can't race, and reuses the same (peer,txid)-keyed session map as the responder path

Records arriving via sync_records are individually ed25519-verified (sig over pk||kw||ih||t_LE||pow_uvarint) before being handed to the RecordSink; a bad signature charges 20 points and drops only that record; each distinct publisher pubkey in an accepted frame is forwarded once to the PublisherObserver (daemon Bootstrap admission signal); PoW threshold enforcement is explicitly delegated to the sink, not this layer

Gossip intake from peer_announce: a valid non-zero 32-byte `pk` is stored on the peer's PeerState and forwarded to the IndexerSink (engine wires this to dhtindex.Lookup.AddIndexer with label "gossip:<addr>") so DHT keyword lookups fan out to gossip-discovered indexers; `endorsed` pubkey lists are routed to the EndorsementSink (daemon Bootstrap) but only when the endorser announced its own pubkey, skipping self-endorsements and all-zero keys

RecordCache: a thread-safe in-memory record store implementing both RecordSource and RecordSink, keyed by deterministic SHA-256 record ID, with FIFO eviction at a soft cap and age-based pruning; the engine attaches one unconditionally (cap 100,000 records), prunes hourly with a 30-day max age (200 ms/500 ms in regtest)

Surfaced upward: POST /search with swarm:true runs the fan-out and returns asked/responded/rejected + hits JSON; CLI `swartznet search --swarm --swarm-timeout-ms` routes through that API; GET /status reports known/capable peer counts; GET /aggregate reports record-cache kind/size/cap and the hex services mask; POST /capabilities updates the 4-field Capabilities at runtime (clamped); GUI Settings tab calls SetCapabilities

Engine-side hardening of the inbound path: sn_search frames are handled on goroutines off anacrolix's read loop (deadlock + head-of-line-blocking avoidance), payload copied, gated by a 256-slot admission semaphore plus a separate 256-slot reply-writer semaphore; overload drops frames/replies rather than queueing

inputs_outputs: IN: anacrolix/torrent callbacks — PeerConnAdded (advertise + track), ReadExtendedHandshake (capability detection), PeerConnReadExtensionMessage (bencoded sn_search payloads), PeerConnClosed (state eviction) (internal/engine/engine.go:692-802)
IN: bencoded sn_search wire frames msg_type 0-8 from remote peers; OUT: bencoded Result/Reject/PeerAnnounce/sync frames written via PeerConn.WriteExtendedMessage under extension name "sn_search"
IN: local Bleve search results via the LocalSearcher interface (engine adapter over indexer.Index); IN: local signed records via RecordSource.LocalRecords(filter)
OUT: swarmsearch.QueryResponse (TxID, MergedHits, Asked/Responded/Rejected) consumed by httpapi POST /search, which CLI --swarm and web UI/GUI ride on

OUT: gossip observations to IndexerSink.NoteGossipIndexer (→ dhtindex.Lookup), EndorsementSink.NoteEndorsement and PublisherObserver.NotePublisherSeen (→ daemon.Bootstrap admission policy), verified records to RecordSink.Add (→ RecordCache)

CONFIG: Capabilities (ShareLocal/FileHits/ContentHits/Publisher) via POST /capabilities and GUI; RateLimit via SetRateLimit; publisher pubkey via SetPublisherPubkey; regtest flag selects feeler cadence

OUT: structured slog events (swarmsearch.peer_capable, .query.answered, .peer_banned, .sync_session.reaped, etc.); no files or persistent state — every structure in this package is in-memory and lost on restart
data_models: Wire envelope: every sn_search message is one bencoded dict with int discriminator "msg_type": 0=query, 1=result, 2=reject, 3=peer_announce, 4=sync_begin, 5=sync_symbols, 6=sync_need, 7=sync_records, 8=sync_end (internal/swarmsearch/wire.go:13-18, sync_wire.go:19-25); spec mirrors docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md and docs/research/SPEC.md §2

Query {msg_type, txid uint32, q, scope("n"/"f"/"c" union, default "nfc"), limit, lang, min_size, max_size, not_ih[][]byte} (wire.go:36-46); Result {txid, total, partial, hits[]}; Hit {ih 20B, ih2 32B opt, n, s, l, sz, t unix, rank 0-1000, matches[]}; FileMatch {fi, fp, pr, sn, off}; Reject {txid, code 0-4, reason} (wire.go:49-108)
PeerAnnounce {msg_type 3, v int, services uint64, pk 32B opt, endorsed [][]byte max 10×32B} (wire.go:209-226)

ServiceBits uint64 append-only bit table: 0 ShareLocal, 1 ShareSwarm, 2 FileHits, 3 ContentHits, 4 LayerDPublisher, 5 CompanionPublisher, 6 CompanionSubscriber, 7 SnippetHighlight, 8 Regtest, 9 SetReconciliation; unknown bits ignored (services.go:18-77)

Sync frames: SyncBegin {txid, algo "riblt-v1", filter{pubkeys,since,prefix}, element_size must=32, local_count, max_symbols, max_bytes}; SyncSymbols {txid, symbols[{c int32,h uint64,b 32B}], done, index=first symbol position}; SyncNeed {txid, ids[] 32B, empty=done}; SyncRecords {txid, records[{pk 32B,kw,ih 20B,t,pow,sig 64B}], missing[]}; SyncEnd {txid, status converged|limit_exceeded|aborted, decoded, sent, bytes_in, bytes_out, abort_code} (sync_wire.go:60-140)

LocalRecord {Pk[32], Kw string, Ih[20], T int64, Pow uint64, Sig[64]}; RIBLT element ID = SHA-256(pk||kw||ih||t_littleEndian) — duplicated identically in sync_session.go:548-559 and record_cache.go:226-235; signature message = pk||kw||ih||t_LE||uvarint(pow) matching companion.RecordSigMessage (sync_session.go:522-534)

RIBLT: symbol {Count int32 signed, KeyXOR uint64, DataXOR [32]byte}; element key = FNV-1a-64 of the 32-byte ID; membership function contributes(key,idx) = SplitMix64(key + idx*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) % 2^(1+idx%12) == 0 — a 12-step geometric rate cycle (riblt.go:36-90)

In-memory state: Protocol.peers map[addr]PeerState{Supported, RemoteExtID, Version, Services, PublisherPubkey[32]}; PeerBook{tried/new map[addr]BookEntry}; misbehaviorTracker map[addr]{score,bannedUntil}; rateLimiter map[addr]tokenBucket; HitCache LRU map+order slice; RecordCache map[[32]byte]LocalRecord + FIFO order; syncSessions map[peer]map[txid]*SyncSession with phase machine Idle→Begun→SymbolsFlowing→Needed→Fulfilled→Ended

Budgets/constants: DefaultSyncMaxSymbols 2000, DefaultSyncMaxBytes 1 MiB, MaxSymbolsPerMessage 100, MaxRecordsPerMessage 500, MaxNeedIDsPerMessage 1000 (sync_wire.go:34-55); record wire-size proxy 32+len(kw)+20+8+8+64 bytes (sync_session.go:540-542)
external_deps: github.com/anacrolix/torrent/bencode — all wire (de)serialisation; github.com/anacrolix/torrent/peer_protocol — ExtensionName/ExtensionNumber/ExtendedHandshakeMessage types; the package deliberately avoids importing the torrent package proper (LtepAdvertiser interface seam, protocol.go:455-462)

BEP-10 (LTEP extension protocol) — carrier for all sn_search traffic; extension name uses sn_ prefix to avoid libtorrent's lt_ namespace (protocol.go:13-15); mainline compatibility is the load-bearing constraint (doc.go:23-26)

crypto/ed25519 + crypto/sha256 — per-record signature verification and RIBLT element IDs; no import on internal/companion or internal/indexer (shapes intentionally duplicated: sync_wire.go:106-118, handler.go:11-27)
Rateless IBLT set reconciliation — homegrown variant of Yang et al. SIGCOMM 2024, no external library (riblt.go:1-24)

Bitcoin Core design patterns explicitly imported: AddrMan tried/new tables (peerbook.go:8-38), Misbehaving()/DISCOURAGEMENT_THRESHOLD=100 + 24h bans (misbehavior.go:8-84), feeler connections (feeler.go:8-16), services bits (services.go:3-17), BIP-152 compact-relay concept for the hit cache (hitcache.go:7-21)

Specs kept in sync per project rules: docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md (v1 wire + peer_announce), docs/05-integration-design.md §5 (message schemas, §8 wire-compat matrix rows 8.4-B/8.4-C), docs/research/SPEC.md §2 (sync protocol) and §3.3 (endorsement gossip)

nonobvious_rules.rule: Never send an sn_search frame to a peer that did not advertise sn_search back; vanilla peers must only ever see an unknown name in the LTEP m dict (mainline-compat invariant)
ServiceBits numbering is append-only and unknown bits MUST be ignored, never rejected — this is the forward-compat contract for all future features

ShareLocal==1 ("answer only for current-swarm torrents") is deliberately treated the same as ShareLocal==0 and rejected with code 4: no swarm-aware searcher exists, and serving the full index under it would silently violate the operator's intent — fail closed

Announced services in peer_announce = ServicesFromCapabilities(caps) OR (DefaultServices() minus BitLayerDPublisher), with the publisher bit re-added only when caps.Publisher>0 — so DefaultServices bits (including BitShareLocal) are always advertised even if the operator downgraded capabilities via POST /capabilities; only the Publisher bit actually tracks runtime caps

The publisher pubkey is only included in peer_announce when caps.Publisher>0 AND a 32-byte key was set; the engine flips Publisher=1 only when neither --no-dht-publish nor --no-index is set — passive nodes must not gossip themselves as indexers (a past latent bug: pubkey set but caps.Publisher left 0 made gossip silently never fire)
An all-zero 32-byte pubkey in peer_announce is rejected (cannot be a real ed25519 identity; accepting it would poison the indexer fan-out set on every reconnect)
Endorsements only count when the endorsing peer announced its own pubkey in the same frame; self-endorsements and all-zero candidates are skipped — a pubkey-less peer cannot influence admission

Endorsed-list cap of 10 is enforced asymmetrically: encode errors out, decode silently truncates then drops wrong-length entries without failing the frame ("local validation fault, not a protocol violation")

txid match alone never authenticates a response: the sender must be in the query's immutable asked-set (populated before registerPending); results/rejects from unasked peers are charged as spoofing, and malformed results are charged BEFORE the pending lookup so guessing a live txid cannot dodge the charge

A Result is "semantically malformed" iff Total>0 with zero hits OR any hit infohash is not exactly 20 bytes; within one peer's Result, duplicate infohashes are deduplicated so a responder cannot double-count Rank toward the 1000 cap or pad Sources with its own address

Merge semantics a rewrite must preserve: score = sum of ranks capped at 1000; name = first non-empty; size = first non-zero; seeders = max; matches = concatenated union; sort by score desc, tiebreak seeders desc; rejects are delivered to the collector as a Result with MsgType=MsgTypeReject

Fan-out selection: all tried peers + up to FeelerCount(2) new peers; fall back to ALL supported peers when no book, tried-table empty (bootstrap), or the tried set has zero overlap with currently-connected supported peers

PeerBook promotion is on observed behavior only (a valid Result), never on advertised capability; AddNew never demotes an existing tried entry; timeouts AND rejects both count as Failures but v1 never auto-demotes (Failures reserved for v1.1)

Ban state is strictly local and never gossiped (gossiped bans = eclipse-attack vector); bans survive OnPeerClosed (Forget keeps banned entries) but not process restart; expired bans auto-clear with a fresh score budget
Rate-limit token bucket starts FULL (burst 10) on a peer's first query; zero QueriesPerSecond or Burst disables limiting entirely; changing config keeps existing buckets which refill at the new rate
Sync frames are gated on the REMOTE peer having announced BitSetReconciliation (bit 9); old/silent peers get reject code 2 ("unsupported scope" — reused code, not a new one) plus a misbehavior charge

sync_symbols.index MUST equal the receiver's running symbols-in count; any mismatch (dropped/reordered frame) is a hard abort because encoder/decoder positions desync permanently and reconciliation would silently produce wrong differences

Sync budgets negotiate downward only: ApplyBegin takes min(peer's max_symbols/max_bytes, own defaults 2000/1MiB); crossing the symbol budget maps to sync_end "limit_exceeded", other violations to "aborted"; byte accounting uses the semantic record size (32+kw+20+8+8+64), not actual bencoded bytes

Responder sessions: cap 4 per peer where a re-begin on an existing txid replaces rather than counts; sessions older than 2 min are reaped lazily on the next inbound sync frame from that peer (no background goroutine), each emitting sync_end aborted; a zero-record responder answers sync_begin with immediate sync_end converged — valid wire behavior for non-publishers

ApplyRecords is phase-gated: sync_records is only legal after this side sent sync_need (PhaseNeeded) or during a streaming fulfilment (PhaseFulfilled) — records straight after sync_begin are a violation

RIBLT element key MUST be a nonlinear function of the ID bytes (FNV-1a-64): a linear key would make XOR-composed symbols self-consistent for phantom elements and the decoder would hallucinate decodings; the contributes() 12-step modulus cycle {2..4096} is what guarantees pure symbols emerge for any difference size in [2,4096] — both are cross-implementation wire-compat requirements

Record ID derivation (SHA-256 over pk||kw||ih||t_LE) is intentionally duplicated in sync_session.go and record_cache.go and must stay byte-identical to each other and to SPEC §2.4, or the same record exists under two IDs and dedup/reconciliation breaks

Signature verification of synced records happens in swarmsearch (charge 20 on failure), but PoW threshold enforcement is deliberately NOT here — it belongs to the RecordSink; there is intentionally no ScoreInsufficientPoW constant

Feeler probes reuse the real Query path with the magic string "__sn_feeler__" (syntactically valid, unlikely to match) so promotion happens through the identical code path as user queries; remote nodes run a genuine Bleve search for it

Inbound handling must run off anacrolix's read loop (client lock held during the callback): synchronous handling self-deadlocks on reply() and stalls every peer during a Bleve search; the payload must be copied because the decoder buffer is reused

Empty scope means "responder's choice" and is always accepted; unknown scope letters are ignored for forward compatibility; only explicit 'c'/'f' requests against a node lacking those capabilities are rejected (wire-compat matrix row 8.4-B: reject rather than silently downgrade)
OnPeerClosed drops peer state, rate-limit bucket, and PeerBook entries — so PeerBook tried/new status does NOT survive disconnect, meaning promotion is per-connection-lifetime only

readers.purpose: Layer D of SwartzNet's three-layer search: internal/dhtindex publishes and looks up keyword→infohash mappings as BEP-44 mutable items on the mainline DHT (target = SHA1(publisher_pubkey || keyword-salt)), plus BEP-46-style pointer put/get, PPMI (per-publisher pointer) primitives for the v0.5 "Aggregate" redesign, and BEP-51 crawl primitives. internal/companion implements the "companion content index": a publisher periodically snapshots its local Bleve index into a gzipped-JSON single-file torrent, seeds it, and advertises the infohash via a BEP-46 pointer; subscribers resolve the pointer, download the torrent, and import the records into their own Bleve index. The package also carries the newer signed/PoW-protected B-tree ("Aggregate") index-torrent format with a deterministic builder and a defensive prefix-query reader. Everything rides plain BEP-44/46/51/3/9 so vanilla clients see only mainline traffic.

capabilities.behavior: Background DHT keyword publishing: every torrent whose metadata arrives is tokenised (name → up to 8 keywords) and one BEP-44 mutable item per keyword is put to the mainline DHT under SHA1(node_pubkey || keyword); all entries are re-published on an hourly refresh ticker so they outlive the 2h BEP-44 TTL

Keyword extraction with fixed rules: lowercase, unicode letter/digit runs only, ≥3 bytes, English stop-word and file-extension deny lists, dedup preserving first-appearance order, capped at 8 per torrent

Persistent publish manifest at ~/.local/share/swartznet/publisher.json (JSON, atomic tmp+rename) recording per-keyword hits, LastPublished, LastError, PublishCount; a restarted node resumes publishing its full hit lists
Retraction: removing a torrent from the engine scrubs its infohash from every keyword entry in the manifest and persists, so the next refresh tick stops re-announcing it

Layer-D search: POST /search with dht:true (and CLI `swartznet search --dht`, GUI search tab) fans out parallel BEP-44 gets for the query's first token to every known indexer pubkey; hits are merged by infohash, scored (source reputation + multi-source bonus + known-good-Bloom boost), sorted, and returned in the response's dht section

Reputation-aware lookup: indexers below MinIndexerScore are skipped, every responding indexer's HitsReturned is recorded, and per-hit (infohash→indexer) attribution is written to a SourceTracker so a later /flag demotes only the indexers that returned the flagged hash

Known-indexer set management: self pubkey auto-added as "self"; peers gossiped via sn_search peer_announce are added through gossipIndexerSink; bootstrap-admitted anchor publishers are added via AddIndexer; AddIndexerHex validates 64-hex keys

BEP-46 pointer put/get: PutInfohashPointer publishes a signed mutable item {"ih":<20B>,"ts":<unix>} under any ≤64-byte salt, failing closed if the put reached zero DHT nodes; GetInfohashPointer/GetInfohashPointerInfo fetch and validate it (Info variant surfaces the publisher timestamp for staleness policy)

PPMI (publisher-pointer mutable item) primitives: PutPPMI/GetPPMI store/fetch a small bencoded {ih, commit?, topics?, ts, next_pk?} value at the fixed salt SHA256("snet.index") per publisher; Lookup.Query can optionally resolve PPMIs first and fall back to legacy per-keyword gets per publisher

BEP-51 crawl primitives: SampleInfohashes issues one sample_infohashes query (samples, interval hint, num, merged v4/v6 neighbour nodes); CrawlOnce fetches each sample's metainfo, classifies snet.pubkey signatures, and forwards signed publishers (valid AND invalid sig) to a sink for admission policy
CLI `swartznet crawl-probe --addr host:port [--target hex] [--json]`: one-shot BEP-51 probe from a throwaway loopback DHT server, printing samples/interval/num/nodes; no daemon or state needed

Companion publisher worker: on start and hourly thereafter it walks the local Bleve index, writes <CompanionDir>/swartznet-content-index-<pk12>-v1.json.gz plus companion.torrent (atomic writes), seeds the torrent through the engine, and puts a BEP-46 pointer to the new infohash at salt "_sn_content_index"
Manual companion refresh via POST /companion/refresh (and GUI button), throttled to one attempt per MinInterval (1 min default); throttled calls return HTTP 429

Companion subscriber worker: for each followed publisher pubkey, hourly (plus immediately on Follow) it resolves the BEP-46 pointer, downloads the companion torrent through the engine, gunzips/decodes the JSON, and imports every torrent record and content chunk into the local Bleve index, making foreign catalogues searchable via all local search paths

Engine-side companion fetch: FetchCompanionTorrent adds the infohash, waits for metadata, requires exactly one file, rejects declared length >32 MiB before requesting pieces, rejects unsafe file names, polls to completion, and returns the on-disk path

HTTP API companion management: GET /companion (publisher status + per-follow sync results), POST /companion/follow and /companion/unfollow (64-hex pubkey + label) which mutate the worker and atomically rewrite the on-disk follow file
Follow-list persistence: daemon startup loads companion-follows.json (JSON array of {pubkey,label}); missing file is fine, >1 MiB file is rejected wholesale, malformed rows are skipped with a warning

Aggregate B-tree builder: BuildBTree deterministically packs sorted signed records into fixed-piece-size pages (root at piece 0, BFS level layout, signed trailer as last piece) and returns bytes + SHA-256 tree fingerprint for the PPMI commit field

Aggregate B-tree reader: OpenBTree verifies the trailer signature before anything else; Find(prefix) walks root→leaves fetching only overlapping pages, silently dropping records with bad ed25519 signatures or insufficient hashcash PoW; VerifyFingerprint optionally re-derives the full fingerprint
Hashcash PoW: MineRecordPoW finds a nonce giving ≥N leading zero bits of SHA256(sig-message) (refuses N>40); SignAndMineRecord enforces mine-then-sign ordering; readers verify at 1 hash per record

CLI `swartznet aggregate build --out F [--in JSONL] [--key] [--seq] [--piece-size] [--pow-bits]` signs+packs offline; `aggregate inspect FILE` prints trailer metadata; `aggregate find [--verify] FILE PREFIX` runs a prefix query — all without daemon or network
Engine mints per-keyword Aggregate records (currently PoW=0) into the swarmsearch RecordCache on every torrent add so sn_search sync sessions can distribute them
Regtest mode substitutes accelerated time constants for both publishers (5-10s refresh, 100ms min-interval) so scenario tests run in seconds; never for production

Publisher status surfaces in `swartznet status` and GET /status: total keywords, total hits, per-keyword publish counts / last publish / last error; companion status in GET /companion and the GUI Companion tab

Privacy modes: --no-index and DisableDHTPublish suppress the keyword Publisher worker (leech-only Layer D) while keeping lookup, pointer getter, AND the pointer putter alive — companion pointer publication is an explicit user opt-in governed by CompanionDir, not by DisableDHTPublish
cmd/dht-smoke standalone probe performs real BEP-44 keyword put/get round-trips against the live DHT using the same AnacrolixPutter/Getter

Aggregate B-tree page (piece-sized, 16 KiB–4 MiB): 16-byte header = magic "SNAGG\0" + version 0x01 + kind (0x00 root/0x01 interior/0x02 leaf/0xFF trailer) + level + flags + LE16 payload-len + 4 reserved; leaf payload = LE16 count + (uvarint len + bencoded Record)*; interior payload = LE16 count + (uvarint sep-len + sep + LE32 child-piece-index)*, first separator forced empty — internal/companion/btree.go:25-72,252-432

Aggregate Record (bencode): {pk:32B, kw:string ≤64B, ih:20B, t:int64, pow:uvarint, sig:64B}; encoded ≤256B; sort/lookup key = kw||0x00||ih; sig message = Pk||Kw||Ih||LE64(T)||uvarint(Pow) — internal/companion/btree.go:76-196

Aggregate Trailer (last piece, 162-byte payload, little-endian): trailer_version(1)=0x01, pubkey(32), seq(8), created_ts(8), root_piece_index(4)=0 invariant, num_pages(4), num_records(8), min_pow_bits(1), tree_fingerprint(32)=SHA256(concat of canonical sorted record encodings), publisher_sig(64) over all preceding fields — internal/companion/btree.go:59-72,438-564

nonobvious_rules.rule: Keywords whose UTF-8 salt exceeds 64 bytes are DROPPED, never truncated — truncation could alias distinct keywords onto one DHT target

EstimateValueSize stamps a representative non-zero Ts before marshalling because EncodeValue overwrites Ts=0 with a 10-digit timestamp at put time; estimating with Ts=0 would let a near-cap entry pass eviction but fail the live encode, making the keyword permanently unpublishable

Manifest.AddHit evicts the OLDEST hit (slice front) while the encoded value exceeds 1000 bytes; replacing an existing hit can still trigger eviction because the replacement may be larger; multi-shard spill (More/SaltForShard) is deliberately NOT the overflow mechanism in v1
Keyword entries that become empty are deleted from the manifest (RemoveHit/RemoveAllHits) so refreshAll never re-publishes empty values and the manifest cannot grow unboundedly
Every put uses getput's discovered seq+1 via nextSeq, which clamps at MaxInt64 instead of wrapping (graceful-degrade against corruption)

checkPutStats fails closed when a put traversal reached zero DHT nodes even though getput.Put returns nil error in that case — otherwise MarkPublished would advance and the 55-min throttle would suppress retries for an item nobody can fetch; shared by keyword, pointer, and PPMI put paths so the guard cannot drift

MinPutInterval (default 55 min, just under the 1h refresh and the 2h BEP-44 TTL) is a hard per-keyword publish budget: publishOne silently skips if the keyword published more recently, because anacrolix/dht has no put rate cap of its own; 0 disables (tests/regtest)

Tokenize lowercases letters but passes digits through; dedup preserves first-appearance order; the 8-keyword cap applies AFTER filtering; the stop-word list is deliberately short and English-only because 'a missed stopword is one extra DHT put while a dropped legitimate keyword is permanently un-discoverable'

Lookup.Query issues a get for ONLY the first token of the query (multi-keyword AND/OR deferred to a later milestone); an empty indexer set or a reputation-filtered-to-empty set returns an empty response, not an error

Hit score = average source reputation (0.5 when no tracker) + 0.05 per extra source capped at 0.2 + 0.25 flat Bloom boost, clamped [0,1]; sort order is BloomHit desc, Score desc, source count desc, name asc; source label falls back to first 16 hex chars of the pubkey
Publishers whose PPMI resolves are excluded from the legacy per-keyword fan-out (no double-query), but IndexersAsked counts the combined set; PPMI fetch failure silently falls back to legacy
BEP-46 pointer ts is omitempty on the wire; decoders treat absent/zero ts as 'unknown freshness, accept' for back-compat with pre-ts publishers
All remote-value decoders (keyword, pointer, PPMI) reject payloads over the 1000-byte BEP-44 cap BEFORE unmarshalling, because a malicious node can return up to ~64 KiB regardless of the storage cap

Crawler classification forwards pubkeys with INVALID signatures to the sink (sigValid=false) so reputation/admission can demote them; unsigned torrents are silently skipped (the vast majority); only malformed bencode is an error

Two salt-derivation conventions coexist: the companion pointer uses the literal ASCII salt "_sn_content_index" while PPMI uses SHA256("snet.index") — the PPMI double-hash is deliberate so passive DHT observers can't classify publishers by salt; the pointer salt predates that decision

Companion file basename embeds the first 12 hex chars of the publisher pubkey; empty pubkey falls back to the legacy generic name so old/test paths still work; subscribers locate the payload by returned path, not by name
The companion infohash intentionally changes on every refresh because Encode embeds a fresh GeneratedAt; the publisher overwrites both files in place and treats CompanionDir as exclusive

An empty local index is recorded as a refresh FAILURE ('nothing to publish'); lastAttempt advances on any outcome (throttles RefreshNow) but lastRefresh advances ONLY on success — it answers 'is my pointer still alive (<2h BEP-44 TTL)?' and must never be advanced by a failure
Companion seeding errors from AddTorrentMetaInfo are swallowed (debug log only) because re-adding the same infohash is benign — anacrolix dedupes internally

FetchCompanionTorrent fail-closes BEFORE requesting pieces: exactly 1 file, declared length ≤32 MiB (info dict is attacker-controlled via the pointer), plain filename only (rejects '', '.', '..', '/' and '\\'); ctx cancel aborts the wait but leaves the torrent in the engine for retry reuse
Decode enforces a 1 GiB decompressed-JSON cap, requires exact Format string and Version==1; Encode force-overwrites Format/Version and normalises nil Torrents to [] so the wire form is stable

Subscriber ingest: infohash lowercased and must be exactly 40 chars else the record is skipped; FileCount is the count of non-empty file paths, not the publisher's claimed count; empty-text chunks are skipped but ChunkIndex still reflects their position; the first hard index error aborts the whole ingest
Unfollow race handling: a sync result arriving for a publisher unfollowed mid-sync is dropped (membership re-checked under the lock) so results never resurrect for unfollowed keys

Interior-page separator semantics: each child's stored separator is the MIN KEY of that child's own subtree (not a between-children separator); the first child's separator is forced empty (= -∞) at encode time; a child's upper bound is the NEXT child's separator — a rewrite using classic B-tree separators would mis-route queries

B-tree reader trust model: only the trailer (and per-record sigs) are signed; interior pages are attacker-controlled, so the walk uses a shared visited-set failing closed on any revisit (defeats Fibonacci fan-in), requires child indices strictly increasing, strictly greater than the parent, and below the trailer piece, and requires ≥3 pages, root at piece 0, and trailer NumPages == actual piece count

Find silently drops records failing signature or PoW verification instead of erroring the query — nothing a subscriber can do about individual bad records once the trailer verified; PoW is only enforced when trailer MinPoWBits>0 (0 = v1.0 back-compat/test mode) and BuildBTree does NOT default MinPoWBits so unit tests don't mine

BuildBTree output is deterministic: records defensively copied then sorted by RecordKey; fingerprint = SHA256 over the concatenated canonical record encodings in sorted order, independent of piece size, so two publishers with identical records get identical PPMI commits; a single-leaf tree still gets a distinct one-child root page (root kind ≠ leaf kind per spec)

PoW mine-then-sign ordering is mandatory (RecordSigMessage includes the Pow nonce); MineRecordPoW refuses bits>40 as cost-prohibitive; VerifyFingerprint bails as soon as record count exceeds the trailer claim so a crafted file can't force unbounded hashing

DisableDHTPublish / NoIndex suppress the keyword Publisher worker but keep the pointer putter alive (companion publication is its own opt-in via CompanionDir) and keep the lookup path; the sn_search Publisher capability bit is only set when actually publishing so passive nodes never gossip themselves as indexers
`aggregate build --key <path>` never auto-generates an identity for an explicit path (a typo would silently sever publisher reputation); only the empty default path may LoadOrCreate

PieceSize must be in [16384, 4 MiB]; MaxKeywordBytes=64; MaxRecordBytes=256; page payload lengths are uint16; MinPoWBitsDefault=20; companion piece length 256 KiB; publisher queue size 64, dropped-on-full

broken_or_unfinished.issue: Multi-shard spill (KeywordValue.More + SaltForShard) is wire-reserved scaffolding: the publisher never sets More or writes shard 1+, and Lookup never follows it — oversize handled only by oldest-hit eviction
Key rotation (KeywordValue.NextPubKey, PPMIValue.NextPk) ships on the wire but is never populated; comments defer rotation logic to v1.1

readers.purpose: internal/httpapi is the loopback-only, unauthenticated HTTP control plane for a running SwartzNet daemon plus the embedded browser web UI served from the same port (default localhost:7654). It is the single seam where the three search layers (L=local Bleve, S=sn_search peer-wire, D=BEP-44 DHT) are reconciled into one combined JSON response, and it is the IPC surface the CLI subcommands (search/status/flag/confirm/files/index) use to talk to a long-running `swartznet add` daemon. It holds zero engine/companion imports — every collaborator is a locally-declared narrow interface or a mirrored struct, wired in by internal/daemon.

capabilities.behavior: POST /search: body {q, limit, swarm, dht, swarm_timeout_ms, dht_timeout_ms, signed_by, highlight}. Always runs Layer L (if index wired); optionally fans out to Layer S (swarm:true) and Layer D (dht:true). Returns {local:{total,hits[]}, swarm?:{asked,responded,rejected,hits[],error?}, dht?:{indexers_asked,indexers_responded,hits[],error?}}. Local failure = whole-request 500; swarm/DHT failures are reported inline as an error string with HTTP 200. signed_by (64-hex pubkey) filters Layer L only. highlight:true adds Bleve <mark>-wrapped fragments per hit.

Search-request hygiene: q required (400 if empty), q capped at 1024 bytes (400 above), limit<=0 defaults to 50, limit capped at 500. Per-layer timeouts: swarm default 2s, DHT default 5s, both clamped to max 30s; handler context deadline is timeout+500ms grace.

GET /healthz: {ok:true, version} where version is a package-global atomic string set via SetHealthzVersion (daemon sets it from opts.Version at startup). Web UI polls it every 5s to drive the connected/offline badge.

GET /status: aggregated daemon snapshot — local{indexed,doc_count}, swarm{known_peers,capable_peers}, publisher{pubkey?,total_keywords,total_hits,keywords[] with keyword/hits_count/last_published(RFC3339 UTC, omitted when zero)/publish_count/last_error}, dht{good_nodes,nodes} (omitted entirely when no DHTStats probe, i.e. DHT disabled), bloom{bit_size,hash_functions,population_bits,estimated_items}, reputation{known_indexers, top_indexers truncated to 10}.
POST /confirm {infohash}: adds the raw 20-byte infohash to the known-good Bloom filter; 400 unless exactly 40 hex chars, 503 if no bloom wired. Returns {ok,infohash}.

POST /flag {infohash}: demotes reputation of ONLY the indexer pubkeys the SourceTracker attributed to that infohash (populated by prior Layer-D lookups), then forgets the attribution. No attribution → demotes nobody (fail closed; response indexers_flagged omitted/0 but ok:true). Logs attribution="targeted"|"none". 503 if no tracker.
POST /torrent {uri}: adds a magnet URI via the TorrentAdder interface; returns {ok,infohash} immediately (metadata fetch async). 503 if no adder, 400 on add error.

GET/POST /capabilities: read/write the sn_search sharing levels. Body/response {share_local,file_hits,content_hits,publisher}. POST clamps share_local to 0..2 and the other three to 0..1, then replaces the whole Capabilities struct; response echoes the post-clamp values.

GET /torrents: {torrents:[TorrentSnapshot]} — per-torrent infohash, name, size, bytes_completed/missing, progress, files, peer counts (active/half_open/pending/total), seeders, paused, status string, indexing flag, indexed_files/index_extracted (omitempty), queued, download_rate/upload_rate, signed_by/trusted_publisher (omitempty). Web UI Downloads tab polls this every 2s while visible; Status tab derives a Torrents card from it.

Torrent control: POST /torrents/{ih}/pause, POST /torrents/{ih}/resume (both idempotent), DELETE /torrents/{ih} (removes torrent, leaves on-disk files). All validate 40-hex path infohash (400), 503 when controller absent, engine error → 400, success → {ok,infohash,action}.

POST /torrents/{ih}/indexing {enabled:bool}: flips the per-torrent indexing toggle; returns {ok,infohash,enabled}. Also exposed to users via CLI `swartznet index` and the web UI's per-torrent '🔍 index: on/off' button.

GET /torrents/{ih}/files: per-file list {index,path,display_path,length,bytes_completed,progress,priority}; POST /torrents/{ih}/files/{index}/priority {priority:"none"|"normal"|"high"}: sets one file's download priority. index parsed with strconv.Atoi (rejects trailing garbage, negatives → 400). Backs CLI `swartznet files` and the web UI files modal with Select All / Deselect All (serial per-file POST loop).

GET/POST /config/rate-limit {upload_bps,download_bps} and GET/POST /config/queue {max_active_downloads}: read/write engine rate limits and download-queue cap. Zero means unlimited; POST always sets both rate fields (no leave-unchanged semantics) and replies with the fresh GET body. Web UI Settings tab converts KiB/s×1024.

GET /aggregate: v0.5 Aggregate-track introspection — {ppmi_enabled, known_indexers, indexers[{pk,label}], record_source_kind("cache"|"custom"|""), record_cache_size, record_cache_max, services (16 lowercase hex chars, big-endian, no 0x), bootstrap?{anchors,admitted,pending}}. bootstrap omitted when no BootstrapProbe wired.

Companion endpoints: GET /companion returns {publisher:{last_refresh,last_infohash,last_error?,published_count,pubkey_hex?}, subscriber:[{pubkey_hex,label?,last_sync_at?,last_error?,torrents_imported,content_imported,generated_at?,pointer_infohash?}]}; POST /companion/refresh triggers an out-of-band publish (any error mapped to HTTP 429 so the GUI can show the MinInterval throttle message); POST /companion/follow {pubkey:64-hex,label?} and POST /companion/unfollow {pubkey} mutate the persisted follow list (bad pubkey → 400, controller error → 500). All 503 when no companion controller.

GET /index/stats: {dir_bytes,doc_count,torrent_count,content_count,corpus_text_bytes,inflation_ratio} — the v1.0.0 index-size-per-corpus measurement. 503 when index absent. Handler comment warns it scans every content doc, so poll at human cadence only.

Embedded web UI: GET /{$} serves index.html and GET /static/ serves css/js from a go:embed FS compiled into the binary; API routes are registered first so they win over the catch-all. If the embed sub-FS fails, the daemon logs a warning and runs API-only. Six tabs: Search, Add torrent, Downloads, Companion, Status, Sharing.

Web UI Search tab: swarm/DHT checkboxes, limit input (UI max 100), optional publisher-pubkey filter, always sends highlight:true; renders three labelled sections (Local Layer L / Swarm Layer S / DHT Layer D) with a header line showing per-layer asked/responded/rejected counts and inline layer errors; every hit gets 👍 confirm and 🚫 flag buttons (flag asks for confirm()); clicking a hit's signed-by badge re-runs the search filtered to that publisher; highlight fragments (max 2) injected via innerHTML relying on Bleve pre-escaping.
Web UI keyboard shortcut: '/' or Ctrl/Cmd+K switches to the Search tab and focuses+selects the query input, ignored while typing in another input.

Web UI Downloads tab: progress bar, secondary indexing progress bar (indexed_files/files with 'N with text' extractor count) shown only when indexing is on and file count known, ↓/↑ rates, signed badge (★ for trusted publisher, ✓ otherwise), pause/resume/remove (remove confirms and notes files stay on disk), files modal, per-torrent index toggle. Immediate re-poll after any control action.

Web UI Status tab polls /status + /index/stats + /torrents + /aggregate every 4s while visible; the three auxiliary fetches use .catch(()=>null) so older daemons missing an endpoint degrade to fewer cards (guarded by web/aggregate_card_test.go). DHT card renders only when the response has a dht block; publisher pubkey row only when publisher.pubkey set; publisher keyword table shows per-keyword state ('ok' or 'ERR: …').

CSRF/DNS-rebinding guard on every non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request: Host header must be loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, or literal 'localhost', case-insensitive, port and IPv6 brackets stripped); if an Origin header is present its host must be loopback, else if a Referer is present its host must be loopback (Origin checked first, Referer only when Origin absent). Fails closed with 403. curl/CLI (no Origin/Referer, loopback Host) unaffected; reads are always exempt.
Every request body is capped at 1 MiB via http.MaxBytesReader; overflow surfaces as a JSON decode failure (400). Middleware order: body cap wraps the CSRF guard which wraps the mux.

Server lifecycle: New/NewWithOptions default addr to localhost:7654 and logger to slog.Default; Start binds synchronously (so Addr() works with :0) then serves in a goroutine; a non-loopback bind logs a loud 'API is UNAUTHENTICATED' warning but still binds (operators may front their own auth); Stop is idempotent and a Server is reusable across Start/Stop cycles (fresh http.Server each Start). Timeouts: ReadHeader 2s, Read 5s, Write 30s, Idle 60s, MaxHeaderBytes 256 KiB.

All handlers whose collaborator is nil return 503 'X not configured' — every collaborator in Options is optional, so a partially-wired daemon (e.g. --no-index, --no-dht) serves a coherent degraded API.

inputs_outputs: In: TCP listener on Options addr (default localhost:7654; 'localhost:0' supported; empty --api-addr disables the whole API at the daemon level) — internal/httpapi/server.go:241,288; docs/08-operations.md:113

In: JSON request bodies (≤1 MiB) from three client kinds: CLI subcommands search/status/flag/confirm/files/index acting as HTTP clients (cmd/swartznet/cmd_search.go:112, cmd_status.go:36, cmd_flag.go:23-34, cmd_files.go:57,132, cmd_index.go:54), the embedded browser UI, and arbitrary local tools (curl)

In: live collaborator objects injected by daemon.New — indexer.Index, swarmsearch.Protocol, dhtindex.Publisher/Lookup, reputation BloomFilter/Tracker/SourceTracker, engine (TorrentAdder+TorrentController adapters), companion adapter, DHTStats probe, BootstrapProbe (internal/daemon/daemon.go:230-255)
Out: JSON responses (Content-Type: application/json) and the embedded HTML/CSS/JS web UI

Out: state mutations forwarded to other subsystems: bloom.Add, tracker.RecordFlagged, sources.Forget, engine add/pause/resume/remove/indexing/priority/rate-limit/queue, swarm.SetCapabilities, companion Follow/Unfollow (persists follow list to disk) / RefreshNow

Out: slog events — httpapi.listening, httpapi.non_loopback_bind warning, httpapi.serve_err, httpapi.local_err, httpapi.confirm, httpapi.flag (with attribution targeted|none), httpapi.add_torrent, httpapi.torrent_control, httpapi.set_capabilities, httpapi.companion_follow/unfollow, httpapi.web_assets_unavailable
No files are read or written by this package at runtime; the web assets are compiled in via go:embed (web/embed.go:17)
data_models: SearchRequest/SearchResponse: the layer-reconciliation seam. Response is {local: always-present LocalResult with hits:[] never null, swarm: *SwarmResult present only when requested AND swarm wired, dht: *DHTResult likewise}. Each layer keeps its own hit shape (LocalHit with doc_type/infohash/name/size_bytes/file_index/file_path/mime/extractor/score/signed_by/fragments; SwarmHit with infohash/name/size/seeders/score/sources; DHTHit with infohash/name/seeders/size/files/sources) — no merged cross-layer hit type, per the documented architecture rule. internal/httpapi/server.go:396-493; docs/05-integration-design.md:117
StatusResponse: local/swarm/publisher always present; dht, bloom, reputation are omitempty pointers so absent subsystems disappear from the JSON rather than rendering zeros. server.go:615-688

TorrentSnapshot and TorrentFile: hand-mirrored copies of engine.TorrentSnapshot/engine.FileSnapshot re-declared here (with JSON tags) so httpapi never imports internal/engine; the engine returns these httpapi types directly. server.go:68-106

CompanionPublisherStatus / CompanionFollowStatus: mirror internal/companion types via an adapter for the same no-import reason; time.Time fields serialize as RFC3339 and the zero value '0001-01-01T00:00:00Z' is the web UI's 'never' sentinel. companion.go:41-64; web/static/app.js:992-994,1044
AggregateStatusResponse: services field is a fixed-width 16-char lowercase hex rendering of the 64-bit ServiceBits (big-endian, no 0x prefix — formatServicesHex). aggregate.go:25-100,150-156
IndexStats: one-for-one mirror of indexer.Stats. server.go:690-700
Mutation envelopes: {ok:true, infohash, ...} shape shared by confirm/flag/add/control/indexing/priority responses; FlagResponse.indexers_flagged omitempty. server.go:807-816,1190-1194
CapabilitiesBody doubles as both GET response and POST request; field names deliberately match swarmsearch.Capabilities. server.go:929-937
Embedded web assets: index.html + static/style.css + static/app.js bundled via //go:embed at build time. web/embed.go:17-18
healthz version: package-level atomic.Pointer[string] — global across every Server instance in the process, not per-server state. server.go:1235-1253
external_deps: Go stdlib net/http only — no router/framework; relies on Go 1.22+ ServeMux method+wildcard patterns ('POST /torrents/{infohash}/pause', 'GET /{$}') and r.PathValue (server.go:307-343,998)
go:embed for the web UI bundle (web/embed.go)
internal/indexer (Layer L, Bleve-backed) via *indexer.Index — Search/DocCount/Stats
internal/swarmsearch (Layer S, sn_search BEP-10 LTEP extension) via *swarmsearch.Protocol — Query/KnownPeers/CapablePeerCount/Capabilities/SetCapabilities/RecordSource; DefaultServices for /aggregate
internal/dhtindex (Layer D, BEP-44 mutable items) via *dhtindex.Publisher (Status) and *dhtindex.Lookup (Query, Indexers, PPMIGetter)
internal/reputation — BloomFilter (known-good, /confirm), Tracker (Bayesian reputation, /flag + /status), SourceTracker (per-hit indexer attribution for targeted flagging)
internal/companion (BEP-46 mutable-pointer companion index) reached only through the CompanionController interface — no direct import

BitTorrent protocol context surfaced to users: BEP-10 (capabilities/sharing levels), BEP-44 (DHT publisher status), BEP-46 (companion pointer), BEP-52 file paths mentioned in the Sharing tab copy (web/index.html:177)
Security model: loopback bind + OS trust, no auth token; browser attacks handled by the in-package CSRF/DNS-rebinding guard rather than any external mechanism (csrf.go:10-38)

nonobvious_rules.rule: Layer failure asymmetry: a Layer-L (local Bleve) error fails the whole POST /search with 500, but Layer-S and Layer-D errors are swallowed into a 200 response as swarm.error / dht.error strings. A rewrite that makes all three uniform breaks both the CLI and the web UI header rendering.

The swarm/dht response sections appear ONLY when the request asked for that layer AND the collaborator is wired; asking for swarm on a swarm-less daemon silently omits the section rather than erroring. resp.local.hits is initialized to an empty slice so it serializes as [] never null.

Per-layer timeout budget: client ms value clamped to (0, 30s], defaults 2s (swarm) / 5s (DHT), and the handler context gets timeout+500ms — the extra 500ms grace lets the fan-out layer return partial results before the HTTP context dies. 30s deliberately mirrors the server WriteTimeout.

Magic limits that clients depend on: search limit default 50 / cap 500; query cap 1024 bytes; body cap 1 MiB; reputation top_indexers truncated to 10; header cap 256 KiB. The web UI separately caps its limit input at 100.

/flag is fail-closed by design (M9): it demotes only SourceTracker-attributed indexers and demotes NOBODY when attribution is missing, because the old 'penalize every known indexer' fallback let an attacker crater the whole reputation table by seeding one unattributed spam hit. It also Forget()s the attribution after flagging. ok:true is returned even when zero indexers were flagged.

CSRF guard checks Origin first and consults Referer only when Origin is absent; the literal hostname 'localhost' is trusted but any other DNS name is rejected even if it resolves to 127.0.0.1 (that is the DNS-rebinding defense). GET/HEAD/OPTIONS are always exempt.
Middleware nesting is withMaxBodyBytes(withCSRFGuard(mux)) so a CSRF-rejected request never reads its body — a rewrite that swaps the order changes DoS characteristics.

POST /capabilities and POST /config/* have replace semantics, not merge: SetCapabilities overwrites the entire struct and POST /config/rate-limit always writes both fields, with zero meaning 'unlimited' rather than 'unchanged' (the code comment even contradicts itself about this). Clamp ranges: share_local 0..2, file_hits/content_hits/publisher 0..1.

Every /torrents/{infohash} route validates exactly-40-lowercase-hex-decodable path segment before touching the engine (400 otherwise); the file index uses strconv.Atoi specifically because Sscanf would silently accept '3abc'.

Companion refresh maps ANY RefreshNow error to HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) — the expected error is the publisher's MinInterval throttle and the GUI shows the message verbatim; follow/unfollow errors map to 500, pubkey parse errors to 400 (must be exactly 64 hex chars, checked by length before hex-decode).

API routes are registered on the mux before the static-file catch-all so they take precedence; the root handler pattern 'GET /{$}' matches only the exact root, so unknown paths 404 out of the file server instead of falling back to index.html (no SPA-style fallback).

Web UI trusts Bleve highlighter output: fragments and highlighted names are injected via innerHTML on the explicit assumption that Bleve's HTML highlighter pre-escapes text and only adds <mark> tags. A rewrite of either side that drops the escaping guarantee becomes an XSS.

Web UI back-compat contract: /index/stats, /torrents and /aggregate fetches in the Status tab must tolerate 404 from older daemons via .catch(()=>null) — enforced by a dedicated test that greps the embedded JS source for the literal pattern.

Poll cadences are part of the UX contract: health 5s always, downloads 2s and status 4s only while their tab is visible (re-armed via setTimeout, cancelled when hidden); control actions trigger an immediate refresh.

The web UI derives its Torrents status card from torrent.status string values 'downloading'/'seeding'/'queued'/'paused' and defaults the pill to 'metadata' — the engine's status vocabulary is an implicit cross-layer enum the API never validates.

Server binds non-loopback addresses if asked (operators may add their own auth) but emits a loud one-time warning; the guard against browsers is CSRF-only, the guard against the network is bind-address-only.
The healthz version string is process-global (package atomic), so two Server instances in one process always report the same version; tests and daemon both write it via SetHealthzVersion.

hex publisher-status timestamps: PublisherKeywordEntry.last_published is RFC3339 in UTC and omitted (not zero-rendered) when the time is zero; companion timestamps instead serialize Go zero time and the UI string-compares against '0001-01-01T00:00:00Z' — two different 'never' conventions in one API.

readers.purpose: Gives each SwartzNet node a single persistent ed25519 keypair (the "publisher identity") and builds three local trust mechanisms on it: (1) optional infohash-preserving .torrent signing via snet.pubkey/snet.sig metainfo fields, (2) a user-managed publisher allowlist (trust list) that auto-confirms signed torrents, and (3) a spam-resistance layer combining a per-indexer Bayesian reputation tracker, a known-good-infohash Bloom filter, and per-hit source attribution used to rank/filter Layer-D DHT lookup results and to target flag/confirm feedback.

capabilities.behavior: First run generates an ed25519 keypair and persists it as raw 64 bytes at identity.key (mode 0600, parent dir 0700); later runs load it and refuse to proceed (never silently regenerate) if the file exists but has wrong permissions, wrong size, is a directory, or has a public half that doesn't match its seed.

The identity powers everything publisher-shaped: BEP-44 DHT puts are signed with it, the node registers its own pubkey as indexer 'self', the sn_search PeerAnnounce pk field carries it, and aggregate LocalRecords are minted/signed with it. Losing it severs publisher reputation. Identity load failure is non-fatal: node still downloads/searches locally, just cannot publish.

`swartznet create --sign [--identity <path>]` signs the created .torrent and prints 'Signing with identity <hex>'. Explicit --identity is load-only (missing file = hard error, to avoid orphaning the torrent under a fresh untrusted key); only the default XDG path may auto-create. `--identity` without `--sign` is a usage error. Same load-only rule applies to `swartznet aggregate build --key`.

Signing adds two optional top-level bencode fields, snet.pubkey (32 B) and snet.sig (64 B), to the metainfo dict; the payload signed is "SN-TORRENT-V1|" || SHA1(info dict). The info dict bytes are untouched so the infohash is preserved and vanilla clients (which ignore unknown top-level keys) are unaffected. Re-signing replaces existing snet fields. SignFile writes atomically (tmp + rename, 0644). Formal spec in docs/11-signing-protocol.md.

When a .torrent file is added (AddTorrentFile path), the signature is verified: valid → handle records SignedBy (64-char hex) and logs engine.torrent_signature_verified; invalid → warning logged but the torrent is still added, just unsigned; absent → silent (ErrNotSigned is normal). SignedBy is persisted in the session store and restored across restarts without re-verification.

SignedBy is indexed in Bleve as lowercase keyword field 'signed_by' (schema v0.7+); `swartznet search --signed-by <hex>` filters local results by signer, routed through the daemon API, and a SignedBy-only query (empty text query) is valid.

`swartznet trust list|add|remove` (aliases ls/rm; --file override; --json on list) manages the publisher allowlist entirely offline against trust.json — no daemon round-trip needed. add is idempotent and relabels; remove is idempotent; list prints a PUBKEY/LABEL table or '(no trusted publishers yet ...)'.

Trusted-publisher effect: a torrent signed by a trust-listed pubkey is auto-confirmed into the known-good Bloom filter the moment metadata arrives (no waiting for download completion), logged as engine.bloom.trusted_publisher_confirmed.

TorrentSnapshot carries SignedBy and TrustedPublisher (JSON signed_by / trusted_publisher in GET /torrents); GUI Downloads tab shows a trusted badge, a right-click 'Trust this publisher' / 'Revoke trust for this publisher' action pair, and a signature-details dialog (full pubkey, trust status, label, signed infohash).

Per-indexer reputation: every Layer-D query records HitsReturned for each responding indexer; indexers whose derived score falls below configurable MinIndexerScore (config default 0 = disabled) are skipped before the DHT fan-out; hit ranking folds in average source reputation, multi-source bonus, and Bloom membership.

Known-good Bloom filter: a torrent's infohash is auto-added when its download completes (background goroutine with 24h cap, cancelled on remove/shutdown); Bloom membership marks LookupHit.BloomHit, adds +0.25 score, and sorts Bloom hits above all others.

POST /confirm adds the 40-hex infohash to the Bloom filter (503 if no filter configured). POST /flag demotes (RecordFlagged) only the indexer pubkeys that the SourceTracker attributes to that infohash, then forgets the attribution; if no attribution exists it fails closed and demotes nobody. Response {ok, infohash, indexers_flagged}.

`swartznet flag <infohash>` / `swartznet confirm <infohash>` POST to the running daemon (default localhost:7654, --api-addr override, 5s timeout), validate 40-hex input, and print 'flagged:'/'confirmed:' on success.

GUI search hit cards (local + swarm) offer Confirm/Flag buttons and a right-click menu (copy infohash, copy publisher pubkey when signed, confirm, flag). GUI Confirm adds to the Bloom filter AND RecordConfirmed's attributed source indexers; GUI Flag demotes attributed sources and shows a 'no attribution — no reputations changed' dialog otherwise. Signed hits show '✓ signed by <first 8 hex>'.
SourceTracker (in-memory LRU, default 10,000 infohashes) is populated by Lookup.Query with which indexer pubkeys returned each hit, so flag/confirm target exactly the responsible indexers.

Curated seed list: at engine startup seeds.json ({"version":1,"seeds":[...]}) is imported via MarkSeeded, giving each pubkey a +0.45 score bonus decaying with a 90-day half-life (cold-start bootstrap); missing file is fine, bad entries are skipped with per-entry errors, version != 1 is rejected wholesale.

Daemon cold-start Bootstrap marks admitted anchor pubkeys as seeded on the tracker (same decaying bonus), exempts anchors from the MaxTrackedPublishers cap (default 100), and uses reputation thresholds for admission decisions (0.3 for crawl candidates, 0.5 for 'strong endorsers', default endorsement threshold 3).

Status surfaces: GET /status includes BloomStatus (bit_size, hash_functions, population_bits, estimated_items) and ReputationStat (known_indexers + top-10 indexer table with score and R/C/F counters); GUI Status tab shows truncated publisher pubkey, Bloom estimated items, and a reputation table (score to 3 decimals, hits as returned/confirmed/flagged).

Persistence lifecycle: trust.json is rewritten atomically on every Add/Remove; the Bloom filter and reputation tracker are saved atomically only at engine Close. Empty-path stores/trackers/filters are valid in-memory-only instances whose Save is a no-op.

nonobvious_rules.rule: Identity file permissions must be EXACTLY 0600 — anything else, including the stricter 0400, is rejected as 'compromised' with an instruction to chmod or delete. Comparison is against the literal perm bits, deliberately ignoring umask effects.

On load, the public half (bytes [32:64]) is re-derived from the 32-byte seed and compared; independent corruption of the trailing bytes fails loud at load time instead of surfacing later as 'signature does not verify'.

Auto-creation of a missing identity is allowed ONLY at the default XDG path; any explicitly user-supplied key path is load-only and fails closed, because signing under a freshly minted key would silently orphan publisher reputation.
Signature payload is "SN-TORRENT-V1|" (with trailing pipe) prepended to the raw 20-byte infohash as a domain separator; Sign and Verify must build it byte-identically (shared signingPayload helper).

SignBytes decodes the metainfo as map[string]bencode.Bytes so the info dict bytes pass through untouched (infohash preserved); the re-encode canonicalizes top-level key order but never alters info. A rewrite that round-trips info through a typed struct would change the infohash and break everything.

Verification error taxonomy: if EITHER snet field is missing → ErrNotSigned (a normal outcome, not an error condition); wrong pubkey/sig lengths → plain error (neither sentinel); crypto verify failure → ErrBadSignature but the returned Signature struct is still fully populated (pubkey/sig/infohash).

A .torrent with a BAD signature is still added and downloads normally — the engine only logs a warning and leaves SignedBy empty. Signature verification only happens on the file-add path; magnet/infohash adds can never have a SignedBy (snet fields are top-level, not inside the BEP-9-exchanged info dict).

Trust pubkeys are normalized to lowercase at every boundary (load, Add, Remove, IsTrusted, Label); entries with invalid hex are silently dropped on load rather than erroring; Add on an existing key overwrites the label; List/save order is sorted by pubkey.

Reputation score: neutral 0.5 for zero-counter records; otherwise (max(0, confirmed−flagged)/max(1,returned)) Bayesian-smoothed toward 0.5 with prior weight 5; then + seed bonus 0.45·2^(−age/90d) if SeededAt set (negative age clamped to 0); final clamp [0,1]. Constants 0.5/5.0/0.45/90d are load-bearing for ranking compat.
Tracker.Threshold treats cutoff ≤ 0 or NaN as 'always passes' — MinIndexerScore=0 (the default) disables filtering entirely. Snapshot ordering is score-desc with pubkey-asc tiebreak.
Re-importing an already-seeded pubkey (seed list reload or anchor re-admit) refreshes SeededAt to now, restarting the bonus decay ('maintainers re-bless the list').

Bloom index derivation is frozen by the on-disk format: h1 = FNV-64a(input); h2 = the SAME hash state continued with one extra 0xff byte; h2 |= 1 (forced odd stride, Kirsch-Mitzenmacher); index_i = (h1 + i·h2) mod m. A rewrite must reproduce this exactly or existing known-good.bloom files return garbage membership.

Bloom defaults: 1,000,000 expected items at 0.01 FP rate (≈9.6M bits ≈1.2MB); m/k from standard formulas with ceil and floor-at-1. Loader rejects m==0, k==0, and any bitsLen ≠ (m+63)/64 (both undersized AND oversized) to fail closed on corrupt files.

Flagging fails closed: with no SourceTracker attribution for the infohash, NO reputations are demoted (both HTTP and GUI). The earlier M5d fallback of demoting every known indexer was deliberately removed as attacker-weaponizable (seed unattributed spam → one flag craters the whole table).
After a successful flag the SourceTracker entry is Forgotten so repeated flags cannot double-dock the same indexers; Sources() lookups also refresh the LRU position of the queried infohash.

Layer-D hit ranking: score = mean(source reputations, 0.5 if no tracker) + 0.05 per extra source capped at +0.2 + 0.25 if BloomHit, clamped [0,1]; final sort is BloomHit first, then score desc, then source count desc, then name asc.

Trusted-publisher auto-confirm fires at metadata-arrival (autoIndex) time, not download completion — the trust relationship substitutes for the completion signal. Plain (untrusted) torrents only reach the Bloom filter via completion or explicit confirm.
Bloom filter and reputation tracker are persisted ONLY at engine Close (trust.json, by contrast, is saved on every mutation). A crash loses the session's confirmations/flags/auto-confirms.

Bootstrap admission constants: anchors are MarkSeeded and exempt from the MaxTrackedPublishers cap (default 100); crawl candidates pass bloomPolicy at tracker score ≥ 0.3; endorsers count as 'strong' at score ≥ 0.5; default endorsement threshold 3. Since unknown pubkeys score 0.5, an unknown crawl candidate passes the 0.3 gate whenever a bloom filter + tracker are attached.
RecordReturned ignores n ≤ 0 and indexers whose fetch errored are not counted at all — reputation only accrues on responses that actually carried hits, so silent non-responders neither gain nor lose.

CLI split: `swartznet trust *` operates directly on trust.json offline (no daemon needed); `swartznet flag`/`confirm` require a running daemon and go through localhost HTTP (default localhost:7654). The flag CLI prints correct past tense ('flagged' not 'flaged') via a special case.
