readers.purpose: These documents are the normative design and spec-of-record for SwartzNet's wire behavior: the layered architecture (Layer L local Bleve / Layer S sn_search peer-wire / Layer D BEP-44 DHT keyword index), three standalone BEP-style drafts (sn_search LTEP extension, BEP-44 keyword-index convention, snet.pubkey/snet.sig torrent signing), plus README (user contract) and CHANGELOG (behavioral history). The load-bearing constraint they all encode: strict mainline BitTorrent compatibility — no new reserved bit, no new DHT verb, no new UDP port; a vanilla client must observe only BEP-3/5/9/10/44 traffic.

capabilities.behavior: Layer S peer-wire search: two peers that both advertise `sn_search` in their BEP-10 LTEP `m` dict can exchange free-text queries (msg_type 0), ranked results with per-file/content matches (msg_type 1), rejects with 5 defined codes (msg_type 2), and per-direction capability announcements (msg_type 3) over their existing BT TCP connection; peers not advertising the extension never receive a single sn_search frame

Capability negotiation via a 64-bit `services` bitfield in peer_announce (bits 0-9 defined: ShareLocal, ShareSwarm, FileHits, ContentHits, LayerDPublisher, CompanionPublisher, CompanionSubscriber, SnippetHighlight, Regtest, SetReconciliation); unknown bits MUST be ignored never rejected; absence of peer_announce = services 0 and the peer is still answered

Aggregate set-reconciliation session (msg_types 4-8: sync_begin/symbols/need/records/end) using Rateless IBLT, gated on services bit 9; peers without the bit receive reject code 2 for sync frames; per-session max_bytes budget enforced with `limit_exceeded` abort; protocol violations tear the session down with terminal sync_end + misbehavior charge

Layer D legacy: publisher writes one BEP-44 mutable item per (pubkey, keyword) — salt = lowercased UTF-8 keyword, target = SHA1(pubkey||salt), value = {ts, hits[{ih,n,s,f,sz}], more, next_pk} ≤1000 bytes; shards spill to salt `keyword#1`, `#2`… with root `more:1`; hourly refresh against 2h BEP-44 expiry

Layer D v0.5.0 PPMI: one BEP-44 item per publisher at fixed double-hashed salt SHA256("snet.index") with v = {ih (companion torrent infohash), commit (SHA256 canonical-record fingerprint), topics (optional cuckoo digest), ts, next_pk}; real keyword records live in a companion B-tree torrent; v0.5 dual-writes/dual-reads both formats for migration

Layer D lookup: searcher tokenizes query same as publishers, picks most-distinctive token, fans out BEP-44 gets across known indexer pubkeys in parallel, verifies each signature, merges hits by infohash weighted by per-pubkey reputation; single-indexer errors never abort the lookup; Lookup.Query resolves PPMI first, falls back to legacy per-keyword

Indexer pubkey discovery via four channels: self-pubkey (single-node testability), hardcoded seeds (empty in v1), sn_search peer_announce `pk` gossip (only nodes with Publisher cap =1 emit it; receivers auto-add to Lookup's indexer set; zero pubkey rejected), and user-supplied; Aggregate adds anchors + BEP-51 sample_infohashes crawl + HTTPS bootstrap fallback

Torrent signing: `swartznet create --sign` (and GUI checkbox, default on) adds top-level `snet.pubkey` (32B) + `snet.sig` (64B ed25519 over "SN-TORRENT-V1|"||infohash) to the .torrent; infohash is unchanged so signed and unsigned twins share one swarm; verification is automatic at .torrent add time; magnet adds get signed_by=""

Publisher trust: local JSON allowlist (trust.json); trusted-publisher torrents are auto-confirmed into the known-good Bloom filter the moment metadata arrives (bypassing wait-for-completion); CLI `swartznet trust list/add/remove`; GUI right-click Trust/Verify-signature; ★/✓/— badges

Search by publisher: Bleve schema v3 persists signed_by on every TorrentDoc; `swartznet search --signed-by <pubkey>`, POST /search {signed_by}, web-UI publisher input + clickable badges pivoting to "everything else by this publisher"; Layer-L only (swarm/DHT layers carry no signed metadata)

Unified search fan-out: one query fires Layers L/S/D in parallel (CLI --swarm/--dht flags, POST /search {q, signed_by?, swarm?, dht?, highlight?}), merged and deduped by infohash at the httpapi boundary with per-layer badges; local hits stream first, swarm ~100ms, DHT 1-5s; Bleve operators (+required -excluded "phrase" field:value fuzzy~1) supported

Spam resistance: per-pubkey Bayesian reputation (hits_returned/confirmed/flagged) gates which indexers are queried and demotes merged hits; known-good Bloom filter (1M items @1% FP, ~1.2MB) boosts confirmed hits +0.25; `swartznet flag`/`confirm` CLI + POST /flag /confirm; flag demotes only the indexers that returned that infohash (SourceTracker), failing closed with zero demotions when attribution is missing

Ingestion pipeline: piece-verify callback → file-complete tracker → MIME sniff → extractor dispatch (19 pure-Go extractors: plaintext, subtitle, PDF, EPUB, DOCX, ODT, RTF, archive, FB2, PPTX, ODP, MOBI, ID3, EXIF, FLAC, OGG, MKV, MP4, ZIM) → chunker → batched Bleve writes; extraction idempotent by (infohash, file_index, file_content_sha256); per-torrent indexing toggle via Engine.SetTorrentIndexing / POST /torrents/{ih}/indexing / `swartznet index <ih> on|off`
Global --no-index prevents Bleve opening at all AND cascades to disable the Layer-D keyword publisher and zero the Publisher capability bit (node still subscribes/fetches, contributes nothing)

Companion (F3) content-index torrents: hourly Publisher builds gzip+JSON index from local Bleve, seeds it as a single-file torrent named swartznet-content-index-<pubkey-prefix-12>-v1.json.gz (256 KiB pieces), and publishes a BEP-46-style mutable pointer at salt `_sn_content_index` carrying {ih, ts}; Subscriber follows pubkeys (companion-follows.json), resolves pointer, downloads torrent, ingests into local Bleve; GET/POST /companion {refresh,follow,unfollow} + GUI/web Companion tabs

Full torrent-client surface: add magnet/.torrent, create .torrent (piece-length choices, trackers, webseeds BEP-19, private BEP-27, name override, optional sign, optional seed-in-place), pause/resume/remove, per-file priority none/normal/high, upload/download rate limits, FIFO max-active-downloads queue, session persistence across restarts (session.json + torrents/<ih>.torrent, magnet entries upgraded to file entries after metadata)

Three frontends over one daemon: static CLI (subcommands add, search, create, index, files, flag, confirm, status, trust, crawl-probe), embedded web UI at localhost:7654 (go:embed), native Fyne GUI (5 tabs, system tray, --torrent/--tab flags); all call internal/daemon.New

HTTP API (loopback-only by default; non-loopback binds refused without explicit opt-in; CSRF/DNS-rebinding defense on mutating endpoints): POST /search /torrent /confirm /flag, GET/DELETE torrent management, per-file priority, GET/POST /config/rate-limit /config/queue /capabilities /companion, GET /status /status.dht /index/stats /healthz

Diagnostics/ops: cmd/dht-smoke live BEP-44 put/get smoke with -stress flags reporting per-put latency percentiles; `swartznet crawl-probe --addr` one-shot BEP-51 sample_infohashes; GET /status.dht {good_nodes, nodes} (nil when DHT disabled); testbed with docker+netem scenarios s1-s12 including s11 vanilla-client wire-interop proof

Wire-compat test matrix (§8, all four directions MUST pass): vanilla client downloads from us with zero sn_search frames; we download from vanilla swarms without advertising sn_search to them; DHT stays healthy for non-participants (our BEP-44 items are indistinguishable from anyone else's); two SwartzNet clients negotiate search, mismatched scope gets reject code 2, publishers cross-register pubkeys via peer_announce pk gossip, unknown fields tolerated for forward compat

Testing-only DHT flags: `--dht-insecure` (disables BEP-42 node-ID security, needed on docker bridges, gated/fail-closed outside tests) and repeatable `--dht-bootstrap=HOST:PORT` (replaces public mainline bootstrap hosts); `--no-dht-publish` leech-only mode keeps gets but skips every put

inputs_outputs: In: magnet URIs / .torrent files / local content roots (create); free-text queries via CLI/HTTP/GUI; pubkeys for trust/follow/signed-by filters; config flags (--no-index, --no-dht, --no-dht-publish, --api-addr, --data-dir, --index-dir, --dht-bootstrap, --dht-insecure, --identity, --key)
In (wire): BEP-3 piece traffic, BEP-9 ut_metadata, BEP-10 LTEP handshakes, BEP-11 ut_pex, inbound sn_search frames (msg_types 0-8), BEP-5/44 DHT queries, BEP-51 sample_infohashes responses

Out (wire): standard BEP-3/5/9/10/44 traffic to vanilla peers; sn_search frames only to peers that advertised the extension; BEP-44 puts (legacy keyword items, PPMI, BEP-46 companion pointers) at ≤5 puts/sec, hourly refresh, ≥1-confirmed-node success criterion

Out (files): downloaded content under data dir; Bleve index dir (schema v3); identity.key (0600); trust.json; reputation.json; known-good.bloom; seeds.json; session.json + torrents/<ih>.torrent copies; companion dir artifacts (swartznet-content-index-<pkprefix12>-v1.json.gz + wrapping .torrent); companion-follows.json (1 MiB cap); config.json (GUI settings); created .torrent files (atomic tmp+rename, optionally with snet.pubkey/snet.sig)
Out (API/UI): JSON over localhost:7654 (loopback only by default, empty --api-addr disables); layer-attributed merged search results; OS notifications and system-tray presence (GUI)
data_models: sn_search LTEP envelope: BT message ID 20, ext msg ID = receiver's m["sn_search"], payload = one bencoded dict discriminated by msg_type 0-8 (docs/06:140-168). Query {msg_type,txid u32,q,scope subset of n/f/c,limit,lang,min_size,max_size,not_ih[20B...]}; Result {txid echo,total,partial,hits[{ih 20B,ih2 32B opt,n,s,l,sz,t,rank 0-1000,matches[{fi,fp,pr,sn,off}]}]}; Reject {txid,code 0-4,reason}; peer_announce {v int, services uint64} (docs/06:174-267)

ServiceBits uint64: bit0 ShareLocal, 1 ShareSwarm (mutually exclusive with 0 in practice), 2 FileHits, 3 ContentHits, 4 LayerDPublisher, 5 CompanionPublisher, 6 CompanionSubscriber, 7 SnippetHighlight, 8 Regtest, 9 SetReconciliation, 10-63 reserved (docs/06:112-126)

BEP-44 KeywordValue: bencoded {ts int, hits[{ih 20B, n opt, s opt, f opt, sz opt}], more opt int, next_pk opt 32B} ≤1000 bytes; salt = lowercase keyword (≤64B), shard salts keyword#N; target = SHA1(pubkey||salt); ih2 deliberately removed from v1; next_pk on wire but never populated in v1 (docs/07:124-214)

PPMI (v0.5): salt = SHA256("snet.index") fixed 32B, v = {ih 20B, commit 32B, topics opt 32B, ts, next_pk reserved} (docs/05:330-341); companion B-tree pages magic SNAGG\0, interior/leaf/trailer kinds, ed25519-signed trailer, BFS piece assignment, hashcash PoW D=20 on records (CHANGELOG:274-283); byte-level normative spec delegated to docs/research/SPEC.md §1-3
BEP-46 companion pointer: mutable item at salt `_sn_content_index`, v = {ih, ts omitempty} — TS=0 decodes as "unknown freshness, accept" (CHANGELOG:361-388,1996-1999)

Signed .torrent: top-level keys snet.pubkey (exactly 32B) + snet.sig (exactly 64B); payload = 14-byte literal "SN-TORRENT-V1|" || 20B SHA-1 infohash = always 34 bytes; keys outside info dict so infohash unchanged; one-without-other = treat as unsigned (log, no hard error); re-sign overwrites; future versions bump the domain prefix, verifiers MUST tolerate unknown snet.* keys (docs/11:129-215,279-292)

Bleve schema v3: TorrentDoc {infohash keyword, name text, trackers keyword, added_at, size, seeder_count, signed_by keyword hex64} + nested File {path,mime,size,pieces_root} + Content {file_index, text ~2KiB chunks, lang, offset}; SchemaVersion mismatch triggers full clean rebuild on open (docs/05:200-227; CHANGELOG:1288-1300,2062-2068)
BEP-44 canonical signing buffer: `4:salt<len>:<salt>3:seqi<seq>e1:v<len>:<v>` per BEP-44 (docs/07:219-227)

Companion index v1 file: gzip(JSON CompanionIndex{TorrentRecord/FileRecord/ContentChunk}), FormatVersion=1, format-magic guard, 1 GiB decode cap, wrapped in single-file v1 torrent w/ 256 KiB pieces (CHANGELOG:1982-1994)

On-disk state: identity.key (ed25519, mode exactly 0600 enforced, pubkey re-derived from seed and verified on load), trust.json, reputation.json (+SeededAt/SeedLabel), known-good.bloom (custom format, exact bitset-length check, odd-stride double hashing), seeds.json (versioned SeedList), session.json (per-torrent paused/indexing/queue_order/addedVia/DataPath/content_name), companion-follows.json ({pubkey,label} array)
external_deps: anacrolix/torrent (MPL 2.0) — BT engine; extension points used: Callbacks.PieceStateChange, LocalLtepProtocolMap.AddUserProtocol, PeerConnReadExtensionMessage, WriteExtendedMessage; MPL discipline = no core patches (docs/05:162-179)

anacrolix/dht/v2 + exts/getput — BEP-44 put/get, BEP-42 node-ID derivation, BEP-51 sampling; known upstream trap: NewAnacrolixDhtServer leaves Exp=0 so items expire instantly, must pin sc.Exp=2h (CHANGELOG:627-647)
Bleve (pure Go) — Layer L full-text index, BM25, QueryStringQuery operators, HTML highlighter (docs/05:191-198)

Fyne v2.7 (BSD-3, CGo/OpenGL) — native GUI; ledongthuc/pdf (BSD-3-Clause, not MIT — corrected in M13a); golang.org/x/net/html; klauspost/compress (zstd for ZIM); golang.org/x/time/rate (CHANGELOG:2041-2051,1276-1277,1753)

Protocols: BEP-3, BEP-4 (why LTEP not reserved bit), BEP-5, BEP-9, BEP-10 (LTEP), BEP-11 (PEX), BEP-19 (webseeds), BEP-27 (private), BEP-42, BEP-44, BEP-46 (pointer pattern), BEP-51 (crawl), BEP-52 (ih2/pieces_root fields); RFC 8032 ed25519

Design patterns borrowed: Bitcoin Core BIP-9 services-bits (unknown-bit tolerance), BIP-152 compact-encoding (future v1.1 profile), Rateless IBLT (SIGCOMM 2024) for set reconciliation (docs/06:106-110,320-324; CHANGELOG:290-292)

nonobvious_rules.rule: Mainline-compat is the load-bearing constraint: no new reserved bit, no new DHT verb, no new port, no new overlay; all extensions are LTEP opt-in and DHT items are plain BEP-44 — "there is no distinction between our DHT items and anyone else's" is stated as THE reason BEP-44 was chosen over a custom verb
Extension name is `sn_search` with prefix sn_ (NOT lt_ — lt_ is historically libtorrent's namespace)
Signing fields MUST live outside the info dict so signed and unsigned twins share one infohash/swarm; moving them inside would 'fork the network'

Signature payload is exactly 34 bytes: 14-byte literal "SN-TORRENT-V1|" (trailing | is decorative but byte-exact) || 20-byte infohash; domain prefix is the version anchor — v2 = new prefix + new field names, never in-band negotiation

identity.key loader rejects any file mode other than exactly 0600; explicit --key/--identity paths are load-only and error on missing file — identity is never regenerated implicitly (losing it loses publisher reputation)

Magnet adds always get signed_by="" because metainfo bytes aren't available at add time — and BEP-9 only transports the info dict, so snet.* top-level fields can never arrive via ut_metadata (this blocks the BEP-51 crawler from classifying publishers)

peer_announce pk gossip: only nodes with Publisher capability = 1 emit their pubkey; non-publishers MUST suppress pk so pure subscribers can never pollute indexer sets; all-zero 32-byte pubkey is rejected at the sink while the rest of the frame is still processed

Absence of peer_announce = services 0, NOT a protocol error; responder MUST NOT refuse a query solely because the initiator never announced; unknown service bits MUST be ignored (additive extensibility 'forever')
txid echo is mandatory: responder MUST return the query's txid so the initiator can route replies; result/reject frames from peers outside a query's fan-out set are dropped and charged as misbehavior

BEP-44 anacrolix wrapper needs sc.Exp pinned to 2h — upstream NewAnacrolixDhtServer leaves Exp=0 which makes every stored item instantly expired (put succeeds, get returns 'value not found'); a rewrite that drops this pin silently breaks all of Layer D

A publish that reached zero DHT nodes is a failure, not success (all three put paths: keyword, BEP-46 pointer, PPMI share one checkPutStats guard) — previously the rate limiter suppressed retry for ~55m after a phantom success

Publisher throttles: MinPutInterval 55 minutes per keyword (self-DoS guard since anacrolix has no put rate cap); design budget 5 puts/sec total; 3 consecutive failures → keyword marked unhealthy → daily retry; only items with activity in last 24h are refreshed
dhtindex.Publisher publishes ONLY Tokenize(torrent.Name) keywords — never content tokens (an s12 test bug came from querying a content word)

Tokenization contract (cross-implementation agreement required for lookups to find anything): lowercase Unicode letters+digits, split on everything else, drop tokens <3 bytes, drop file-extension noise (mp4/iso/pdf...), drop stopwords, cap 8 keywords per torrent; searcher picks the longest non-stopword token

KeywordValue keeps next_pk on every wire message but v1 NEVER populates it — wire shape frozen now so subscribers can adopt rotation later without a format bump; ih2 was removed from v1 for the opposite reason (would waste bytes against the 1000-byte cap while unpopulated)

Key rotation is deliberately not linkable at protocol level for legacy items (old entries just expire after 2h; clean-slate reputation is a feature); PPMI/next_pk rides the current key's signature so only the current key holder can announce a successor

Manifest evicts oldest-first when a keyword entry would overflow the 1000-byte cap, and size estimates reserve timestamp width so near-cap entries can actually publish; RemoveTorrent → publisher.Retract scrubs the infohash from every keyword so removed torrents stop being re-announced

Companion torrents: subscribers enforce a 32 MiB acceptance limit (maxCompanionBytes) on declared size BEFORE downloading any pieces; B-tree walk keeps one shared visited-set across the whole traversal and fails closed on ANY page re-visit (interior structure is unsigned — hostile layouts otherwise force Fibonacci-growth page reads), capping the walk at NumPieces fetches
Subscribers locate the companion payload by the path returned from FetchCompanionTorrent and never key on the filename — the publisher-tagged filename is cosmetic

Ranking formula is spec'd: 0.4·bm25(name) + 0.2·bm25(files) + 0.2·bm25(content) + 0.1·log(seeders+1) + 0.1·freshness, freshness = exp(-(now-t)/30d), ×1000 rounded to int 0-1000; queriers free to re-rank the merged union
Trusted-publisher torrents skip the normal wait-for-download-completion path and are auto-confirmed to the known-good Bloom the moment metadata arrives
Flagging an infohash with no recorded source attribution demotes NOBODY (fail closed) — the earlier 'demote everyone seen recently' fallback was attacker-weaponizable

Seed-list reputation bonus decays with a 90-day half-life (fresh seed ≈0.95) so organic reputation dominates after a quarter; anchors get MarkSeeded (high starting score), NOT RecordReturned(pk,0) which is a silent no-op; anchors don't consume MaxTrackedPublishers slots

SubscribeFileEvents returns a fresh buffered channel per caller with broadcast fan-out AND replays already-complete files at subscribe time — single shared channel silently split events between CLI progress and the indexer (historical stall bug), and seeds whose pieces verified before subscription never got indexed

Backpressure drops, doesn't block: file-complete→extract channel capacity 64; full channel drops the request and an hourly background scan picks up missed files; extract budgets: 100 MiB global per-file cap, 64 MiB text budget per zip entry (decompressed), 60s soft watchdog, reader closed only by the extracting goroutine after Extract returns
.txt/.text/.md need explicit MIME-table overrides — Go's builtin mime table lacks .txt, so Alpine/scratch deployments silently skip plaintext extraction without them

Per-torrent seed storage keys file paths on the real on-disk basename (custom FilePathMaker), not info.Name, so renamed torrents seed in place while downloaders see the chosen name; basename persisted as session field content_name, legacy entries fall back to info.Name; create --seed seeds in place from the positional root and keeps DHT enabled

RestoreSession runs VerifyData per entry (anacrolix never eagerly verifies on-disk pieces; a fresh infohash with no peers otherwise sits at 0% forever); AddTorrentMetaInfo persists to the session manifest like every other add path; the magnet→metainfo upgrade goroutine is spawned ONLY for AddMagnet/AddInfoHash (on file paths it raced writeTorrentCopy and corrupted the saved bytes via re-marshalling)
x.pe= peer hints must be dotted-quad IPs — hostnames don't reliably round-trip anacrolix's StringAddr dialer (testbed pins static IPs for this reason)

Bit 8 (BitRegtest) is a deliberately 'loud' capability so accidental regtest→mainnet cross-connections are obvious; --dht-insecure/--regtest are gated and config.Validate fails closed on them outside tests

Threat-model partition is explicit: spam/poisoning/sybil/tamper are in scope; anonymity, query privacy, censorship resistance, content policy are OUT of scope (bring your own VPN/Tor) — 'fast and useful' side of the Freenet tradeoff
UIs MUST distinguish ErrNotSigned (benign) from ErrBadSignature (firm tamper signal), and SHOULD NOT penalise unsigned torrents in default rankings (— placeholder vs ✓ badge, no value judgment)
Bleve index schema bumps trigger a full clean rebuild on first open (SchemaVersion sentinel mismatch), not a migration

Layer isolation is architectural law: three response types (indexer.SearchResponse / swarmsearch.QueryResponse / dhtindex.LookupResponse) reconciled only at the httpapi boundary; no shared cross-layer type
Content-chunk target is 2 KiB (M13e shrank it from 10 KiB based on BM25-relevance research) — a rewrite copying the design doc's '~10KB chunks' would regress relevance

Layer-D privacy contract: keyword goes over the wire only as SHA1 target (dictionary attack possible, accepted); PPMI double-hashed salt makes every publisher's item look identical to observers, moving keyword enumeration from passive observation to download-and-index

broken_or_unfinished.issue: Spec-internal contradiction on the peer_announce schema: doc 06's msg_type-3 schema defines only {v, services}, yet doc 05 §8.4, doc 07 §discovery, and the CHANGELOG all describe an implemented 32-byte `pk` field on peer_announce (publisher-pubkey gossip). The BEP draft that is supposedly the wire spec-of-record omits a field the system relies on for indexer discovery.

Doc 05 §5.1 still specifies the retired capability mechanism — `sn_search_v`/`sn_search_cap` keys in the LTEP handshake with the "L0F0C0P0" string — which doc 06 explicitly replaced with the services-bitfield peer_announce (retired during M15b). Doc 06's reject-code table also still says "sn_search_cap" (line 255). Two conflicting capability schemes coexist in the spec set.

Scope-mismatch handling contradiction: doc 06's Query section says a responder "SHOULD silently downgrade rather than reject" an unsupported scope letter, but the reference implementation was deliberately changed to send Reject code 2, citing wire-compat matrix row 8.4-B (doc 05 §8.4 also specifies reject). The BEP draft's capability section permits either, but its SHOULD points opposite to both the matrix and the shipped behavior.
Stale doc: doc 05 says the per-torrent indexing CLI is "a future `swartznet index off <infohash>` subcommand (not yet implemented)", but v0.3.1 shipped `swartznet index <infohash> on|off`.

Migration-schedule version collision: doc 05/doc 07 schedule the PPMI migration as "v0.5 dual-writes... v0.6 writes PPMI only; v0.7 drops the legacy read path", but v0.6.0 and v0.7.0 were already released (2026-04-13) as extractor/search-by-publisher releases containing none of those phases — the Aggregate redesign itself sits in the Unreleased section dated after v0.7.0. The stated retirement timeline cannot be literal.

Stale chunk size in the design doc: §4.1 and §6 specify "~10KB chunks" but M13e shrank DefaultChunkTargetBytes to 2 KiB; also §2 diagram says "18 pure-Go extractors" while the ZIM entry brought the total to 19.

Rate-limit numbers diverge between spec and implementation: doc 06 states "100 queries per peer per hour" (n/f) and "10 per hour" (c) — repeated as a definitive default under Security Considerations — but M12f implemented a per-peer token bucket of 5 q/s steady / burst 10 with no scope-differentiated hourly budget on record.

Likely-aspirational design features with no implementation trace anywhere in the CHANGELOG: publisher stats written to /var/log/swartznet/publisher.json (§7); optional AES-256-GCM/age index encryption at rest (§6 Privacy); user-editable deny-glob indexing exclusions with per-file UI override (§6 Opt-out); 'default off indexing for torrents added via sn_search result clicks' (§11).

BEP-51 crawler channel is explicitly half-finished: primitives (SampleInfohashes, PublisherFromMetainfo, CrawlOnce, crawl-probe CLI) exist, but there is no production MetainfoFetcher because BEP-9 cannot transport the top-level snet.* fields; closing it needs a new LTEP extension (e.g. ut_signature) or an out-of-band convention — acknowledged open gap.

Seed/anchor pubkey list never shipped: doc 05 §4.3 designs a hardcoded ~20-pubkey seed list, doc 07 says the list is "Empty in the v1 reference release", M13c built the loading machinery but states "the actual shipping seed list file is not bundled — distribution is a post-v1 operational decision", and the Aggregate redesign re-scopes it to "~5 reputation anchors". Cold-start discovery therefore has no shipped trust root.
v1.0.0 is explicitly blocked on externalities: real-world data for the reputation prior weight and at least one second client implementing sn_search (BEP-1 requirement for Final status).

open_questions: Which scope-mismatch behavior is normative going forward — doc 06's 'SHOULD silently downgrade' or the implemented/matrix-mandated Reject code 2? The BEP draft needs one answer before a second client implements it.

Is the peer_announce `pk` field meant to be part of the public sn_search BEP (and just missing from doc 06's schema), or an implementation-private extension that a second client need not send? Related: is a `services` bit implied for it?
What is the real retirement schedule for legacy per-keyword BEP-44 items now that the doc's v0.6/v0.7 phase labels collide with already-released v0.6.0/v0.7.0 version numbers?

Are the §6/§7 aspirational features (index encryption at rest via age, deny-glob exclusions, publisher.json field telemetry, default-off indexing for sn_search-click adds) still planned, or abandoned scope that should be excised from the design doc?

Who curates and how do you distribute the seed/anchor pubkey list (§13.4 cold-start question) — the machinery exists but the operational decision is explicitly deferred; a rewrite can't know whether to bundle one.
Should the documented per-hour scope-differentiated rate limits (100/hr n+f, 10/hr c) be restored on top of the implemented 5 q/s token bucket, or should doc 06 be rewritten to match the bucket?

Doc 05 §13.6 (publisher identity exposure) was answered by M13d's 'honest subset' (--no-dht-publish + docs), with next_pk shipped-but-unused — is key rotation still committed for v1.1, and does trust migration via next_pk apply to trust.json entries automatically?

The 06 draft's rule 'mask off only the bits it understands (bits ≥ the highest defined bit in its own build)' is self-contradictory as worded (mask off understood bits? ignore bits ≥ highest?) — what exact masking behavior did the author intend a second implementation to perform?

readers.purpose: Provides SwartzNet's layered test-and-operations surface: Layer A is `internal/testlab`, an in-process multi-engine harness (real sockets, no containers) that pins the wire-compat matrix, sn_search/Layer-D behaviors, and adversarial handling; Layer B is `testbed/`, a Docker+tc-netem multi-container environment with 12 assertion scenarios driven by `scripts/run-testbed.sh`; plus process-level fixtures (`tests/torrent-test` + `scripts/test-multi-peer.sh`), release/GUI build scripts, an autonomous improvement loop (`.claude-iterate.sh`), and the user-facing operations guide (`docs/08-operations.md`) and agent conventions (`AGENTS.md`). Modeled explicitly on Bitcoin Core's functional-test framework (MiniNode analog, netem profiles, layered A/B/C/D testbed).

capabilities.behavior: `scripts/run-testbed.sh <s1..s12|swarm|all> [--json=path]` drives Docker scenario runs end-to-end: validates docker compose v2 + socket access with actionable error text, auto-rebuilds `dist/swartznet-testbed-linux-amd64` when any .go source is newer, brings up the right compose stack with the scenario's NETEM_PROFILE, waits ≤120s for containers to reach running, executes the assertion script, tears down via EXIT trap with `--profile '*' down -v`, writes `testbed/results/<scenario>-<timestamp>.log`, prints a box-drawn scoreboard with per-scenario durations, and exits nonzero on any failure

`--json=<path>` emits a machine-readable run summary ({started_at, finished_at, total_wall_clock_s, overall_exit, scenarios:[{name,result,duration_s,netem_profile}]}) via a python3 heredoc for CI bots and perf-regression trending

3-node compose stack (2 seeds + 1 leech, subnet 172.27.0.0/24, host ports 17654-17656) where seeds start `swartznet add --regtest --no-dht /fixture/fixture.torrent` with ROLE=seed pre-copied content, and the leech bootstraps purely from `x.pe=172.27.0.2:42069&x.pe=172.27.0.3:42069` magnet hints — no DHT, no tracker

6-node swarm stack (2 seeds + 4 leeches, 172.28.0.0/24, ports 17664-17669) with full-mesh x.pe hints, plus two profile-gated services: `late-joiner` leech-5 (s9) and `vanilla` leech running stock anacrolix/torrent CLI `torrent download --no-seed --no-dht --no-pex` (s11)

6-node DHT-enabled stack (172.29.0.0/24, ports 17680-17685) where every node runs `--regtest --dht-insecure --dht-bootstrap=<seed-ip>` to form a private mainline-compatible DHT for Layer-D BEP-44 publish/lookup (scenario s12); seeds cross-bootstrap to each other, never to self

Container entrypoint applies an optional tc-netem profile then, for ROLE=seed, copies /fixture/content into /data with `cp -a` so anacrolix's piece-verify marks the torrent complete at startup; ROLE=leech starts empty; unknown ROLE defaults to leech with a warning
Four netem profiles applied inside containers (CAP_NET_ADMIN): lan (0.5ms/1Gbit), home-dsl (20ms±5ms/25Mbit), mobile-4g (40ms±20ms/10Mbit), lossy (75ms/5% loss/20Mbit)

Scenarios s1-s4 assert daemon lifecycle under network profiles: /healthz `"ok":true`, /status contains "local", /torrents non-empty on all 3 nodes; s4 additionally asserts POST /search {"q":"aethergram"} returns >0 local hits on both seeds (waiting for /index/stats content_count≥1 first)

s5/s6/s8 assert real piece transfer: seeds hash-verify to progress=1.0 in 30s, leeches reach 1.0 (90s single-leech / 120s 4-leech / 300s lossy), and on-disk sha256 of every downloaded file matches the fixture byte-for-byte; s6 additionally polls at 100ms to record peak active_peers during the transfer window and fails if peak <2 (proves both seeds connected via x.pe hints)

s7 asserts Layer-S sn_search fan-out over real LTEP: all leeches indexed (content_count>0), querier has capable_peers≥1 in /status, then POST /search {"q":"aethergram","swarm":true,"swarm_timeout_ms":3000} from inside leech-1 must show swarm.asked≥1, responded≥1, and a hit whose infohash equals the fixture's

s9 proves pass-along resilience: after 4 leeches complete, both seeds are docker-stopped, leech-5 is started via compose profile and must download the full 4 MiB exclusively from ex-leeches within 60s with byte-exact content; prober switches to leech-1 since seed-1 dies

s10 kills seed-1 only after leech-1 crosses progress≥0.3 under lossy netem (single-seed-failure path, seed-2 alive), requires all 4 leeches to converge within 300s plus byte check; if leech-1 finishes before the trigger it exits 0 as a graceful 'no mid-transfer window' skip

s11 proves mainline wire-compat with a non-SwartzNet client: the stock anacrolix `torrent` CLI container must exit 0 within 240s having downloaded the fixture from SwartzNet peers using only BEP-3/9/10 (no DHT, no PEX, no sn_search); bytes are verified via `docker cp` from the stopped container

s12 asserts the full Layer-D round-trip: DHT formation (known_peers>0), both seed publishers primed (total_keywords>0), at least one BEP-44 put emitted (last_published set), 20s settle, then POST /search {"q":"corpus","dht":true} from leech-1 must show indexers_asked≥2 (pubkey-gossip), indexers_responded≥1 (sc.Exp fix), and the fixture infohash in dht.hits

`scripts/test-multi-peer.sh` is a container-free E2E harness driving 4 real `dist/swartznet` processes on loopback (seeder ports 42170/17650, peers 42171-3/17651-3): builds the binary, creates a .torrent from the generated fixture, seeds via symlinked source, launches 3 peers on a magnet with x.pe=127.0.0.1 hint, asserts completion, per-file sha256 manifest equality, waits for indexed_files==files, then asserts search for 'photon' returns hits on every peer; writes tests/torrent-test/results/run-<ts>.txt

`scripts/gen-test-fixture.sh` deterministically regenerates the 15-file (~485 KiB) multi-peer corpus: 3 'books' × 5 extensions with per-book cleartext markers (photon/polity/meridian) and LCG-derived filler/binary payloads so piece hashes are stable across runs

`scripts/gen-swarm-fixture.sh` regenerates the 4-MiB swarm fixture (8 × 512-KiB chapters, marker 'aethergram', fixed-seed random), builds the .torrent with 64-KiB pieces via `swartznet create`, and extracts+persists the infohash with an embedded minimal bencode parser into testbed/fixture-swarm/INFOHASH

`scripts/build-release.sh <version>` cross-compiles 5 static CLI binaries (linux/darwin × amd64/arm64 + windows-amd64.exe) with CGO_ENABLED=0, `-trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.Version=..."`, and writes dist/SHA256SUMS; `scripts/build-gui.sh [version]` builds the CGo Fyne GUI for the native host only, stamping Version and BuildDate ldflags

run-testbed.sh builds the vanilla anacrolix CLI (`github.com/anacrolix/torrent/cmd/torrent@v1.61.0`) in a throwaway temp Go module (to avoid polluting go.mod) into dist/torrent-vanilla-linux-amd64, only when the file is missing

testlab.NewCluster(t,n) spawns n real engine.Engine instances in-process with per-node t.TempDir state (data/bleve/identity/publisher/reputation/bloom/companion), DHT disabled, Seed=true, Regtest=true, OS-assigned ports, debug logs captured per node; every node joins a metadata-less shared infohash so LTEP handshakes fire; WireMesh() creates the O(N²) peer mesh and WaitAllHandshaked() gates on all pairs advertising sn_search

testlab.NewDHTCluster(t,n) is the DHT-enabled sibling (DisableDHT=false, DHTInsecure=true, DisableIPv6=true, ListenHost=127.0.0.1) chain-bootstrapped node0→placeholder, node1→node0, rest→{node0,node1}, forming a live intra-cluster DHT without touching public routers — the in-process counterpart to docker scenario s12

testlab.MiniPeer is a Bitcoin-Core-MiniNode-style pure-code BT peer: performs the 68-byte BEP-3 handshake (reserved byte 5=0x10), the BEP-10 LTEP handshake (optionally omitting sn_search via DialVanillaMiniPeer to impersonate a mainline client), sends/receives extended messages, and injects raw malformed bytes for adversarial tests; rejects messages >1 MiB

testlab pins the docs/05 §8 wire-compat matrix in-process: 8.1-A vanilla peer never receives an sn_search frame (vanilla_peer_scenario_test.go:12-31); 8.1-A/B a real anacrolix client fetches metadata via BEP-9 and completes a piece download from a SwartzNet seeder (vanilla_download_scenario_test.go:20-32); 8.1-C ut_pex passes through and unknown LTEP keys are ignored (pex_ltep_scenario_test.go:3-22); 8.4-B scope-c query to a C0 responder yields Reject code 2 over the wire (scope_reject_scenario_test.go:12-29); 8.4-C publisher-pubkey gossip auto-registers Layer-D indexers (gossip_pubkey_scenario_test.go:59-127)

testlab pins protective behaviors over real sockets: misbehavior scoring bans a peer flooding 1-char queries past BanThreshold=100 and silently drops post-ban messages (misbehavior_scenario_test.go:12-31); per-peer rate limiter rejects the 4th+ query in a burst=3 window (ratelimit_test.go:1-28); sybil publisher demoted below MinIndexerScore is excluded from lookups (sybil_scenario_test.go:13-29); stale txid / oversized payload / future protocol version frames are tolerated without crash (minipeer_adversarial_test.go:13-107); hit-cache population across queries (cache_scenario_test.go:1-20); AddrMan-style peer-book new→tried promotion only after a correct response (peerbook_scenario_test.go:1-26)

testlab pins core user flows end-to-end in-process: magnet add → metadata fetch → full download (the only test of the `swartznet add <magnet>` metainfo path, magnet_scenario_test.go:15-37); multi-file torrent with nested dirs + per-file ingest (multifile_scenario_test.go:1-46); download → extract → Bleve index → local query (content_search_scenario_test.go:1-40); file-event fan-out delivers every file to every subscriber independently (file_events_fanout_scenario_test.go:1-35); F3 companion publish → BEP-46 pointer → subscriber sync (companion_scenario_test.go:1-48); Aggregate RIBLT sync over LTEP + publisher-observer admission gating (aggregate_sync/aggregate_observer scenario tests); Layer-D publish/lookup/refresh/multi-indexer-merge with fake and real DHT (layerd_test.go, layerd_refresh_scenario_test.go, layerd_dht_cluster_test.go, layerd_gossip_scenario_test.go)

`.claude-iterate.sh` runs `claude --print --permission-mode bypassPermissions` in an infinite loop with a fixed prompt: run `go test ./... -count=1 -short`, fix failures or add tests to the weakest-coverage area, make ONE incremental improvement, re-test, commit; priority order 'test coverage > edge cases > performance > code quality'; appends to .claude-iterate.log, retries after 30s on nonzero exit, 10s pause between iterations

docs/08-operations.md is the operator manual: the full XDG file-layout tree, a what-to-back-up/recoverability table (identity.key is the one unrecoverable file), 0600 identity permission enforcement + fix, daemon startup sequence and flags table, command cookbook (search/status/confirm/flag/create --sign/index/files/trust/aggregate/crawl-probe), backwards-compat statement, privacy/threat model (visible: IP to ~8 closest DHT nodes, persistent pubkey, hourly timing fingerprint; not visible: downloads/local queries/loopback UI), troubleshooting playbook, GUI feature docs, and the 19-extractor table

nonobvious_rules.rule: x.pe= magnet peer hints MUST be dotted-quad IP:port, never hostnames — anacrolix feeds the raw string into its peer list as StringAddr with lazy resolution and has been observed to silently drop non-dotted-quad hints; this is why every compose stack pins static IPAM subnets

All API probes run via `docker exec <container> curl http://<hostname>:7654/...` over the internal bridge, never via host-published ports — on stock Ubuntu (UFW DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=DROP) host→container HTTP is RST'd even though the TCP handshake completes; published ports exist only for manual inspection

Seed containers pre-populate /data with `cp -a` (preserving timestamps) so anacrolix's piece-verify pass marks the torrent complete at startup; scenario seed-progress assertions (30s) depend on this hash-verify shortcut

Scenarios s1-s11 all run --regtest --no-dht; s12 is the ONLY DHT-enabled scenario and requires all three of: --regtest (publisher refresh 1h→5s), --dht-insecure (BEP-42 derives secure node IDs from IP — container/loopback IPs never qualify, so every put target would be silently filtered), and --dht-bootstrap pointing at in-cluster seeds (public bootstrap routers unreachable from the bridge → no DHT ever forms)

DHT seeds must cross-bootstrap to each other, never to themselves — self-bootstrap caused BEP-44 put transaction timeouts (get_peers returned the seed's own entry; the put raced its own listen socket)

testlab DHT cluster node 0 bootstraps to placeholder 127.0.0.1:1 instead of an empty list — an empty DHTBootstrapAddrs falls through to anacrolix's global default (router.bittorrent.com etc.), which poisons the isolated cluster with live-mainline routes (observed as puts to 5.196.x.x)

testlab DHT nodes force DisableIPv6=true (anacrolix otherwise creates udp4+udp6 DHT servers, the engine picks one, and IPv4-mapped-IPv6 addrs pollute routing tables) AND ListenHost=127.0.0.1 (the BEP-44 put-token validator SHA1s the query's source IP; a 0.0.0.0 bind lets the kernel vary source IP per send, tripping 'invalid token' → silent value-not-found)

anacrolix's NewAnacrolixDhtServer does not copy the dht default Exp=2h, leaving sc.Exp=0 so bep44.Wrapper.Get treats every stored item as instantly expired (put succeeds, get returns ErrItemNotFound); the engine must set sc.Exp=2h and this is pinned by TestLayerDDHTClusterRoundTrip and s12's indexers_responded≥1 assertion

Layer-D publishes only keywords from Tokenize(torrent.Name), not extracted content — s12 must query 'corpus' (from name testbed-swarm-corpus), while Layer-L/S scenarios query the content marker 'aethergram'; a rewrite that queries the content marker over DHT will always get zero hits

The swarm fixture is deliberately 4 MiB / 64-KiB pieces because the 3-KiB fixture transfers in <1s and anacrolix tears down connections at completion, making active_peers/capable_peers unobservable; s6 therefore polls at 100ms and asserts on PEAK active_peers captured during the transfer window, not post-completion snapshots, and s7 only requires capable_peers≥1 on the querier (seeds drop LTEP state after leeches finish)
s7 waits on /index/stats content_count>0 rather than indexed_files==files, explicitly so the test does not hinge on the exact chunker output count (which changes if DefaultChunkTargetBytes changes)
s10 treats 'leech already at progress=1 before the churn trigger' as a graceful exit-0 skip, not a failure — there is no mid-transfer window to test

s11's vanilla client runs with --no-pex specifically so a success can only be attributed to the x.pe= hints (PEX could mask a broken hint path); --no-dht matches the swarm's policy; --no-seed makes the container exit after verify so the scenario can poll for exit code 0

Teardown must use `docker compose --profile '*' down -v` — plain `down -v` leaves profile-gated containers (leech-5, vanilla-leech) running, which holds the bridge network and fails removal with 'Resource is still in use'

The `swarm` alias runs the s6 and s7 assertion scripts against ONE compose lifecycle (log file named s6-<ts>.log); `all` = s1..s5, swarm, s8, s9, s10, s11, s12; extras still run after a primary failure so the log captures everything, with exit = max of all codes

testlab clusters always set Seed=true, NoUpload=false (anacrolix won't serve data otherwise) and Regtest=true (production timers → seconds; the F3 companion scenario would otherwise wait 3600s for its first refresh tick)

Cluster nodes join a shared 'swarm' by bare infohash (AddInfoHash, not AddTorrentMetaInfo) with NO metadata or payload anywhere — the LTEP handshake (which sn_search rides on) fires before metadata exchange, so the mesh handshakes even though the metadata fetch never completes; over a DHT-only path this mesh does NOT converge (nothing announces the fake infohash) so DHT tests must still call WireMesh explicitly

readers.purpose: This area is SwartzNet's design memory: the milestone ledger, pre-v1 blocker research with verdicts, a Bitcoin-Core pattern adopt/reject analysis, the approved "Aggregate" redesign of the distributed layer (proposal + byte-level spec + roadmap + milestone report), four protocol research surveys, overnight test-harness session notes, and two whole-codebase security review campaigns with their fix accounting. It records what was planned, what was deliberately rejected (and why), what shipped, and what remains deferred — the docs double as external wire specs, so a rewrite must treat them as contracts, not commentary.

capabilities.behavior: Milestone ledger maps every shipped feature to a milestone M1→v0.7.0 (torrent engine, Bleve Layer L, 18 extractors, sn_search Layer S, BEP-44 Layer D, spam resistance, web UI + Fyne GUI, signed .torrents, trust list, search-by-publisher with schema v2→v3 bump persisting signed_by)

data_models: PPMI (Publisher Pointer Mutable Item): BEP-44 value dict {ih: 20B infohash of index torrent, commit?: 32B SHA256 of canonical record set, topics?: 32B cuckoo digest, ts: unix, next_pk?: 32B reserved for key rotation} at fixed salt SHA256("snet.index"), seq = BEP-44 native monotonic — defined docs/research/PROPOSAL.md:59-78, implemented internal/dhtindex/ppmi.go

SNAGG B-tree companion index file: 16-byte page header (magic "SNAGG\0", version 0x01, kind 0x00 root/0x01 interior/0x02 leaf/0xFF trailer, level, flags, u16 payload_length, 4B reserved-zero); one page per BitTorrent piece (256 KiB - 4 MiB required); root always piece 0, trailer always last piece; keys = lowercased keyword || 0x00 || 20B infohash; trailer = {version, pubkey 32B, seq u64, created_ts, root_piece_index, num_pages, num_records, min_pow_bits, tree_fingerprint 32B, publisher_sig 64B ed25519} — docs/research/SPEC.md:63-158

Record: canonical bencoded dict {pk 32B, kw utf-8 <=64B, ih 20B, t int, pow varint hashcash nonce, sig 64B ed25519 over pk||kw||ih||t||pow}; whole record bounded at 256 bytes by construction — SPEC.md:112-133
RIBLT element ID: record_id = SHA256(pk||kw||ih||t)[:32] — deliberately excludes pow and sig so re-signings dedupe — SPEC.md:292-302

sync wire messages 4-8: sync_begin {txid, algo:"riblt-v1", filter{pubkeys required, since?, prefix?}, element_size:32, local_count, max_symbols, max_bytes}; sync_symbols {symbols[<=100]{c:i32, h:u64, b:32B}, done, index}; sync_need {ids[<=1000]}; sync_records {records[<=500], missing[]}; sync_end {status converged|limit_exceeded|aborted, decoded, sent, bytes_in, bytes_out, abort_code} — SPEC.md:264-398

nonobvious_rules.rule: Mainline compatibility is the load-bearing constraint: no new reserved bits, no new DHT verbs, no new UDP ports; every extension must live in the LTEP extension space, BEP-44 value payloads, the BEP-11 flag byte, or ordinary torrents. Multiple attractive designs (BitSwap, GossipSub, iroh-blobs, HyParView, relays, Tapestry publish-along-path, Autobase) were rejected on this ground alone
RIBLT record_id excludes pow and sig: two valid signings of the same semantic record must produce the same ID so reconciliation converges globally

B-tree builds must be byte-deterministic: identical input records must yield byte-identical files, hence identical infohash and PPMI commit — this is what makes RIBLT convergence coherent; a rewrite that changes page-fill order silently breaks the network
BEP-44 publish budget: hard cap 1 put/key/hour (MinPutInterval 55 min in code) because BEP-44 TTL is 2h with 1h re-announce; manual refreshes violating this must be rejected
Bans/misbehavior scores are strictly local, NEVER gossiped — sharing bans is a DoS vector letting adversaries eclipse victims (Bitcoin banman lesson)
Unknown service bits MUST be ignored, never rejected — the invariant that makes the 64-bit sn_search capabilities bitfield additive-forever; the documented bit table never shrinks
Peers without services bit 9 (BitSetReconciliation) MUST NOT receive msg_types 4-8; receiving one when unsupported yields reject code 2

Sync rate limits are config knobs, not wire constraints: 1 active sync session per TCP connection, 1 initiation per peer per 5 min, 10 MB sync_records per peer per hour, default max_symbols 2000 / max_bytes 1 MiB
Reputation seed bonus decays exponentially with a 90-day half-life so organic trust dominates after one quarter; puzzle/WoT bootstrap was explicitly rejected (Freenet's decade of data: users hate it)

Ephemeral publisher keys are rejected by design — they destroy the reputation system; the long-term plan is Tor-v3-style rotation under a stable root via the reserved next_pk PPMI field (schema-only, no rotation logic)
Planned SOCKS5 proxying is scoped to the BEP-44 put path ONLY, never torrent swarm traffic, 'to avoid Tor Project ire over bulk traffic'; Tor and I2P daemon integration are both explicitly rejected

peer_announce includes the publisher pk only when caps.Publisher==1 — pure subscribers must not pollute peers' indexer sets; gossip-learned pubkeys are labelled "gossip:<peer_addr>" for ops traceability

Cold-start admission policy: a crawled publisher is admitted iff PoW >= min bits AND (>=2 hits in local known-good Bloom OR >=1 hit matching an anchor index); endorsement shortcut: a pubkey endorsed by 3+ peers each with reputation > 0.5 bypasses the Bloom gate; followed-publisher cap 100; anchors seed at score 0.8
The HTTPS bootstrap fallback serves pubkeys only, never records, so compromising it can only delay bootstrap, not poison the index
Bleve Store=true on the text field is a deliberate v1 tradeoff (snippet highlighting over 3-5x disk) — the 7-12x index-bloat horror stories are all Store=true artifacts, not scorch
Hashcash minted at D=0 during the dual-read migration window even though MinPoWBitsDefault=20; readers enforce trailer min_pow_bits, so bumping D is a coordinated schema bump, not a flag flip
Legacy per-keyword BEP-44 read compatibility must be retained >= 12 months after Aggregate; old items are left to expire via TTL rather than actively deleted

Fail-closed on state transitions is a project-level production rule the review campaigns enforce: a put reaching zero DHT nodes must not record success; 'declared but unenforced limits' were treated as blocking-class findings twice

Proof-of-Work consensus, mining, fee markets, BIP9 soft-fork machinery, chain reorg handling are explicitly rejected as wrong-problem — 'Take the peer layer. Leave the chain.' is the canonical framing for any future 'should we copy X from Bitcoin' question
indexed_files counts all processed files (extracted + skipped + failed), not just text-yielding ones — binary files that produce zero chunks still increment it; index_extracted counts the text subset

snet.pubkey/snet.sig must remain TOP-LEVEL metainfo fields (signing binds the infohash, so they cannot live inside the info dict without recursion) — this deliberately trades away BEP-9 crawlability of signatures

readers.purpose: Defines the repo's two automated pipelines: test.yml is the merge gate that runs hygiene checks (go.mod tidiness, gofmt -s, go vet) plus a race-enabled test sweep on every push/PR to main; release.yml turns any pushed v* tag into a GitHub Release carrying 5 static CLI binaries, 4 CGo GUI binaries, a unified SHA256SUMS, and release notes extracted from CHANGELOG.md. Together they are the only automation surface — .github/workflows contains exactly these two files.

capabilities.behavior: Merge gate runs on every push to main and every PR targeting main; a single ubuntu-latest job named 'go test -race' must pass.
CI fails if `go mod tidy` would change go.mod or go.sum (tidiness is enforced via `git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum` after running tidy).
CI fails with a GitHub `::error::` annotation listing files if `gofmt -l -s` reports anything under cmd/ or internal/ (only those two trees are checked).
CI runs `go vet ./...` over the whole module, including the Fyne GUI package — which is why the job first apt-installs gcc + OpenGL/X11/xkbcommon dev headers.

CI runs `go test -race -count=1` over every module package EXCEPT internal/testlab (filtered via `go list ./... | grep -v '/internal/testlab$'`), with a 15-minute step timeout; testlab integration scenarios are documented as local-only (`go test -race ./internal/testlab/...`).
Pushing any tag matching `v*` triggers the release pipeline; no other event does.

build-cli job invokes scripts/build-release.sh with the tag name, producing 5 pure-Go static CLI binaries (linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-amd64, darwin-arm64, windows-amd64.exe) named swartznet-<tag>-<suffix>, each built with CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, and -ldflags '-s -w -X main.Version=<tag>', plus a SHA256SUMS file; uploaded as artifact 'cli-binaries' (7-day retention).
build-gui-linux job builds the Fyne GUI natively on ubuntu-latest with CGO_ENABLED=1 after apt-installing gcc/libgl1-mesa-dev/xorg-dev/libxkbcommon-dev, producing swartznet-gui-<tag>-linux-amd64.

build-gui-darwin job builds BOTH darwin-arm64 (native) and darwin-amd64 (cross-compiled with CC='clang -arch x86_64' CXX='clang++ -arch x86_64' GOOS=darwin GOARCH=amd64) on a single macos-latest arm64 runner.
build-gui-windows job builds swartznet-gui-<tag>-windows-amd64.exe natively on windows-latest, using `shell: bash` for the build step.

publish job (gated on all four build jobs) downloads all artifacts, copies only files matching name 'swartznet*' into release/ (deliberately dropping the CLI-only SHA256SUMS), and regenerates a single SHA256SUMS covering CLI + all GUI binaries.

Release notes are extracted from CHANGELOG.md as the text between the `## <tag>` heading and the next `## ` heading (awk); if the section is missing/empty, the body falls back to the literal 'See CHANGELOG.md for details.'

A GitHub Release is created via softprops/action-gh-release@v2 named exactly the tag, with body from the extracted notes, attaching release/swartznet-<tag>-*, release/swartznet-gui-<tag>-*, and release/SHA256SUMS; tags starting with 'v0.' are flagged prerelease.
The workflow token is granted `contents: write` solely so the publish job can create the Release and upload assets.

CHANGELOG.md release-notes contract: per-release sections headed `## vX.Y.Z` (in practice `## vX.Y.Z — YYYY-MM-DD`, e.g. CHANGELOG.md:1279); the awk extractor matches the tag as a regex substring of the heading line and prints until the next `^## ` line (release.yml:172-176).

nonobvious_rules.rule: internal/testlab is deliberately excluded from CI tests (multi-client loopback scenarios with real piece-verify are unreliable on shared runners) — but the exclusion grep is end-anchored (`/internal/testlab$`), so any future testlab SUBpackage would silently run in CI. Currently testlab has no subpackages.

gofmt is scoped to cmd/ and internal/ only, because research/ holds vendored upstream clones (libtorrent, transmission, anacrolix/torrent, tribler) that must not be reformatted or gate CI. go vet/test naturally exclude research/anacrolix-torrent because it has its own go.mod, but gofmt would recurse into it — hence the explicit path scoping.

The merge-gate job installs Fyne C build deps even though it never builds a GUI binary — `go vet ./...` and the test sweep must compile cmd/swartznet-gui and internal/gui, which need CGo + OpenGL/X11 headers. Removing the apt step breaks vet, not just builds.

darwin-amd64 GUI is cross-compiled from the arm64 macos-latest runner using CC='clang -arch x86_64' because GitHub retired the macos-13 Intel runner in April 2026; a rewrite must not reintroduce a macos-13 matrix leg.

The publish job's `find artifacts -type f -name 'swartznet*'` intentionally excludes the CLI-only SHA256SUMS from build-cli; a fresh SHA256SUMS covering all 9 binaries is regenerated in release/ and that regenerated file is what ships. Verification tooling must expect GUI entries in the released SHA256SUMS.

Prerelease flag is purely lexical: any tag starting with 'v0.' is a prerelease; everything else (including hypothetical 'v1.0.0-rc1', which still matches the 'v*' trigger) publishes as a full release.

The CHANGELOG extractor treats '## <tag>' as an awk REGEX matched anywhere in the line ($0 ~ tag) — this substring semantics is load-bearing because real headings carry a date suffix ('## v0.7.0 — 2026-04-13'); an exact-equality rewrite would break every release. Side effects: dots in the tag match any character, and the tag's own heading line is consumed (never printed).
Missing CHANGELOG section is a supported, non-fatal path: empty extraction falls back to the literal body 'See CHANGELOG.md for details.' (comment says this is for hotfix tags).

CLI binaries must stay fully static: CGO_ENABLED=0 is forced in build-release.sh precisely so there is no glibc/musl dependency, and the 5-target matrix (including linux-arm64, which has NO GUI counterpart) lives only in that script — CI inherits it by delegation.

All release binaries are built with -trimpath and stripped ('-s -w'), and get the tag injected as main.Version; source defaults for Version track the latest released tag and are bumped in the same commit that cuts a release (so go-run shows something meaningful).
Tests run with -count=1 (cache-busting) and -race; only the test step has the 15-minute timeout — vet/fmt/tidy run under the default job timeout.
The Windows GUI build step explicitly sets `shell: bash` — the multi-line env-var + backslash-continuation syntax would fail under the default PowerShell.
setup-go pins '1.24' (floating latest patch) with module caching in all four jobs, while go.mod pins 1.24.1 — CI intentionally rides the 1.24.x patch train.
build-release.sh deletes any previous dist/ outputs for the same version (and SHA256SUMS) before building, so re-runs are clean; it exits 2 on wrong argument count.

nonobvious_rules.rule: MPL discipline is architectural, not just legal: because MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft, any change inside anacrolix files must be published MPL, so the project deliberately routes ALL integration through extension APIs (piece callbacks, LocalLtepProtocolMap.AddUserProtocol, direct DHT library access) and keeps zero patches. Stated motive includes retaining the option to 'ship a proprietary product'. A rewrite that patches the engine directly breaks both the license posture and the stated design forcing-function.
nonobvious_rules.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:20,172; CLAUDE.md:76; docs/reviews/2026-06-06-whole-codebase-review.md:106 ('no vendored patches, respecting MPL')

nonobvious_rules.rule: ledongthuc/pdf is BSD-3-Clause, NOT MIT — earlier project docs mis-attributed it as MIT and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES self-declares 'this file is the authoritative attribution', overriding all other documentation. A rewrite regenerating attribution from stale docs would silently reintroduce the M13a bug.

Full license text is reproduced only for the BSD-3-Clause deps (ledongthuc/pdf, golang.org/x/net) — because the BSD binary-redistribution clause requires reproducing the notice 'in the documentation and/or other materials' — while MPL-2.0, Apache-2.0, and even stdlib BSD entries are referenced by URL only. The asymmetry is the point of the file, not sloppiness.

The copyleft-free guarantee is deliberately version-pinned ('As of v0.3.0 the extractor hot path ... is entirely covered by the entries above plus the Go standard library') rather than stated timelessly — a hedge that makes the sentence technically true even as the extractor set grows, though nothing else in the file reads as historical.

The project license itself was a late decision: the original agent brief said the project was MPL-2.0; the actual LICENSE is Apache-2.0, and docs/09 explicitly reasons the Blocker-5 audit conclusions 'still hold ... with even more headroom' under Apache-2.0. Historical docs may therefore describe the project as MPL.

GPL/LGPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL/CDDL/EPL extractor dependencies are a standing prohibition, not a one-time check — future format support must pick MPL/Apache-compatible libs or be built in-house (this is why archive.go stops at stdlib-supported formats and why post-v1 candidates were license-screened).
Copyright identity is 'The SwartzNet Authors', year 2026, with no CLA/DCO machinery and contributions accepted under Apache-2.0 §5 defaults.

CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md speak of 'the vendored library', but there is no vendor/ directory — anacrolix/torrent is a normal Go module dependency, and the full-source clones under research/torrent-clients/ are reference-only reading material, not build inputs. The 'no patches' rule is enforced by not forking, not by vendor-tree hygiene.

readers.area: gap:Second regtest env gate and GUI logging env
readers.purpose: This area implements the fail-closed safety layers around the two production-dangerous test knobs (Regtest fast-forward timings and DHTInsecure/BEP-42-off), which exist in TWO independent layers with TWO different env vars: a CLI argument gate (SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 in `swartznet add`) and a config-validation gate (SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 or go-test auto-detection in Config.Validate, hit by every frontend via engine.New). It also covers env-driven slog level control (SWARTZNET_LOG), which is honored by BOTH the CLI and the GUI binary via duplicated newLogger implementations, and the GUI's config layering (defaults -> saved config.json overrides -> CLI flags).

capabilities.behavior: Config-level fail-closed gate: any attempt to construct an engine with cfg.Regtest or cfg.DHTInsecure set fails with error 'config: Regtest/DHTInsecure are test-only knobs; set SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 to use them outside tests' UNLESS the process is a `go test` binary (testing.Testing()) OR env SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST is exactly "1". This is the universal chokepoint — all three frontends pass through it because engine.New calls cfg.Validate.

CLI-level gate in `swartznet add`: passing --regtest or --dht-insecure without env SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 prints a per-flag stderr message ('--regtest is a testing-only flag (set SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 to enable)' / '--dht-insecure disables BEP-42 node-ID security and is testing-only...') and exits with usage code, before any daemon is constructed. This gate exists ONLY in cmd_add.go — no other subcommand exposes these flags.

In a production (non-test) binary, running `swartznet add --regtest` requires BOTH env vars: SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 to pass the CLI gate, then SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 to pass Config.Validate inside daemon.New. Setting only SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 gets past arg parsing but daemon.New still errors out.
capabilities.evidence: cmd/swartznet/cmd_add.go:65 + internal/config/config.go:295 (independent checks, different env names)

capabilities.behavior: GUI binary honors SWARTZNET_LOG env var for slog level: "debug"->Debug, "warn"->Warn, "error"->Error, anything else (including "info", empty, garbage) -> Info; logs are slog text-handler to stderr. The CLI binary has an identical, separately-maintained copy of this function.

GUI cannot set the dangerous knobs at all: swartznet-gui exposes only --data-dir, --index-dir, --port, --no-dht, --no-dht-publish, --api-addr, --torrent (repeatable), --tab; and the persisted config.json override whitelist (userConfigOverrides) admits only data_dir/index_dir, so a stray config.json cannot inject Regtest/DHTInsecure through the GUI either.

GUI config layering: config.Default() first, then GUI-saved overrides from config.DefaultUserConfigPath() (~/.local/share/swartznet/config.json) for DataDir/IndexDir, then CLI flags win over both. A malformed saved config prints 'warning: load saved config: ...' to stderr and continues on defaults; a missing file is silently fine.

SaveUserOverrides persists GUI Settings-tab edits as pretty-printed JSON atomically (write path+".tmp" then rename, removing tmp on rename failure); empty fields are omitted (omitempty) so next launch falls back to Default() rather than locking in blank strings.

Config.Validate has side effects: it creates DataDir (MkdirAll 0755) and the PARENT of IndexDir (Bleve creates the leaf itself); it rejects empty DataDir and ListenPort outside 0-65535. Directory creation happens BEFORE the dangerous-flags check, so a rejected regtest config still creates DataDir on disk.

config.Default() supplies all XDG-aware paths under swartznetShareRoot() ($XDG_DATA_HOME/swartznet, else ~/.local/share/swartznet, else ./swartznet-state): data/, index/, identity.key, publisher.json, reputation.json, seeds.json, known-good.bloom, companion/, companion-follows.json, trust.json; ListenPort defaults to 42069 (matching anacrolix default 'to reduce port surprise'); Seed=true.

`swartznet add <magnet|path.torrent>` (the smoke-test command): dispatches on 'magnet:' prefix, prints companion publisher/subscriber and HTTP-API startup lines, waits up to 5 minutes for metadata (else error; Ctrl-C exits with interrupt code), prints Name/Hash/Size/Pieces and up to 20 file names ('... and N more'), calls DownloadAll, then runs a 3-second-ticker progress loop printing '[HH:MM:SS] pct% have/total peers=a/t piece-events=N files-done=N' plus inline '✓ file complete: path (size)' lines from an independent file-events subscription; exits cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

GUI --torrent flag (repeatable) auto-loads .torrent files at startup via Eng.AddTorrentFile, printing 'Loaded <path>' per success and 'warning: load <path>: err' per failure (continues on failure); --tab selects the startup tab (downloads|search|status|companion|settings); GUI exits 0 after the Fyne loop ends, 1 on daemon.New failure, 2 on flag-parse failure.

GUI Version defaults to 'v0.8.0' (bumped per release so go-run launches show a meaningful version); BuildDate empty means the About dialog shows '(dev build)' — both overridable via -ldflags by build-gui.sh/build-release.sh.

inputs_outputs: Env vars in: SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST (config gate, exact string "1"), SWARTZNET_UNSAFE (CLI add gate, exact string "1"), SWARTZNET_LOG (debug|warn|error, both binaries), XDG_DATA_HOME + HOME (path resolution, config.go:442-449)

external_deps: stdlib testing package imported by PRODUCTION config code solely for testing.Testing() (Go 1.21+) test-binary detection (config.go:15,277)
log/slog with TextHandler for both binaries' logging
internal/daemon (daemon.New wires everything; both frontends differ only in Options), internal/engine (engine.New is where Validate is enforced), internal/gui (Fyne UI, receives the Daemon)

BEP-42 (DHT node-ID security — what DHTInsecure disables), BEP-44 (mutable-item puts whose cadence Regtest accelerates), BEP-46 (companion pointer republish cadence, also accelerated); the gates exist to protect mainline from these accelerations
anacrolix/torrent conventions leak in: default ListenPort 42069 chosen to match anacrolix; ListenHost empty delegates to anacrolix default 0.0.0.0 (config.go:38-50,234)

nonobvious_rules.rule: There are TWO distinct env-var gates for the same two knobs, and a production binary needs BOTH: SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 (arg-parse layer, only in `add`) and SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 (config layer, all frontends). They came from two separate review findings (docs/reviews/2026-06-06-whole-codebase-findings.json:506 proposed SWARTZNET_UNSAFE; :616 proposed SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST) implemented independently. A rewrite that unifies them to one var changes operator-visible behavior.
Both gates match the exact string "1" — SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=true or SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=yes do NOT unlock anything.

Any `go test` binary silently bypasses the config-layer gate via testing.Testing() — this is how internal/testlab sets Regtest=true on every spawned engine with no env vars. The boolean is threaded into dangerousFlagsRejected(inTest) as a parameter specifically so the production branch is unit-testable from inside a test binary.
Production package internal/config imports "testing" — looks like a mistake but is the deliberate mechanism for test-binary detection.

Validate's directory-creation side effects (MkdirAll DataDir, MkdirAll parent-of-IndexDir) run BEFORE the dangerous-flags rejection, so even a refused regtest config creates DataDir on disk. IndexDir itself is deliberately NOT created — 'Bleve itself creates the leaf'.

SWARTZNET_LOG switch has no "info" case — "info", empty, and unknown values all fall through to LevelInfo. The function is duplicated verbatim in cmd/swartznet/main.go and cmd/swartznet-gui/main.go and the two copies must stay behavior-identical.

GUI precedence chain is defaults < saved config.json < CLI flags, and only DataDir/IndexDir are persistable — the whitelist is intentionally narrow ('changing the BitTorrent listen port... via a JSON file surprises operators'); it also happens to be a second line of defense keeping Regtest/DHTInsecure out of GUI reach.
Both binaries use port flag default -1 as the 'not set' sentinel because 0 is a meaningful value (OS-assigned port); only port >= 0 overrides the config.

add's --no-index does NOT set cfg.NoIndex; it is passed as daemon.Options.NoIndex and the daemon 'copies the flag down' so the engine sees a consistent view — Config.NoIndex and Options.NoIndex are dual representations of one setting.

Regtest's exact acceleration constants are contract: dhtindex RefreshInterval 1h->5s, MinPutInterval 55m->100ms, companion Interval 1h->10s, MinInterval 1m->100ms; same code paths as production, no mocks; engine logs 'engine.regtest_mode_active' at Warn on startup — but the comment explicitly says a logged warning is not enough, hence the hard Validate rejection.

The gate error strings are operator-facing contracts: the config gate names SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST, the CLI gate names SWARTZNET_UNSAFE — each message only tells the operator about ITS OWN env var, so an operator following the CLI hint still hits the second gate with a different var name.

add's metadata wait has a hard 5-minute timeout; file lists print at most 20 entries then '... and N more'; progress ticks every 3s; a closed file-events channel keeps the loop alive until ctx cancels rather than exiting.

broken_or_unfinished.issue: The entire Docker testbed appears broken by the gates: every compose service and the Dockerfile CMD run `swartznet add --regtest` (docker-compose.dht.yml also adds --dht-insecure) but NOTHING sets SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 or SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 — not the compose environment blocks, not the Dockerfile ENV, not entrypoint.sh (which just exec's "$@"). As written, containers exit at the cmd_add gate with the usage error; even if UNSAFE=1 were added, the config gate would reject next. The gates were added in the 2026-06 review campaign after the testbed was written.

readers.area: gap:Unclaimed docs: docs/README.md and pre-design research reports 01-04
readers.purpose: docs/README.md is the audience-routed index of the whole doc set and the spec-of-record classifier: it declares docs 06/07/11 to be self-contained, normative BEP-style protocol specs (the Go code is explicitly the "reference implementation"), 05 the architecture synthesis, 08 the ops manual, and 01-04/09/10 background rationale. Docs 01-04 are the pre-M1 research reports that produced every load-bearing design commitment: pick anacrolix/torrent as the engine (01), copy Tribler's engine/search-overlay separation but reject its flood-query model (02), adopt aMule-style keyword->infohash DHT indexing hardened with Bloom-filter + publisher-reputation filtering (03), and build exclusively on BEP-10 LTEP + BEP-44 mutable items with exact byte-level wire formats and interop rules (04). Doc 04 in particular is the direct ancestor of the sn_search and DHT-keyword-index specs, including message-type numbering, salt-sharding convention, and the mainline-compatibility rules restated in CLAUDE.md.

capabilities.behavior: Routes readers by audience (user / protocol implementer / architect / historian) to the right documents in reading order; a third-party implementer is told docs 06, 07, 11 are each 'a self-contained, BEP-style specification' sufficient to 'produce a wire-compatible peer in any language', making those three files the normative wire contract and the repo merely the reference implementation

Classifies 05-integration-design.md as the synthesis document (three-layer architecture, wire format, daemon layer, ingestion, threat model, backwards-compat test matrix, roadmap) and 08-operations.md as the sole user-facing manual

Frames docs 01-04 plus 09-10 as the 'why we made the choices we did' record, each standalone and readable in any order, with one-line verdicts (01 concludes anacrolix/torrent; 02 names Tribler as closest prior art; 03 identifies aMule's keyword-hash DHT as the most applicable pattern; 04 catalogs every relevant BEP with byte-level walkthroughs)

Doc 01 scores five torrent stacks (libtorrent 6.5, Transmission 2, anacrolix/torrent 9.5, rqbit 5, WebTorrent 3) on BEP-10 extension API, piece-verify hooks, BEP-44 access, license, maintainability, and commits the project to anacrolix/torrent via extension-API-only integration (LocalLtepProtocolMap.AddUserProtocol, PeerConnReadExtensionMessage callbacks, WriteExtendedMessage, piece-completion callbacks) with a 4-phase roadmap (extension registration -> message handler -> piece indexer -> DHT publication) that matches the shipped Layer-S/Layer-L/Layer-D split

Doc 02 reverse-engineers Tribler end-to-end (IPv8 ContentDiscoveryCommunity, msg_id 201/202 RemoteSelect/SelectResponse, LZ4-compressed signed TorrentMetadata, SQLite FTS5 title-only index, flood-to-20-random-peers) and issues reuse/rewrite verdicts: keep the engine/search-overlay separation and signed-metadata idea, rewrite query routing, ranking, and spam handling; its closing lesson ('decentralization without a metadata location mechanism means flooding random subsets') is the stated reason SwartzNet integrates with DHT instead

Doc 03 surveys aMule/Kad, GNUnet, Gnutella, RetroShare, YaCy, Freenet on search primitive, routing, index structure, publisher model, scalability, and anonymity, then recommends the staged plan the project follows: Phase 1 aMule-style keyword->infohash DHT index, Phase 2 publisher reputation + local filtering, Phase 3 optional encrypted index, Phase 4 ML/semantic extras; its hybrid blueprint (DHT index + known-good-infohash Bloom filter + per-publisher reputation scoring with results ranked BF-hit > high-rep > low-rep > dropped) is the design implemented as known-good.bloom + reputation.json

Doc 03 also drafts the security posture: expect spam from day one, per-IP rate limiting on keyword nodes, 24h TTL with republish, min-3-char keyword filtering, multi-word queries resolved by single-keyword DHT lookup plus client-side intersection, and publisher-ID-in-every-result so reputation is trackable

Doc 04 catalogs every BEP the design touches (3,4,5,9,10,11,14,18,42,43,44,46,49,51,52 + drafts 32/33/36/55) with a use-verdict table, and provides byte-exact walkthroughs a wire-compatible reimplementation can be built from: the 68-byte BEP-3 handshake with LTEP bit reserved[5]&0x10, the LTEP ID-20 frame envelope, per-direction m-dictionary ID negotiation, hex-dumped example query frames, and the full BEP-44 get-token->put->refresh cycle including the literal signing-buffer byte string

Doc 04 defines the search extension's inner message scheme (bencoded payload with msg_type discriminator: 0=query, 1=result, 2=reject, txid correlation, hits carrying 20-byte 'ih' + name + score) that the shipped sn_search spec preserved verbatim for types 0-2 before appending types 3 (peer_announce) and 4-8 (sync)

Doc 04 specifies the DHT keyword-index storage convention adopted by doc 07: per-publisher ed25519 keypair, salt = keyword, target = SHA1(pubkey||salt), value schema of timestamp + list of 20-byte infohashes (~40-45 per 1000-byte item), shard overflow via salts 'keyword#1', 'keyword#2'... with a root item at the bare keyword, hourly refresh, CAS-guarded read-modify-write for appends, and BEP-46-style pointer items to 'index torrents' when in-band storage overflows (the shipped companion-index pattern)

Doc 04 states the interoperability contract (section 5) later formalized as the wire-compat test matrix: vanilla clients must be able to download from us and vice versa; search messages only ever sent to peers that advertised the extension; DHT participation (ping/find_node/get_peers/announce_peer) unaffected; a vanilla client observing us sees only standard BEP-3/5/10 traffic plus one ignorable name in the m dict

Doc 04 records the standardization strategy: ship in own client first, publish own spec docs, get a second implementation ('tested in live swarms'), only then submit a BEP; and picks the extension name prefix 'sn_' (sn_search) because 'lt_' is historically libtorrent's - the first place the SwartzNet name appears on a wire example is its handshake v-string 'SwartzNet 0.1'
