nonobvious_rules.rule: Never claim a new BEP-3 reserved handshake bit; capability is announced only through the BEP-10 'm' dictionary (BEP-4's own recommendation). This is the root of the 'no new reserved bit' constraint in CLAUDE.md

Extended message IDs are per-direction and per-peer: each side picks arbitrary numeric IDs for the extensions it is willing to RECEIVE, and the sender must use the receiver's advertised number; the two directions normally use different numbers for the same extension

Unknown extended message IDs are dropped silently ('drop unknown' is the universal LTEP rule); never send a search message to a peer that did not advertise the extension, and never signal an error about its absence - this is how invisibility to vanilla clients is achieved

No new DHT verb (Option A chosen over Option B) and no second UDP port / second DHT: the keyword index rides standard BEP-44 get/put so any vanilla BEP-44 node stores it; a new verb would fragment on node density. If a verb were ever added, unknown-method must degrade to classic routing, not fail

The 'capable subset' of search-aware DHT/peer nodes is a VIEW over the full routing table, never a separate routing table - polluting the routing table with capable-only entries is explicitly forbidden; capable peers are pre-seeded from BEP-10 sessions that advertised the search extension

BEP-44 mechanics a rewrite must preserve exactly: bencoded v <= 1000 bytes (error 205), salt <= 64 bytes (207), strictly monotonic seq with no-downgrade list-head semantics (302), ed25519 signature over the literal buffer '4:salt<len>:<salt>3:seqi<seq>e1:v<len>:<v>' (206), CAS field for racing publishers (301), get-before-put write tokens, ~1h republish against ~2h expiry

BEP-44 has no append primitive, so 'add an infohash to a keyword' is a CAS-guarded read-modify-write, and crowdsourced contribution requires one keypair per contributor with searchers doing one GET per (pubkey, keyword) and unioning across trusted indexer pubkeys - multi-publisher aggregation is a client-side trust decision, not a protocol feature

Shard-overflow salt convention: shard 0 lives at the bare keyword, overflow shards at 'keyword#1', 'keyword#2', ...; readers fetch the root first then fan out. Proposed in doc 04 and shipped unchanged in doc 07

Inner message-type numbering 0=query, 1=result, 2=reject with txid request-correlation was fixed in doc 04 and is frozen in the shipped sn_search spec (which appended 3=peer_announce, 4-8=sync); renumbering breaks wire compatibility

Extension naming is by convention, not registry: the 'lt_' prefix belongs to libtorrent, so the project must use its own two-character prefix - 'sn_search'. Doc 04's worked examples all say 'lt_search' but the closing section overrides the name

BEP-42 (node ID derived from IP via crc32c) and BEP-43 (honor ro:1, don't table read-only nodes) must be obeyed by any node holding index data, or modern clients evict it from routing tables and the index becomes unreachable
BEP-14's multicast verb is literally 'BT-SEARCH' but is LAN peer discovery, historically named, and unrelated to text search - 'do not confuse them'
BEP-18 already occupies the 'search engine' BEP number with a deferred centralized OpenSearch-style spec; any future SwartzNet BEP gets a new number and may want to mark BEP-18 obsoleted-in-spirit

Standardization path is deliberately deferred: ship in own client, publish own spec docs (docs 06/07/11 are exactly this artifact), get a second independent implementation ('tested in live swarms'), only then submit a BEP draft

Search-hit records should be designed to optionally carry a BEP-52 per-file merkle root ('pr') alongside the torrent infohash ('ih') so future versions can deduplicate the same file across repackaged torrents

Spam defense is an application-layer responsibility by design (DHT stores are unauthenticated): known-good-infohash Bloom filter + per-publisher reputation, results ranked BF-hit > high-rep publisher > low-rep > dropped, publisher ID mandatory in results, entries TTL-expired to force active republishing - decided before any code was written ('plan for spam from day one; design filtering first')
Multi-word search is resolved by hashing/looking up a single keyword in the DHT and doing intersection/filtering client-side; AND/OR must never be pushed into the DHT itself

docs/README.md's classification is itself normative: implementers are directed to read ONLY 06/07/11 end-to-end to build a wire-compatible peer, so any wire-format change must land in those files (CLAUDE.md restates this as 'if you touch wire format, keep those specs in sync')

xchecks.summary: Cross-checked README.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs 05/06/07/08/11 against the code. Core wire-compat, signing (SN-TORRENT-V1 payload, 0600 identity gate, ErrNotSigned/ErrBadSignature semantics), paths/XDG defaults, HTTP API surface, services bits, reject codes, hit-cache size, tokenizer rules, PPMI fields, 32 MiB companion cap, and recent CHANGELOG fixes (content_name, seed-in-place, --no-index cascade) all check out and are not listed. 18 discrepancies were found: stale wire-format text in doc 05 §5, doc 06's peer_announce schema missing implemented `pk`/`endorsed` fields, rate-limit defaults that don't match the token-bucket implementation, unimplemented DHT keyword sharding despite spec MUSTs, first-token (not longest-token) DHT lookup, unconditional Layer-D refresh, a publisher subsystem (priority queue / 5 puts-s / backoff / stats file) that was never built, missing lingua-go language detection, missing index encryption, missing deny-glob, 2 KiB (not 10 KB) chunks, no sha256-keyed extraction idempotency, no drop+hourly-rescan overflow path, a rank formula that is just Bleve-score×1000, an L1 sharing level that rejects everything, a Go 1.22 build claim vs a go.mod pin of 1.24.1, a "not yet implemented" note for a CLI command that ships, and a stale extractor count.

findings.title: Doc 05 §5 documents a retired sn_search wire format (sn_search_v / sn_search_cap handshake keys, peer_announce as an ip/port/cap/pk gossip list)
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md §5.1 (lines 394-419) says the LTEP handshake carries `sn_search_v` and `sn_search_cap` ("L0F0C0P0" cap string), and §5.2.4 (lines 507-519) defines peer_announce (msg_type 3) as a gossip list of other peers `{ip, port, cap, pk}`. Neither exists in code: capability negotiation is a per-connection self-announcement carrying `v` + a 64-bit `services` bitfield, exactly as the newer spec docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md (lines 100-138, 259-291, which explicitly notes the M15b retirement of the old schema) describes. No Go source sets sn_search_v/sn_search_cap (the only hit is a historical comment at internal/swarmsearch/protocol.go:23). Doc 05 §5 contradicts both the code and doc 06.
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:407-409,507-519 vs internal/swarmsearch/protocol.go:547-569 (announce built from ServiceBits, no handshake keys) and internal/swarmsearch/wire.go:209-221 (PeerAnnounce = msg_type/v/services/pk/endorsed); docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md:285-291 documents the retirement doc 05 never picked up

findings.title: Doc 06's peer_announce schema omits the implemented `pk` and `endorsed` wire fields
findings.detail: docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md (lines 259-283) defines peer_announce as exactly `{msg_type, v, services}`. The implementation additionally emits and parses `pk` (sender's 32-byte ed25519 publisher key, sent when the Layer-D publisher is on) and `endorsed` (up to 10 32-byte pubkeys, channel-C gossip). docs/05-integration-design.md:673 and docs/07-bep-dht-keyword-index-draft.md:273-277 both describe the `pk` behavior, so the standalone wire spec — which CLAUDE.md requires to be kept in sync with wire changes — is out of date and contradicts the sibling docs and the wire bytes actually sent.
findings.evidence: docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md:261-267 (schema without pk/endorsed) vs internal/swarmsearch/wire.go:209-221 (Pubkey `bencode:"pk"`, Endorsed `bencode:"endorsed"`), internal/swarmsearch/protocol.go:558-568 (pk attached when caps.Publisher==1), internal/swarmsearch/handler.go:124-192 (pk/endorsed consumption)

findings.title: Rate-limit defaults contradict the docs: token bucket 5 queries/sec + burst 10, not "100 queries/hour" / "10/hour for c scope" / one-outstanding-query
findings.detail: docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md asserts under Security Considerations that sn_search provides "Rate-limited responses (default 100 queries/hour; configurable)" (line 389) and lists suggested defaults of one outstanding query per connection (second query MUST get reject code 0), 100/hour for n/f scope and 10/hour for c scope (lines 296-302). docs/05-integration-design.md:539-542 states the same numbers declaratively. The implementation is a per-peer token bucket defaulting to 5 queries/second with burst 10 (= up to 18,000/hour), installed unconditionally in the Protocol constructor; there is no per-scope budget and no outstanding-query serialization anywhere in the handler.
findings.evidence: docs/06-bep-sn_search-draft.md:296-302,389 and docs/05-integration-design.md:539-542 vs internal/swarmsearch/ratelimit.go:32-37 (DefaultRateLimit 5.0 qps / burst 10), internal/swarmsearch/protocol.go:240 (wired in New), internal/swarmsearch/handler.go:655-751 (handleQuery: no scope budget, no outstanding-query tracking)

findings.title: DHT keyword sharding ("more" flag, salts keyword#1, keyword#2, n_shards) is documented as MUST but not implemented
findings.detail: docs/07-bep-dht-keyword-index-draft.md:132-146 says publishers "MUST shard by appending #<n>" and shard 0 SHOULD set `more:1`; line 190 repeats "MUST reject larger payloads at publish time and MUST shard". docs/05-integration-design.md:293-297 describes the same spill with an `n_shards` counter (which exists in no schema). The code explicitly does the opposite: the publisher never sets More, never writes shard 1+, Lookup never follows it, and oversize entries are handled by evicting the oldest hit instead. `n_shards` appears nowhere in the codebase.
findings.evidence: docs/07-bep-dht-keyword-index-draft.md:132-146,190 and docs/05-integration-design.md:293-297 vs internal/dhtindex/schema.go:41-53 ("As of v1 this is NOT implemented: the publisher never sets More and never writes shard 1+, and Lookup never follows it") and schema.go:166-177 (SaltForShard "reserved for the future multi-shard scheme")

findings.title: Layer-D lookup picks the FIRST query token, not "the most distinctive token (longest non-stopword)"
findings.detail: docs/07-bep-dht-keyword-index-draft.md:246-248 specifies searcher behaviour step 2 as "Picks the most distinctive token (longest non-stopword)". The implementation runs Tokenize (which preserves first-appearance order with no length ranking) and takes tokens[0] — the first qualifying token. Searching "new ubuntu" queries the DHT for "new", not "ubuntu". The code comment at lookup.go:259 even (incorrectly) claims tokens[0] is "the longest non-stopword", so doc and comment both misstate the behavior.
findings.evidence: docs/07-bep-dht-keyword-index-draft.md:246-248 vs internal/dhtindex/lookup.go:274-279 (`keyword := tokens[0]`) and internal/dhtindex/tokenize.go:84-124 (appearance-order tokenizer, no length sort)

findings.title: Layer-D refresh policy: docs say only items with activity in the last 24h are refreshed; code refreshes every manifest entry unconditionally
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md:304 states "We only refresh items that have had activity (a download, a seed session) in the last 24 hours; stale items are allowed to expire." The publisher's refresh ticker calls refreshAll, which re-publishes every entry in the manifest every RefreshInterval (1h), gated only by the 55-minute MinPutInterval throttle. There is no activity tracking and entries never expire on their own (they persist until RemoveHit/Retract).
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:304 vs internal/dhtindex/publisher.go:285-298 (refreshAll iterates the whole manifest snapshot) and publisher.go:49-52 (RefreshInterval 1h, MinPutInterval 55m — no activity window)

findings.title: Doc 05 §7 publisher subsystem (priority queue, 5 puts/sec budget, exponential backoff + "unhealthy" daily retry, stats file) was never built
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md §7 claims: (3) a worker draining "a priority queue of (keyword, reason) pairs" with High/Medium/Low priorities (lines 622-626); (4) publishes "rate-limited per-second... Default: 5 puts/second across all keywords" (line 627); (5) failed puts "stay enqueued with exponential backoff. After 3 failures we mark the keyword 'unhealthy' and drop to a daily retry schedule" (line 629); and "The publisher writes stats to /var/log/swartznet/publisher.json" (line 633). Reality: a plain buffered task channel + ticker (no priorities), a per-keyword 55-min MinPutInterval (no global puts/sec budget), MarkFailed just records the last error (no backoff, no unhealthy state, no retry schedule), and publisher.json is the keyword manifest at ~/.local/share/swartznet/publisher.json, not a stats file; nothing writes under /var/log.
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:622-633 vs internal/dhtindex/publisher.go:168-202 (channel+ticker loop), 244-279 (publishOne: MinPutInterval throttle, MarkFailed only), internal/config/config.go:326 (publisher.json = manifest path); repo-wide grep for "/var/log" only matches testlab manifest paths

findings.title: Language detection (lingua-go) and language filtering are documented but absent
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md:237 says "Lang detection via github.com/pemistahl/lingua-go so results can be language-filtered", the §4.1 schema includes `lang: keyword (detected)` (line 224), and the §6 pipeline diagram has a "chunker + lang detect" stage (line 587). lingua-go is not in go.mod, ContentDoc has no Lang field, and no detection code exists — only forward-looking comments ("M5 will replace this ... once lingua-go is integrated"). Relatedly, the sn_search Query's documented `lang`/`min_size`/`max_size`/`not_ih` filter fields (docs/06:180-187) are decoded from the wire but never applied by the responder — handleQuery uses only Q, Scope and Limit.
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:224,237,587 vs go.mod (no lingua dep), internal/indexer/content.go:22-34 (no Lang field), internal/indexer/schema.go:73-74 and internal/dhtindex/tokenize.go:27-30 ("lands with M5" comments); internal/swarmsearch/wire.go:42-45 vs handler.go:655-751 (Lang/MinSize/MaxSize/NotIH never read)

findings.title: Optional index encryption at rest ("AES-256-GCM via age") does not exist

There is no age dependency in go.mod and no encryption/passphrase code anywhere in internal/indexer or internal/config. The Bleve index is stored plaintext with no opt-in alternative.

Per-file override via the UI." findings.title: Content chunk size is 2 KiB, not the ~10 KB the docs state

The chunker was retuned to 2 KiB, and its own comment calls the old 10 KiB target "an order of magnitude larger than the sweet spot". The doc was not updated.
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:224,587 vs internal/indexer/extractors/chunker.go:5-17 (DefaultChunkTargetBytes = 2*1024 with the M13e rationale comment)

findings.title: Extraction idempotency is NOT keyed by file_content_sha256 as documented
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md:600 claims "Extraction is keyed by (infohash, file_index, file_content_sha256). If a file is re-downloaded or a torrent is re-added, we don't re-extract the same content." The Bleve doc ID is c:<infohash>:<file_index>:<chunk_index> — no content hash anywhere in the ingest path (no sha256 in engine.go or the pipeline). Re-adding a torrent re-runs extraction; writes merely overwrite by doc ID. The documented skip-re-extract behavior does not exist.
findings.evidence: docs/05-integration-design.md:600 vs internal/indexer/content.go:36-41 (docID = infohash/fileIndex/chunkIndex only); grep sha256 in internal/engine/engine.go and internal/indexer returns nothing in the ingest path

findings.title: Pipeline overflow handling: docs describe drop-plus-hourly-rescan; code blocks on submit and has no recovery scan
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md:596 says when the capacity-64 extract channel is full, requests are dropped and "a background scan picks up missed files on the next hour." In code, Pipeline.Submit BLOCKS until a slot frees or Stop (internal/indexer/pipeline.go:117-124); actual drops happen one layer up when a file-tracker subscriber buffer overflows (internal/engine/file_tracker.go:74-76,97-106, events "dropped and logged"), and no background/hourly scan exists anywhere to recover them — a dropped file-complete event is simply never indexed. The documented recovery mechanism is unimplemented.

findings.title: Peer-wire rank is raw Bleve score × 1000, not the documented weighted BM25 + seeders + freshness formula
findings.detail: docs/05-integration-design.md §5.3 (lines 523-535) says "We ship a simple default" rank = 0.4·bm25(name) + 0.2·bm25(files) + 0.2·bm25(content) + 0.1·log(seeders+1) + 0.1·freshness, scaled to 0-1000. The responder actually sets Rank = int(bleveScore * 1000) with no seeder or freshness terms and no field weighting; since BM25 scores are unbounded, Rank can also exceed the documented 0-1000 range (doc 06 line 223 also states "0-1000").

xchecks.summary: Scanned all non-vendored Go source in /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet for unfinished-work markers, dead exports, unread config, and swallowed errors. Marker hygiene is excellent: zero TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK, no panic() outside tests, go vet clean, and every config.Config field is read somewhere. However, cross-referencing exported identifiers against production call sites revealed that the v0.5 "Aggregate" cold-start subsystem (daemon/bootstrap*, dhtindex crawler/PPMI, swarmsearch endorsements, companion B-tree) is a largely unwired work-in-progress: all three bootstrap channels (A: anchors, B: BEP-51 crawl, C: endorsement gossip) plus the HTTPS fallback are inert in production builds, and the placeholder admission policy actually admits any unknown pubkey (score 0.5 >= 0.3 threshold) — the opposite of its documented "default-deny". Eight findings are marked as genuine defects (unfinished/broken), plus several documented-deferral notes that are not defects.

findings.title: Bootstrap admission gate is a placeholder that admits ANY unknown pubkey (inverts its documented default-deny)
findings.detail: daemon.Bootstrap.bloomPolicy is self-described as a placeholder: 'Today we don't yet know the candidate's hits... this check is a placeholder... the conservative default is false'. The finished version was meant to check that >=2 of the candidate's hits appear in the known-good Bloom filter OR >=1 overlaps an anchor's index (requires fetching the candidate's companion torrent pre-admission). The actual code never reads the Bloom filter contents — it only nil-checks it, then returns tracker.Threshold(cand, 0.3). reputation.Tracker.Score returns defaultUnknownScore = 0.5 for unknown pubkeys, so Threshold(unknown, 0.3) is TRUE. Default config always sets BloomPath and ReputationPath, so bloom and tracker are both non-nil in production — meaning every crawled/sync-observed publisher pubkey is admitted into the Layer-D Lookup set (up to MaxTrackedPublishers=100) with zero vetting. Same bug in countStrongEndorsers: unknown endorsers pass the '>= 0.5' reputation bar (0.5 >= 0.5), so 3 freshly-generated Sybil pubkeys clear EndorsementThreshold for free. Bonus staleness: the comment says 'tests set it to true via the test-only BloomOverride helper' — no identifier named BloomOverride exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.evidence: /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/daemon/bootstrap.go:445-458 (bloomPolicy), 463-484 (countStrongEndorsers), 443-444 (nonexistent BloomOverride reference); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/reputation/reputation.go:75 (defaultUnknownScore = 0.5), 224-232 (Score returns it for unknown), 313-318 (Threshold); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/engine/engine.go:887-903 (bloom+tracker always loaded when paths set); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/config/config.go:242-244 (Default() sets both paths)

findings.title: Dead scaffolding: Bootstrap.candidateQueue and type candidate never used — the documented admission rate-limit queue was never built
findings.detail: staticcheck U1000 flags both. The doc comment on type candidate says 'We queue them rather than admit immediately so admission stays rate-limited per the MaxTrackedPublishers cap' — but nothing ever appends to or drains candidateQueue. Actual behavior: admit() admits immediately, and when the cap is full it logs a Warn and returns false; the refused candidate is never queued for later admission (it lingers only in the observed/endorsements maps hoping for a future endorsement). The finished version was meant to queue over-cap candidates and admit them as slots free up.
findings.evidence: /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/daemon/bootstrap.go:92 (candidateQueue []candidate, unused), 100-108 (type candidate + queueing doc), 401-432 (admit: direct admission, cap refusal drops); staticcheck: 'internal/daemon/bootstrap.go:92:2: field candidateQueue is unused (U1000)' and 'bootstrap.go:104:6: type candidate is unused (U1000)'

findings.title: HTTPS last-ditch bootstrap channel fully implemented but never invoked; runAnchorLoop waits forever on a signal only tests can send
findings.detail: bootstrap_https.go implements the SPEC §3.5 fallback: fetch anchor pubkeys from a project HTTPS endpoint when channels A/B/C all come up empty. FallbackToHTTPS has zero production callers (only tests), DefaultBootstrapURL is declared as "" and never read anywhere, and there is no 'channels returned nothing' detection in the daemon. The daemon's channel-A driver runAnchorLoop blocks on the anchorsAdded channel that only FallbackToHTTPS signals — so in every production build it parks forever after the initial (empty-anchor, hence skipped) run. The finished version: daemon detects an empty admitted set after a timeout, calls FallbackToHTTPS(DefaultBootstrapURL) with the production client, which wakes runAnchorLoop to re-fetch.
findings.evidence: /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/daemon/bootstrap_https.go:68 (var DefaultBootstrapURL = "", never read), 149 (FallbackToHTTPS — no non-test callers per grep of cmd/ and internal/), 1-12 (file header describing intended trigger); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/daemon/bootstrap.go:226-238 (runAnchorLoop select on anchorsAdded); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/daemon/daemon.go:209-219 (daemon starts the loop, nothing triggers the fallback)

findings.title: No production path to configure bootstrap anchors: DefaultAnchorPubkeys empty and the promised CLI flag/config field does not exist
findings.detail: DefaultAnchorPubkeys is an empty list whose comment says it 'MUST be populated with real operator keys before a production release' and that 'operators can inject their own via BootstrapOptions.AnchorHexes or a CLI flag'. But daemon.New unconditionally uses DefaultBootstrapOptions() — there is no CLI flag, no config.Config field, and no daemon.Options field that reaches BootstrapOptions.AnchorHexes (grep of cmd/ and internal/config finds no anchor-related knob; the only hit is the status display). Combined with the unwired HTTPS fallback, channel A (anchor PPMI fetch) is a guaranteed no-op in every current deployment. The finished version: a --anchor flag or config entry feeding AnchorHexes, plus a populated default list at release.

findings.title: Channel B (BEP-51 crawler) has primitives but no production driver: CrawlOnce has zero non-test callers
findings.detail: dhtindex implements the full per-tick crawler (CrawlOnce: sample_infohashes query -> metainfo fetch -> snet.pubkey extraction -> PublisherSink) and the low-level SampleInfohashes primitive, and crawler.go explicitly says 'A production crawler layers on top: a worker pool that picks targets, respects per-node Interval hints, expands to Nodes... That logic lives outside this package' — but that worker pool does not exist anywhere. The only production caller of any crawler code is the `swartznet crawl-probe` diagnostic subcommand, which is explicitly 'pure ops tooling' calling SampleInfohashes once. So the daemon never crawls; the only channel-B-shaped input is sync-record ingestion via swarmsearch's PublisherObserver. The finished version: a daemon background worker feeding Bootstrap.CandidateFromCrawl continuously.

findings.title: Channel C endorsement gossip is receive-only: no SwartzNet node ever sends the Endorsed field
findings.detail: The PeerAnnounce wire message carries an Endorsed list ('SPEC §3.3 channel-C gossip primitive... pubkeys the sender vouches for') and the receive path routes entries into Bootstrap.IngestEndorsement. But the only production sender — OnRemoteHandshake's announce in protocol.go — populates only Version, Services, and Pubkey; nothing in the repo ever sets pa.Endorsed. Between current SwartzNet nodes, channel C can never fire; IngestEndorsement is reachable only from hypothetical third-party implementations. The finished version: nodes gossip endorsements for publishers they trust (e.g. admitted publishers with good reputation) in their outgoing announces, capped at MaxEndorsedPerAnnounce.

findings.title: PPMI publish side unwired: PutPPMI never called and Lookup.SetPPMIGetter never called in production, so channel A has nothing to fetch even with anchors
findings.detail: Bootstrap channel A admits an anchor only after successfully fetching its PPMI via PPMIGetter.GetPPMI (bootstrap.go RunAnchors). But no code in the repo ever publishes a PPMI: AnacrolixPutter.PutPPMI has zero non-test callers, the PPMIPutter interface is referenced only in tests, EstimatePPMISize is dead, and there is no CLI subcommand or daemon worker that puts a PPMI. Likewise Lookup.SetPPMIGetter (which enables the PPMI-aware query path in Layer-D lookup) is never invoked outside tests. So even if anchors were configured, their PPMIs could only exist if published by an external tool that does not exist in this repo. The finished version: the publisher/daemon periodically PutPPMIs its own index digest, and engine wiring attaches the PPMIGetter to the Lookup.

findings.title: Aggregate B-tree companion format: offline-CLI-only, engine integration explicitly pending; PoW machinery dormant with mining off by default
findings.detail: The signed-record + hashcash-PoW B-tree index format (build_btree.go, read_btree.go, pow.go, btree.go) is complete with builder, reader, and PoW mining/verification, but the running daemon neither produces nor consumes it: companion.Publisher still builds the older gzipped-JSON CompanionIndex via BuildFromIndex. The only producers/consumers are the offline `swartznet aggregate build|inspect|find` CLI commands, and cmd_aggregate_build.go admits the gap: 'Pair it with a separate "push to DHT" step once the engine integration lands'. Additionally, the CLI's --pow-bits flag defaults to 0 (no mining) even though its own help text says '20 = production default', and the exported constant MinPoWBitsDefault (=20) has zero callers — so every index built with defaults ships with MinPoWBits=0 in the trailer, which read_btree.go treats as 'PoW check disabled'. The anti-spam PoW feature is therefore never enforced anywhere today.

Production callers should pass MinPoWBitsDefault explicitly; we don't'); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/companion/publisher.go:306 (daemon publisher still uses BuildFromIndex/JSON format); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/companion/read_btree.go:160-162 (enforcement gated on trailer MinPoWBits > 0)

findings.title: sn_search scope is validated but never applied as a filter; DefaultScope constant is dead code
findings.detail: The query handler rejects scope letters the responder's capabilities don't cover (unsupportedScopeReason), but the actual search — searcher.SearchLocal(q.Q, limit) — takes no scope parameter and always searches the full index, returning name/file/content hits regardless of what the initiator requested (e.g. scope "n" still returns content matches). swarmsearch.DefaultScope ("nfc") is referenced only by the QueryRequest doc comment ('Empty means DefaultScope') and never by code. The BEP draft (docs/06) permits reject-or-downgrade for unsupported letters and doesn't strictly forbid extra hit types, so this is spec-tolerated, but scope narrowing for bandwidth savings is unimplemented and the DefaultScope contract is aspirational. Not marked as a defect since behavior stays within the spec's MAY language.
findings.evidence: /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/swarmsearch/handler.go:699-702 (scope used only for reject gate), 717 (SearchLocal has no scope arg); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/swarmsearch/wire.go:32 (DefaultScope, zero code references); /home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/swarmsearch/query.go:19-21 ('Empty means DefaultScope' contract); docs/06 lines ~194-204 (scope semantics, downgrade-vs-reject MAY)

findings.title: Documented v1 deferrals and stale reservations (not defects): peer-book demotion, DHT shard/rotation fields, ErrPublisherClosed, httpapi.New
findings.detail: Several 'reserved' items are deliberate, documented scope cuts rather than broken code: (1) PeerBook.Failures is incremented by RecordFailure on query timeouts but never used — automatic tried->new demotion is 'reserved for v1.1'; failure counts accumulate with no consumer. (2) dhtindex KeywordValue.More / SaltForShard (multi-shard spill) and NextPubKey (key rotation) ship on the wire but are never set or followed — explicitly documented as v1 format reservations to avoid a future format bump. (3) dhtindex.ErrPublisherClosed says 'Currently unused; reserved for the engine wiring in M4d's second half' — M4d's engine wiring has long since shipped and the sentinel is still unused, so the reservation comment is stale dead code. (4) httpapi.New (server.go:230) is a legacy constructor with no production callers; the daemon uses NewWithOptions. All are cleanup candidates, none change behavior.

findings.detail: No TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK markers exist in production code; panic() appears only in test files; go vet is clean. findings.title: Surface 2: HTTP API routes (internal/httpapi, default localhost:7654)
findings.detail: All routes registered in Server.Start (/home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/httpapi/server.go:307-346). Global middleware: 1 MiB request-body cap (bodylimit.go maxRequestBody=1<<20) then CSRF/DNS-rebinding guard on state-mutating methods (csrf.go: Origin/Referer host and Host header must be loopback, fails closed); server timeouts ReadHeader 2s / Read 5s / Write 30s / Idle 60s; warns loudly if bound non-loopback (API is unauthenticated). Routes: POST /search — body {q (required, <=1024 bytes), limit (default 50, cap 500), swarm bool, dht bool, swarm_timeout_ms (default 2000, cap 30000), dht_timeout_ms (default 5000, cap 30000), signed_by hex64, highlight bool} -> {local:{total,hits:[{doc_type,infohash,name,size_bytes,file_index,file_path,mime,extractor,score,signed_by,fragments}]}, swarm?:{asked,responded,rejected,hits[{infohash,name,size,seeders,score,sources}],error?}, dht?:{indexers_asked,indexers_responded,hits[{infohash,name,seeders,size,files,sources}],error?}}. GET /healthz -> {ok,version}. GET /status -> {local:{indexed,doc_count}, swarm:{known_peers,capable_peers}, publisher:{pubkey?,total_keywords,total_hits,keywords[{keyword,hits_count,last_published,publish_count,last_error}]}, dht?:{good_nodes,nodes}, bloom?:{bit_size,hash_functions,population_bits,estimated_items}, reputation?:{known_indexers,top_indexers[<=10]{pubkey,score,hits_returned,hits_confirmed,hits_flagged}}}. POST /confirm {infohash hex40} -> {ok,infohash} (503 if no bloom). POST /flag {infohash} -> {ok,infohash,indexers_flagged} (demotes only source-attributed indexers; fails closed to 0). POST /torrent {uri magnet} -> {ok,infohash}. GET /capabilities -> {share_local 0-2, file_hits 0-1, content_hits 0-1, publisher 0-1}; POST /capabilities same body, values clamped, echoes result. GET /torrents -> {torrents:[TorrentSnapshot{infohash,name,size,bytes_completed,bytes_missing,progress,files,active_peers,half_open_peers,pending_peers,total_peers,seeders,paused,status,indexing,indexed_files?,index_extracted?,queued,download_rate,upload_rate,signed_by?,trusted_publisher?}]}. POST /torrents/{infohash}/pause | /resume, DELETE /torrents/{infohash} -> {ok,infohash,action} (infohash must be 40 hex). POST /torrents/{infohash}/indexing {enabled bool} -> {ok,infohash,enabled}. GET /torrents/{infohash}/files -> {infohash,files:[{index,path,display_path,length,bytes_completed,progress,priority}]}. POST /torrents/{infohash}/files/{index}/priority {priority: none|normal|high} -> {ok,infohash,index,priority}. GET /aggregate -> {ppmi_enabled,known_indexers,indexers[{pk,label?}],record_source_kind?,record_cache_size?,record_cache_max?,services (hex ServiceBits),bootstrap?{anchors,admitted,pending}}. GET /companion -> {publisher:{last_refresh,last_infohash,last_error?,published_count,pubkey_hex?},subscriber:[{pubkey_hex,label?,last_sync_at?,last_error?,torrents_imported,content_imported,generated_at?,pointer_infohash?}]}; POST /companion/refresh -> {ok} (429 when throttled); POST /companion/follow {pubkey hex64,label?} -> {ok}; POST /companion/unfollow {pubkey} -> {ok}. GET /index/stats -> {dir_bytes,doc_count,torrent_count,content_count,corpus_text_bytes,inflation_ratio}. GET /config/rate-limit -> {upload_bps,download_bps}; POST same body (0 = unlimited), echoes. GET /config/queue -> {max_active_downloads}; POST same, echoes. Web UI: GET /{$} serves embedded index.html, GET /static/ serves app.js/style.css; six browser tabs (Search, Add, Downloads, Status, Companion, Settings). Unconfigured collaborators return 503 'not configured'.

findings.title: Surface 4: Config fields, defaults, and override paths (internal/config)
findings.detail: Config struct (/home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/config/config.go). Share root: $XDG_DATA_HOME/swartznet, else ~/.local/share/swartznet, else ./swartznet-state. Fields with Default() values and overrides: DataDir = <root>/data (flags: add/gui --data-dir; GUI Settings tab persists to config.json); ListenPort = 42069 (flags: add/gui --port; 0 = OS-assigned; range-validated 0-65535); ListenHost = '' (no flag/env; testlab-only); Seed = true (no flag); NoUpload = false (flag: add --leech-only); DisableDHT = false (flag: add/gui --no-dht); DisableDHTPublish = false (flag: add/gui --no-dht-publish); NoIndex = false (flag: add --no-index; passed via daemon.Options, cascades to disable Bleve and Layer-D publisher); DHTBootstrapAddrs = nil (flag: add --dht-bootstrap, repeatable); DisableIPv6 = false (no flag; testlab-only); DHTInsecure = false (flag: add --dht-insecure, double-gated by SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 at CLI and SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 in Validate); Regtest = false (flag: add --regtest, same double gate); HTTPUserAgent = '' (no flag); IndexDir = <root>/index (flags: add/gui/search --index-dir; GUI Settings persists); IdentityPath = <root>/identity.key (no add flag; create --identity, aggregate build --key); PublisherManifest = <root>/publisher.json (no flag); ReputationPath = <root>/reputation.json (no flag); SeedListPath = <root>/seeds.json (no flag; missing file OK); BloomPath = <root>/known-good.bloom (no flag); MinIndexerScore = 0 (no flag); CompanionDir = <root>/companion (no flag; empty disables companion publisher); CompanionFollowFile = <root>/companion-follows.json (no flag); TrustPath = <root>/trust.json (no flag on add; trust subcommand --file). Env: XDG_DATA_HOME relocates the whole root; SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 lets Validate accept Regtest/DHTInsecure outside test binaries; SWARTZNET_LOG sets log level (in cmd layer, not config). Not in Config but user-facing: API address is daemon.Options.APIAddr set by --api-addr (default localhost:7654, '' disables). GUI-persisted overrides file: DefaultUserConfigPath() = <root>/config.json holding only {data_dir, index_dir} (LoadUserOverrides/SaveUserOverrides; missing file OK, malformed JSON is an error); precedence in swartznet-gui is Default() < config.json < CLI flags. Validate() creates DataDir (0755) and IndexDir's parent, and fails closed on Regtest/DHTInsecure without the env opt-in.

findings.title: Surface 5: Files read/written on disk (paths, formats, modes)
findings.detail: All under the share root (default ~/.local/share/swartznet, honours XDG_DATA_HOME): identity.key — raw 64-byte ed25519 private key, created on first run, mode 0600 enforced (loader rejects any other mode; parent dir created 0700) (/home/kartofel/Claude/swartznet/internal/identity/identity.go). publisher.json — dhtindex per-keyword publish manifest, JSON, written 0600 via .tmp+rename (internal/dhtindex/manifest.go). reputation.json — per-pubkey reputation tracker, JSON, 0600 tmp+rename (internal/reputation/reputation.go). seeds.json — read-only curated indexer seed list {version:1,seeds:[{pubkey,label}]}; missing file is not an error. known-good.bloom — binary Bloom filter, 0600 tmp+rename (internal/reputation/bloom.go). trust.json — publisher trust list JSON, 0600 tmp+rename (internal/trust/trust.go). companion-follows.json — JSON array [{pubkey,label}], 0600 tmp+rename (internal/daemon/adapters.go:238-241). companion/ — companion publisher artifacts: swartznet-content-index-v1.json.gz (or swartznet-content-index-<pubkey-prefix>-v1.json.gz for the generic multi-publisher name) = gzipped JSON index snapshot, plus companion.torrent = wrapping metainfo, 0600 tmp+rename (internal/companion/types.go:16,34; torrent.go:58-118). config.json — GUI-persisted {data_dir,index_dir}, pretty JSON, 0644 tmp+rename (internal/config/config.go:414-438). data/ (DataDir) — downloaded torrent content; session.json = open-torrents manifest (version 1, paused/indexing/queue state), 0644 tmp+rename, rewritten on every add/remove/pause/resume/set-indexing; torrents/<infohash>.torrent = per-torrent metainfo copies for session restore (0644 tmp+rename) (internal/engine/session.go:96-97,205-227); .torrent.db / .torrent.bolt.db = anacrolix piece-completion databases created implicitly in DataDir. index/ (IndexDir) — Bleve full-text index directory (index_meta.json, store/), schema v3. Command outputs: swartznet create writes the -o .torrent 0644 tmp+rename (internal/engine/create.go:184-185); aggregate build writes the --out signed B-tree payload and reads --in JSONL (or stdin); aggregate inspect/find read the given index file; add reads .torrent files given as argument; gui --torrent reads .torrent files. GUI additionally persists window geometry via Fyne preferences under app id net.swartznet.gui (Fyne's own config dir, e.g. ~/.config/fyne/net.swartznet.gui/preferences.json). Logs go to stderr only; no log files are written.

findings.title: Mismatch: three environment variables are undocumented, and --regtest/--dht-insecure require two differently-named env gates simultaneously
findings.detail: SWARTZNET_LOG (log level for both binaries), SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 (CLI gate for add --regtest/--dht-insecure), and SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 (config.Validate gate for the same knobs) appear in no README, docs/, or CHANGELOG text. Worse, the two safety gates are inconsistent: cmd_add.go refuses --regtest/--dht-insecure unless SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1, but engine.New -> cfg.Validate (config.go dangerousFlagsRejected) then independently refuses the same flags unless SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 (outside test binaries). An operator following the CLI's own error message ('set SWARTZNET_UNSAFE=1 to enable') will then hit a second, differently-worded failure demanding SWARTZNET_ALLOW_REGTEST=1 — two env vars for one gate, neither documented anywhere.

broken_verified.issue: dht-smoke code contradicts its own docs on stress-phase exit status: doc says 'does not fail the exit status unless ALL puts fail', but run() swallows runStress's all-failed error with log.Warn and returns nil, so the process prints PASS/exit 0 even when every stress put failed
broken_verified.evidence: cmd/dht-smoke/main.go:172-178 (error logged, nil returned) vs main.go:22-25 and runStress return at main.go:300-302
broken_verified.note: runStress's only non-nil return is the all-puts-failed error (cmd/dht-smoke/main.go:300-302), but run() swallows it with log.Warn and unconditionally returns nil (main.go:172-179), so main prints PASS/exit 0 even when every stress put fails — directly contradicting the doc at main.go:22-25 and the inline comment at main.go:176-177 that both say the exit status should fail when ALL puts fail.

broken_verified.issue: dht-smoke bootstrap wait loop degenerates to a busy-ish spin if bootstrapCtx expires before the deadline: the select's <-bootstrapCtx.Done() case returns immediately every iteration (both timers are 30s so the window is small, but the two timing mechanisms are redundant/uncoordinated)
broken_verified.note: At cmd/dht-smoke/main.go:72-92 the two 30s timers are uncoordinated: srv.Bootstrap() (line 74) blocks unbounded by bootstrapCtx (anacrolix/dht v2.23.0 Bootstrap uses context.Background and waits for traversal stall), so the line-78 deadline always outlives bootstrapCtx by the Bootstrap duration; in that window the empty `case <-bootstrapCtx.Done():` (line 89) fires instantly each iteration without breaking or sleeping, degenerating the wait loop into a busy spin of Stats()+log calls — the claim is correct and, if anything, understates the spin window.

broken_verified.issue: Status tab comment claims a disabled-DHT daemon renders '-' in the DHT Routing card, but refresh() always formats the (0,0) values with %d — after the first 4s tick the card shows '0'/'0', not '-'. Only the pre-first-refresh placeholder is '-'.
broken_verified.note: The comments at internal/gui/status.go:97-99 ("a daemon with DHT disabled sees '-' here") and status.go:242-244 ("which the label formatter renders as '-'") contradict the code: refresh() unconditionally does st.dhtLabels[0/1].SetText(fmt.Sprintf("%d", ...)) at status.go:335-336, so the (0,0) returned by a disabled-DHT engine (locked by internal/engine/dht_routing_table_size_test.go) renders as "0"/"0"; the only "-" is the pre-refresh placeholder from makeLabelGroup (status.go:374), which is overwritten immediately since refresh() runs at startup (status.go:183) before the 4s ticker. No formatter maps 0 to "-", so the comments are wrong (a doc/comment contradiction, not a crash-level bug).

broken_verified.issue: Search empty-state after zero-hit searches shows the original generic hint instead of a per-query 'no results for <q>' message; the code comment explicitly documents this as a punt ('we stuck with container.NewStack so we can't replace children').
